item.title: Default featured images for InfoItems from a capture of their source, delivered to the WP Information (design)
item.body:
## Summary

Generate a **default featured image for an InfoItem from its source**, and deliver it as the featured image of the matching **WP Information** record. This builds on the viewport-capture pipeline (#380), but needs its own design: the image has to suit a featured-image slot, sources come in different kinds, and the image must reach the WordPress media library.

Origin: CannObserv/cli#92 (2020, "Create a default featured image from the specified source URL"). It was recast for the Archiver cohort on 2026-10-20 and is closed and redirected here. It will likely touch **Replicator**, **cannobserv** and the **broker**.

## The existing screenshot pipeline (2026-10-20)

| Piece | Where | State |
|---|---|---|
| Contracts: `content.capture` command (`url`, `viewport`, `full_page`, `wait`), `CaptureStoredEvent`, `CaptureFailedEvent` | cannobserv#571 (co-core v0.37.1) | **Landed** |
| Stream and ACLs: `content.capture`, group `replicator.capture` | broker#114 | **Landed**. Go-live check open: broker#116 |
| Renderer: consume the command, render headless, store, publish the fact | replicator#138 (shares runtime with replicator#63) | Open |
| Policy, issuance, consumption, display on InfoItem detail | #380 | Open |

Captures are **temporary until persisted** (cannobserv `docs/change_bus/capture.md` (b)). Keeping one means issuing `content.persist` before `blob_expires_at`.

## What a featured image adds beyond #380

1. **Profile.** A featured image is a fixed-aspect, above-the-fold crop, e.g. 1200×630 for social cards and the theme's thumbnail sizes *(sizes to confirm with the theme)*. A full-page archival screenshot is something else. Does this need a second capture profile on the same command, or a derived crop of #380's capture?
2. **Source kinds.**
   - an HTML page: a viewport capture;
   - a **PDF**: render the first page, which Chromium can't do from a URL the way it renders HTML, so it needs a PDF rasterizer in Replicator *(unverified)*;
   - a **video**: the platform thumbnail (see #410);
   - an **image**: the image itself, resized.

   Which kinds are in the first slice?
3. **Trigger.** At registration (`co-archive register`, cli#277), on demand ("Use as featured image"), or refreshed on change? The featured image is probably set once and kept, unlike archival captures.
4. **Delivery to WordPress.** This is the hardest part. Archiver doesn't write WordPress. A featured image is a WP **media attachment** set as the post's `_thumbnail_id`. On co/v1 this is served for `information` and the other thumbnail-supporting types (CannObserv/cannabis.observer-wordpress#1092). Options:
   - **(a)** the CLI fetches the persisted image and uploads it. The cli's media service, and upstream `co_core_sync.services.media`, expose only `read` today, so this needs an upload facade upstream.
   - **(b)** the WP plugin pulls from Archiver.
   - **(c)** the site renders the Archiver-hosted image without a media attachment.

   Any option depends on the **WP Information ↔ InfoItem link**, which is open on cli#201 and cli#277.
5. **Precedence.** Today the CLI copies an organization's image onto new Information *Sets*, Event Types and Roles, and an Event Type's image onto new Events. Information *records* get no image at all. Does a generated image replace the inherited logo where there is one, or only fill in where there's none? Clearing an image has no write path yet (cannobserv#574).

## Downstream once designed

- Possibly a cannobserv issue: a capture-profile field, and/or a media upload facade.
- Replicator issues: a crop or profile mode, and a PDF first-page renderer.
- A broker issue only if a new stream is needed.
- The Archiver policy, issuance and dashboard work here.
- The WP plugin or theme work for option (b) or (c).
- On the CLI side, a request flag on `co-archive register`.

item.title: Tailscale 1.104.2 for TS-2026-013 (eMudhra intermediates)
item.body:
**Tailscale security bulletin [TS-2026-013](https://tailscale.com/security-bulletins/#ts-2026-013)** (published 2026-10-21; tracked on CannObserv/provisioner#77). The private keys for eight eMudhra TLS intermediates leaked. Tailscale's client trusts the OS root store, so anyone holding one of those keys could pass as a TLS site "with no warning". **The fix is Tailscale v1.104.2 or later.** It's built with Go 1.27.3, which distrusts those intermediates even when they're still in the system store. No workaround is given. Mesh traffic (WireGuard, node keys) isn't affected.

**The same compromise, beyond Tailscale:** exe.dev's advisory (https://exe.dev/security/emudhra-compromise, 2026-10-20) comes with a remediation command, `ssh exe.dev remediate-emudhra-compromise`, run from the Mac. It fixes the system store and the tools that bundle their own roots (uv, claude, opencode, headless-shell). It doesn't reach a Python venv's **certifi**, which httpx and requests use instead of the system store. On `co-provisioner` that certifi still trusted the emSign chain afterwards (CannObserv/provisioner#79; fix at certifi ≥ 2026.10.19, per CannObserv/address-validator#343). A process started before the fix keeps the old trust until it restarts. This upgrade restarts `tailscaled`.

## For this host

- **co-registrar**, a bus participant: after co-processor, and check the consumer reconnected afterwards, with broker's bus-health probe.
- **No `.skills/patching-hosts` knob** in this repo (read 2026-10-22), so this is a hand run of `tailscale` alone, provisioner#60's shape:
  ```bash
  tailscale version --daemon                       # before
  sudo apt-get update
  apt-get install -s --only-upgrade tailscale=1.104.2   # expect: tailscale alone
  sudo NEEDRESTART_MODE=l apt-get install --only-upgrade tailscale=1.104.2 </dev/null
  tailscale version --daemon; systemctl show tailscaled -p MainPID,ActiveEnterTimestamp
  ```
  The version is pinned and `-y` is left out, so apt aborts rather than doing more than the simulation showed.

## What to expect (measured on `co-provisioner`, provisioner#60 and #77)

- The package's postinst restarts `tailscaled`. The tailnet was down for about 2 s: 2.0 s for 1.102.4 → 1.104.1, and 2.2 s for 1.104.1 → 1.104.2.
- Listeners bound to the tailnet address stayed bound. An established tailnet TCP socket survived once (#60) and timed out once (#77). In the timeout case, the client reconnected after one backoff. Expect either outcome.
- `NEEDRESTART_MODE=l` keeps needrestart from restarting anything else. PID1's own lines may be missing from the journal (provisioner#62), so prove the restart from `systemctl show tailscaled -p MainPID,ActiveEnterTimestamp`.

## Done when

- [ ] `tailscale version --daemon` reports 1.104.2 or later for client and daemon, and Go 1.27.3 or later.
- [ ] The host's health checks pass afterwards.
- [ ] A comment on CannObserv/provisioner#77 gives the version before and after and the UTC time. That issue's closing table is built from them.

The order across the cohort is in provisioner#77: co-processor first, as the canary; then each service node, each checked with the broker's bus-health probe; co-broker last.

slot.instructions: `epic` is a GitHub issue that tracks a body of work through a checklist of child issues: `epic.goal` says what it covers, `epic.scope` holds its boundary decisions and rules, `epic.children` its checklist lines (done: ticked), and `epic.parked` what waits on a trigger. `item` is an issue filed since the coordinator last looked, with its state now. Which slot does the coordinator give `item` in this epic?

criteria.child: Work this epic covers and that should be done now or in order: it gets its own checklist line, slotted by dependency. A follow-up to a child, a bug in what a child shipped, or a piece split off a child is a child.
criteria.closed-in-fact: Work this epic covers that is already delivered: the item is closed, or a child's merged change already did it, so it is verified, linked and closed with evidence instead of slotted.
criteria.split: The item mixes work this epic covers with work it doesn't, so the epic's part is filed as its own issue and the rest is left out.
criteria.out of epic: Not this epic's work: another skill, service, area or epic, a record or notice with no action, or tooling around the epic rather than its work. It is said so plainly and cross-linked only where it changes a remaining step.
criteria.duplicate: The same work as an existing child or another open issue, so it is closed in favour of that one.
criteria.park: This epic's concern, but not to be done yet: it waits on a trigger (another repo, a decision, a date, an event) and goes in the parked table with that trigger.

item.title: certifi trusts the compromised eMudhra chain: the live venv accepts emSign G3 (floor certifi>=2026.10.19)
item.body:
**Filed by the epic #357 coordinator (2026-10-23).** It's the Python half of the eMudhra intermediate compromise. #416 covers Tailscale, and this issue covers what #416 doesn't reach. Labels: `[measured]` run today on this host; `[traced]` read in code on `origin/main` `4cfe98a`; `[stated]` a sibling's measurement.

## The exposure `[measured, 2026-10-23T00:4xZ]`
- **The live release's venv (`/srv/archiver/live`, build `5252b265d098`) has certifi `2026.4.22`.** Its bundle carries all four emSign roots, including **emSign ECC Root CA - G3**.
- **It trusts the compromised chain.** With the live venv's own httpx:
  - `httpx.get('https://dv-g3b-noct-emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com/')` returns **HTTP 200**: the impersonation test host, chaining to emSign G3.
  - The Comodo AAA test host (`dv-g3b-aaa-noct-…`) is rejected with `CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED`.
- **The OS store is already fixed:** system `curl` rejects the G3 host (exit 60). The gap is certifi, which httpx and requests use **instead of** the system store.
- **The deploy checkout's `.venv`** (the 8001 dev server) also has certifi `2026.4.22`.

## Why archiver is exposed `[traced]`
- **certifi is transitive.** `uv.lock` lists it under `httpcore`, `httpx` and `requests`. `pyproject.toml` doesn't name it.
- **Nothing in `src/`, `scripts/` or `deploy/` overrides trust:** no `verify=`, no `truststore`, no `SSL_CERT_FILE`, no `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE`. So every outbound TLS call trusts certifi's bundle:
  - **the preview's fetch of arbitrary operator-supplied URLs** (`AsyncFetchDriver`, co-core);
  - **Power Map** (`src/core/power_map/client.py`, `power-map-client`);
  - **the nightly backup's GCS upload** (`google-cloud-storage` → `requests`);
  - **GitHub, from the drift check.**

  The Status check-ins are plain HTTP inside the tailnet (`http://status:9000`), so certifi plays no part in them.

## The fix, as measured on the cohort `[stated: CannObserv/provisioner#79]`
- **The leaked intermediates chain to emSign ECC Root CA - G3 and to Comodo AAA Services.** certifi **2026.10.19** (PyPI, uploaded 2026-10-20T02:24Z) removes **emSign ECC Root CA - G3**, the only emSign change in that release. I diffed the two bundles today: the removed labels are emSign ECC Root CA - G3, Atos TrustedRoot 2011, SecureSign Root CA12 and ePKI Root Certification Authority `[measured]`. The other three emSign roots (C1, C3, G1) remain.
- **provisioner#79's shape:** `[tool.uv] constraint-dependencies = ["certifi>=2026.10.19"]`, rather than a dependency line, since nothing imports certifi. Add a gate test that checks the *installed* certifi version against the floor (`importlib.metadata.version`), so a re-lock can't slip below it.
- **The alternative, raised there:** `truststore`, which makes httpx use the OS store, the one apt and exe.dev remediate. It removes the lag on future distrusts, but it's a bigger change: every client construction site, plus co-core's fetch driver.

## Scope
1. Add the certifi floor and the gate test; `uv lock`. certifi comes from PyPI, not the wheelhouse, so no co-core step is needed.
2. Deploy. `uv.lock` is a runtime file, so the deploy restarts `archiver.service`, and the backup and drift units run from the new release. A restart alone fixes nothing: the bundle comes from the venv.
3. Then refresh the deploy checkout's venv (`git pull --ff-only && uv sync`), which fixes the 8001 dev server.

## Done when
- **The live venv rejects both `noct` test hosts** (post-deploy, read-only):
  ```bash
  /srv/archiver/live/.venv/bin/python -I -c "import httpx; httpx.get('https://dv-g3b-noct-emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com/', timeout=10)"   # must raise ConnectError
  ```
- The gate test fails on certifi < 2026.10.19.
- The deploy checkout's venv has certifi ≥ 2026.10.19.

Refs: #416 (Tailscale, the same compromise); CannObserv/provisioner#77 and #79; exe.dev's advisory (https://exe.dev/security/emudhra-compromise).

item.title: uv.lock ships 21 runtime advisories, all fixable inside the caps; nothing re-locks or audits it
item.body:
**Filed by the epic #357 coordinator during #192's pre-flight (2026-10-23, `origin/main` = `4129d36` = live `4129d366a75f`).**

## What was measured

`uv audit --frozen --no-dev` (uv 0.13.5, OSV; `--preview-features audit-command`) on `main`'s `uv.lock`, which is the live release's lock: **34 findings in 73 runtime packages, 21 unique advisories across 6 packages** `[measured]`. Every fix is inside today's specifiers:

| Package (locked) | Via | Unique advisories | Highest fix | `uv lock --dry-run --upgrade-package` resolves |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| starlette 1.0.0 | fastapi | 5 (PYSEC-2026-161, -248, -249, -2280, -2281) | 1.3.1 | 1.9.0 |
| pypdf 6.19.0 | co-core[extract] | 8 (GHSA-5hx5…, -9mx8…, -qfv9…, -cgf9…, -6vvc…, -39mj…, -7mh2…, -f54x…) | 6.21.1 | 6.21.2 |
| python-multipart 0.0.29 | direct `<1` | 4 (PYSEC-2026-3036, -3037, -3040, -3041) | 0.0.31 | 0.0.32 |
| anyio 4.13.0 | httpx, starlette | 2 (PYSEC-2026-4024, -4025) | 4.14.2 | 4.14.2 |
| idna 3.13 | httpx | 1 (PYSEC-2026-215) | 3.15 | 3.20 |
| mako 1.3.12 | alembic | 1 (PYSEC-2026-4243) | 1.4.2 | 1.4.3 |

The dry-run changed no specifier; the six upgrades resolve with `fastapi`, `co-core` and the rest unchanged `[measured]`. The dev group adds 18 more findings: virtualenv (16, via pre-commit) and openapi-python-client (2, the SDK generator). They're dev-only, so triage them separately.

`uv audit --frozen` ran in a directory with no `.wheelhouse`. It reads `uv.lock` alone and needs no GCS credential `[measured]`.

## Reachability (first pass, `[traced]`, confirmed so far; look for others)

- **pypdf:** it comes in through co-core's extract path. A PDF fetched from a watched source or a preview URL can trigger the infinite-loop and large-memory advisories. This is the widest exposure: the input comes from outside.
- **starlette PYSEC-2026-249 and python-multipart PYSEC-2026-3036/-3040:** form-parsing DoS. The dashboard's `Form(...)` routes are reachable, behind exe.dev auth.
- **starlette PYSEC-2026-161 and -248 (Host header poisons `request.url.path` / `.hostname`):** `git grep` finds no use of `request.url.path` or `.hostname` in `src/` today. **But #404's option A (a same-origin check) compares against the request's host**, so #404 must land on starlette ≥ 1.3.0.
- **Windows-only, not applicable on this host:** starlette PYSEC-2026-2281 (StaticFiles UNC) and mako PYSEC-2026-4243.
- **anyio PYSEC-2026-4025 (TLSStream IDNA 2003):** not traced. Check whether httpx's outbound TLS reaches it.

## Why nothing caught it

The caps aren't the gap: every fix is in range. Nothing re-locks, and nothing audits. Dependabot's `uv` ecosystem can't run here because co-core resolves only from the private wheelhouse (#192, blocker 2). For the record, this audit also shows **no advisory for certifi**. The #418 exposure would not have been flagged by any Python-dependency alert.

CannObserv/broker#86 solved the same problem with a **report-only** lock audit:
- `.github/workflows/audit.yml`: push, PR, a weekly cron and dispatch. No secret, no OIDC.
- `scripts/audit_lock.sh`: always exits 0. A finding is a `::warning::` plus the job summary, so main doesn't turn red on someone else's disclosure date.
- `tests/deploy/test_lock_audit.py` pins the design.

## Proposed scope

1. **Re-lock the six in-cap** and deploy (runtime paths, so the drift check reports `lag` until deployed).
   - starlette 1.0.0 → 1.9.0 is nine minors. Read its changelog, not only the diff.
   - `[Operator decision: take the latest in-cap versions or only the fix floors — recommend latest in-cap, one reviewed jump rather than a second re-lock later]`
2. **Port broker's report-only audit:** the workflow, the script and the guard test. Follow #192's SHA-pin convention if #192 has landed.
3. **Out of scope:**
   - security floors via `constraint-dependencies` (the certifi precedent): a re-lock is enough unless a transitive could regress;
   - the dev-group findings;
   - the SDK's uncapped `attrs` and `python-dateutil`.

No production write. The deploy is the operator's.

item.title: Drop the brainstorming override: symlink upstream, state archiver's design preferences in AGENTS.md
item.body:
## Why

`skills/brainstorming/` is a full fork of `obra-superpowers/brainstorming`, synced at **v6.4.1** (`5bf4e78`, archiver#243). The vendor submodule now records **v7.0.1** (`2ce8aa1`, "brainstorming retune"), and upstream rewrote the skill: an intent-first opening message, "lay out the approaches" in its own message, design-doc sizing, spikes, a builder-check prompt, a visual companion. `.skills/doctor.sh` reports the drift on every session start. Re-syncing a fork this far behind means reapplying each delta onto upstream's new text by hand (docs/CONVENTIONS.md § Re-syncing a `skills/` override), and it will drift again at the next release.

Take upstream as it ships instead: replace the override with a symlink, like every other vendored skill, and state archiver's preferences once in AGENTS.md, where every skill (and an agent with no skill loaded) reads them.

## Preferences to carry into AGENTS.md

From the override's `override-reason:` and body. Each line is a candidate for a terse `## Design & Planning` section (AGENTS.md is the policy file, so keep it short, with detail in docs/SKILLS.md):

1. **Design docs:** `docs/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md`, committed as `#<n> docs: add design doc for <topic>`.
2. **`writing-plans` is optional**, not a required second gate. When a formal plan *is* wanted, it is written and reviewed before implementation, not alongside it.
3. **Hand-off opens a GH issue** for architectural work: summary, design-doc path, scoped decisions. Report the number.
4. **Worktree for any multi-step implementation**, whatever the path: `using-git-worktrees` (archiver's override: own port, `uv sync`, no venv link). Skip for single-commit or directed fixes.
5. **Scope detection:** no brainstorming for a bug with an agreed cause, a directed task with no design ambiguity ("implement GH #<n>", including a coordinator brief), or continuing an approved design. That exemption covers what was asked: scope creep found inside a directed task is a new request.
6. **Process scales, approval doesn't:** spike (question + probe, a nod), bounded (short in-chat design, explicit yes), architectural (design doc + GH issue approved). Any change to a contract another service depends on (a bus payload, a route, an SDK surface) is architectural. In doubt, take the heavier path; hidden complexity upgrades it mid-task.
7. **API changes** flag breaking vs non-breaking (the CHANGELOG trigger and `schema_version` rules already in AGENTS.md).
8. **Visual companion: operator decision.** The override ships none. v7.0.1 *offers* one (SKILL.md § Visual Companion: a local server serving HTML screens, which the user opts into). Either suppress it in AGENTS.md ("don't offer the visual companion"), or allow it and record that its server takes a free port in 3000-9999, never 8000/8001, reached at `https://co-registrar.exe.xyz:<port>/` through the exe.dev proxy.
9. **Proactive suggestion:** on a feature request with no design context, offer brainstorming; don't force it.

## Work

- [ ] Diff v7.0.1 against each preference: drop any upstream now satisfies by default, and keep only the real deltas. Upstream's description ("You MUST use this before any creative work") conflicts with 5; say so explicitly.
- [ ] `git rm -r skills/brainstorming` → `ln -s ../skills-vendor/obra-superpowers/skills/brainstorming skills/brainstorming` (`.claude/skills/brainstorming` already points at `../../skills/brainstorming`).
- [ ] AGENTS.md: the new section (check the context budget: `curating-context` measure, AGENTS.md is paid on every invocation).
- [ ] docs/SKILLS.md: move `brainstorming` from **Local Overrides** to the symlinked list; update its trigger row. Upstream's triggers differ.
- [ ] docs/CONVENTIONS.md § Re-syncing: "all three overrides" becomes two.
- [ ] `skills/using-git-worktrees/SKILL.md:268` names `brainstorming (Phase 4)` as a caller. Check that upstream v7.0.1 still invokes worktrees, or reword.
- [ ] `.socraticodeignore:3` lists `brainstorming` among first-party skills; update it.
- [ ] `.skills/doctor.sh` is clean afterwards (no override-drift line for `brainstorming`).

## Out of scope

The other two overrides (`shipping-work-python-fastapi`, `using-git-worktrees`) are thin, archiver-specific and synced.

slot.instructions: `epic` is a GitHub issue that tracks a body of work through a checklist of child issues: `epic.goal` says what it covers, `epic.scope` holds its boundary decisions and rules, `epic.children` its checklist lines (done: ticked), and `epic.parked` what waits on a trigger. `item` is an issue filed since the coordinator last looked, with its state now. Which slot does the coordinator give `item` in this epic?

criteria.child: Work this epic covers and that should be done now or in order: it gets its own checklist line, slotted by dependency. A follow-up to a child, a bug in what a child shipped, or a piece split off a child is a child.
criteria.closed-in-fact: Work this epic covers that is already delivered: the item is closed, or a child's merged change already did it, so it is verified, linked and closed with evidence instead of slotted.
criteria.split: The item mixes work this epic covers with work it doesn't, so the epic's part is filed as its own issue and the rest is left out.
criteria.out of epic: Not this epic's work: another skill, service, area or epic, a record or notice with no action, or tooling around the epic rather than its work. It is said so plainly and cross-linked only where it changes a remaining step.
criteria.duplicate: The same work as an existing child or another open issue, so it is closed in favour of that one.
criteria.park: This epic's concern, but not to be done yet: it waits on a trigger (another repo, a decision, a date, an event) and goes in the parked table with that trigger.

item.title: JS tests: htmx settle timer outlives htmx-poll-sync tests, fails ~1 in 20 runs after teardown
item.body:
## What happened

The first `push` run of `ci.yml` on `1cc5924` (run 40004235131, attempt 1) failed in `lint` → `npm test`, and that blocked `scripts/deploy.sh`'s CI gate until the job was re-run (attempt 2 green; #192 deploy comment). Every test passed. Vitest failed the run on an **unhandled error** raised outside any test:

```
Test Files  12 passed (12)
     Tests  124 passed (124)
    Errors  1 error
ReferenceError: Element is not defined
 ❯ Timeout.n [as _onTimeout] tests/js/support/htmx-harness.js:126:18
This error originated in "tests/js/htmx-poll-sync.test.js" test file.
```

`htmx-harness.js:126` is the `(0, eval)` that loads `src/dashboard/static/vendor/htmx.min.js`, so every htmx frame maps to that line. The failing frame is a `setTimeout` callback inside htmx.

## Reproduced locally

On this host (Node 24.20.0, vitest 4.1.6, happy-dom 20.9.0), `npx vitest run` failed **1 in 20** runs with the same error. A later run showed a second variant from the same file and frame:

```
TypeError: Failed to execute 'dispatchEvent' on 'EventTarget': parameter 1 is not of type 'Event'.
 ❯ HTMLDivElement.dispatchEvent node_modules/happy-dom/lib/event/EventTarget.js:93:19
 ❯ Timeout.n [as _onTimeout] tests/js/support/htmx-harness.js:126:18
```

So it isn't CI-specific or Node-version-specific, and no JS changed in `4129d36..1cc5924`.

## Likely cause `[inferred, not yet proven]`

htmx settles a swap on a timer: `defaultSettleDelay:20` in the vendored build (`defaultSwapDelay:0`). The tests call `respond()` and assert synchronously; nothing waits for the settle. The last swap's 20 ms timer can outlive its test and fire after vitest has torn down that file's happy-dom environment. htmx then reaches for `Element` / `Event` constructors that no longer belong to a live window, which gives one of the two errors above. `htmx-settle-alpine.test.js` also calls `respond()` but explicitly awaits the settle, which fits it never being the file blamed.

## Fix options

1. **Drain htmx's timers before each test ends.** In `htmx-poll-sync.test.js`'s `afterEach`, `await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, htmx.config.defaultSettleDelay + 5))`, or put the same drain in a shared harness helper. This is the smallest change, and it keeps htmx's real timing.
2. **`vi.useFakeTimers()` + `vi.runAllTimers()`** in `afterEach`. This is deterministic, but it touches every test's timing, and `htmx-settle-alpine` relies on real settles.
3. **`htmx.config.defaultSettleDelay = 0`** in `installHtmx()`. This still schedules a 0 ms timeout, so it narrows the window without closing it. It's the weakest option.

Prefer 1. Prove it the way this was found: a loop of 100 `npx vitest run` runs with zero unhandled errors (a 1-in-20 rate gives ~99.4% odds of at least one failure in 100 runs).

## Why it matters

The lint job gates `deploy.sh`. A 5% flake on `push` blocks deploys at random until someone re-runs, and a re-run habit hides a real failure the day one arrives.

item.title: CI runs the JS lint/tests on Node 20 (EOL 2026-04-30); move to 24, matching the host, and guard it
item.body:
## What

`ci.yml`'s `lint` job sets up Node with `actions/setup-node@… # v4.4.0` and **`node-version: "20"`**. Node 20 reached end-of-life on **2026-04-30**: no more security releases. The JS lint and test run (ESLint, vitest, happy-dom) has been on an unsupported runtime for six months.

The host's runtime is **Node 24.20.0** (`nodejs 24.20.0-1nodesource1`, apt). That's where `pre-ship.sh` runs `npm test` before every push. So CI and the gate before it run different Node majors, the same split #192 closed for the runner image (`ubuntu-24.04`, guarded by `test_runner_image_matches_the_host`).

## Not Dependabot's to move

Dependabot (#192) bumps `uses:` refs, not `with:` inputs, so the setup-node v4 → v7 PR it opens will leave `node-version: "20"` alone. It also isn't the runner annotation about "Node 20 actions forced onto Node 24": that's the runtime the *action* runs on, which the Dependabot bumps fix. This issue is the runtime the project's *JS* runs on.

## Proposed

- [ ] `node-version: "24"` (Active LTS, the host's major). Engines allow it: vitest 4.1.6 `^20 || ^22 || >=24`, happy-dom 20.9.0 `>=20`.
- [ ] Guard it next to the runner pin in `tests/ci/test_workflow_pins.py`: setup-node's `node-version` is a bare major, and on the deploy host (`/srv/archiver/live` present) it equals `node --version`'s major. When the host moves, CI moves with it, the same pattern as `test_runner_image_matches_the_host`.
- [ ] CI green by job. The lint job's `npm test` is the one this changes.

## Out of scope

- The `"latest"` specifiers in `package.json` and `npm install` (not `npm ci`) in CI. That's the npm decision #192 deferred.
- The flaky htmx settle timer (#427), which reproduces on Node 24 too, so this doesn't fix it.
- No production effect: Node isn't in a release; no deploy.

item.title: Bump SocratiCode 1.14.0 → 1.16.1 (SOCRATICODE_SPEC); safe for the shared store, no re-index
item.body:
`.claude/settings.json:59` pins `SOCRATICODE_SPEC` to `socraticode@1.14.0`. The latest release is **1.16.1** (2026-10-15). broker, observo and processor already build on 1.16.0.

## Safe for the shared store

There's no need to re-index or remove anything on co-index (CannObserv/index#13).

- **The embedding text is unchanged from 1.14.0 to 1.16.1.** In the npm tarballs, `embeddings.js`, `embedding-config.js` and `index-profile.js` are byte-identical, and the `indexer.js` changes don't touch chunking. So vectors from 1.16.1 compare with the rest of the store as before (D7), and co-index's `reembed.py` still models them.
- **Qdrant on co-index is now 1.20.0.** SocratiCode's client is `@qdrant/js-client-rest ~1.18.0` with `checkCompatibility: false`. The calls clients make (taken from co-index's access log), plus create, payload index, upsert, delete and a hybrid query, were all tested against 1.20.0.

## What changes

- **1.15.0:** PHP code-graph fixes, Qdrant errors keep their reason, and SocratiCode now waits for its own collection create before reading it.
- **1.16.0:** an opt-in refresh triggered by Git (`SOCRATICODE_WATCHER=git`).
- **1.16.1:** a `limit` on `codebase_symbol`, `codebase_impact` and `codebase_flow`; the symbol graph retries a Qdrant request once on a closed connection; Kotlin Multiplatform and PHP graph fixes; an opt-in auto-cleanup.
  - **Leave `SOCRATICODE_AUTO_CLEANUP` unset.** It refuses a shared, non-loopback store anyway, so it can't fire against co-index.

Changelog: https://github.com/giancarloerra/socraticode/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md

## Ask

1. Set `SOCRATICODE_SPEC` to `socraticode@1.16.1`. Then grep the repo for any other `socraticode@1.14.0` (docs, health hook) and bump those too.
2. Restart the session, then run `codebase_status`. After the next graph build, co-index's `socraticode_metadata` records `builtByVersion: 1.16.1` for this repo.

item.title: Deploy tests still skip on their own drop-in's absence: finish #79's node-signal sweep
item.body:
Follow-up to #79. Its fix (`5fa2444`) added `on_broker_node()` and `read_installed()` to `tests/deploy/conftest.py` and applied them to `test_needrestart.py` and `test_memory_protection.py`. The other deploy modules still decide "not the node" by the absence of the very file they guard. CI stays green with them as they are: none of these files ship on a GitHub runner. The hazard is on the node. Deleting or never installing one of these files skips its own drift check, and the one host the check is for goes quiet.

## Sites

| Module | Test(s) | Skips when |
|---|---|---|
| `test_bus_health_units.py` | `test_installed_service_matches_repo`, `test_installed_timer_matches_repo` | the installed unit is absent (module-local `_read_if_installed`) |
| `test_bus_health_units.py` | `test_every_variable_the_probe_inherits_is_one_it_reads`, `test_the_shared_env_carries_no_redis_password` | `/etc/broker/.env` is absent, or has no `BROKER_REDIS_URL` |
| `test_backup_units.py` | `test_installed_service_matches_repo`, `test_installed_timer_matches_repo` | the installed unit is absent (a second copy of `_read_if_installed`) |
| `test_installed_redis_config_matches_repo.py` | `_assert_installed_matches` (2 tests), `test_installed_wait_script_is_executable` | the drop-in or the wait script is absent |
| `test_live_acl_matches_tracked_acl.py` | `_sudo_file` | the file is absent behind working `sudo -n`. GitHub runners have passwordless sudo, so this is the one site where "sudo works" says nothing about being on the node |

## Weigh

- Most of these are mechanical: swap in `read_installed`, and delete both `_read_if_installed` copies.
- `_sudo_file` and `live_client` need more thought. On the node, a credential that is present but broken already fails rather than skips (by design, see `live_client`'s comment). But a *missing* credential still skips. Using `on_broker_node()` there would turn that into a failure. Check this against the credential-rotation runbook before changing it.
- `/etc/broker` is itself a `NODE_MARKERS` entry. For the `SHARED_ENV` checks, a missing `.env` on the node is a finding, and a `.env` without `BROKER_REDIS_URL` is a separate one.

## Done when

On the node, no test in `tests/deploy/` skips because a file it checks is absent, and `-rs` still shows only the unassigned-DLQ skips. Each converted site gets a pin like #79's (off the node it skips; on the node with the file absent it fails), and CI stays green.

item.title: Remove the old exe-init backup and staged copies after #71's quiet days (not before 2026-10-09)
item.body:
Follow-up from #71 (closed 2026-10-06). `exe-init` was swapped to `14fd603` and the VM rebooted in-guest at 00:00:16Z. The old binary was kept for rollback, and the staged copies are still on disk. Remove them once the new build has run quietly for a few days.

## What to remove

| Path | What it is | Size |
|---|---|---|
| `/exe.dev/bin/exe-init.bak` | the old build (`version unknown`, sha256 `bd33b80e0454...`, 2026-08-29): the one that started sessions at -1000. Root-owned | 14295200 |
| `/var/tmp/exe-init.14fd603` + `.sha256` | the staged new build, copied out of `/tmp` as #71's step 0 | 14327968 + 83 |
| `/tmp/exe-init.14fd603` + `.sha256` | the original staging from 2026-09-29. It survived the reboot; tmpfiles' age rule may clear it first | 14327968 + 83 |

## When

**Not before 2026-10-09**, and only once all of these still hold:
- `/exe.dev/bin/exe-init --version` reads `14fd603`, and sha256 `6403375d4b2f693e260cd210fee072ea73859a390bbf51ba0d249a27195184bf` matches;
- `cat /proc/self/oom_score_adj` reads 0 in a fresh session, and only `exe-init guestd` and exe.dev's `sshd` sit at -1000;
- `uv run pytest tests/deploy/test_memory_protection.py` is green on the node, `test_live_sessions_are_killed_before_the_bus` included;
- the probe has logged no finding traceable to the node itself, and `systemctl --failed` is empty.

## Steps

```bash
/exe.dev/bin/exe-init --version                       # 14fd603
sha256sum /exe.dev/bin/exe-init                       # 6403375d...84bf
sudo rm -f /exe.dev/bin/exe-init.bak
rm -f /var/tmp/exe-init.14fd603 /var/tmp/exe-init.14fd603.sha256 \
      /tmp/exe-init.14fd603 /tmp/exe-init.14fd603.sha256
ls -la /exe.dev/bin/ /var/tmp/exe-init* /tmp/exe-init* 2>&1   # exe-init only; the rest "No such file"
```

No restart, no service touched.

## What removing it gives up

- **The in-guest rollback.** #71's rollback was `mv exe-init.bak exe-init` and a restart. After this, going back means copying a build from a newly created VM. The old build is the buggy one, so nobody should want it back once this new one has proven out.
- **A local copy of the good build.** Re-installing `14fd603` (say, if a platform update overwrote `/exe.dev/bin`) would then also mean copying from a new VM, as #71 did on 2026-09-29.

Close with the `ls` output and the date.

item.title: Take pytest 9.1.2 when it ships: #73's exclusion of 9.1.0/9.1.1
item.body:
Follow-up to #73 (`5aa791d`). **Waiting on pytest 9.1.2.**

#73's cause was upstream, in pytest-dev/pytest#14635. pytest 9.1.0 and 9.1.1 bind a directory's conftest fixtures to the first `Directory` node collected for it. A command line that interleaves a sibling module builds a second node, and that node matches nothing. The fix (pytest-dev/pytest#14645) is backported to `9.1.x` but not released: on 2026-10-06 PyPI's newest is 9.1.1. So `pyproject.toml` now pins `pytest>=9.0.3,!=9.1.0,!=9.1.1,<10`, and the lock holds 9.0.3.

## When 9.1.2 is on PyPI

```bash
uv lock --upgrade-package pytest   # no pyproject edit: the spec already admits it
uv sync --group dev
uv run pytest tests/deploy/test_pytest_collection.py   # six orders; red means 9.1.2 lacks the fix
uv run pytest
```

`9.1.2.dev28+g45a2a8d0e` (9.1.x's head on 2026-10-06) already passes all six. Once the lock is on 9.1.2, the `!=` exclusions and their comment in `pyproject.toml` can be dropped or kept; either is fine.

## Done when

The lock is on a pytest that carries the fix, `test_pytest_collection.py` is green on it, and CI is green.

item.title: co-status#28: one report per fault from co-broker; send metadata.fault to hear new findings
item.body:
**From co-status ([CannObserv/status#28](https://github.com/CannObserv/status/issues/28)): what the `co-broker` monitor sends is changing.** It's reviewed and goes out in co-status's next deploy. Suggested, not urgent: nothing in `src/broker/bus_health.py` (`post_checkin`) breaks.

**Today**, every `alert` check-in sends its own report. A check-in every 10 minutes while there are findings means 6 reports an hour, and nothing when the findings clear.

**After the deploy**, a run of `alert` check-ins is **one fault**:
- it reports when the fault opens;
- `co-broker` has no `renotify_seconds`, so **it doesn't repeat**;
- the first `ok` sends **"[co-status] co-broker has cleared"**.

A check-in that sends no report still gets a 202 and is recorded, with `dispatches: []`. `src/broker/bus_health.py` (`post_checkin`) reads only the status code.

**What this costs you without a change:** a **new finding** that turns up while a fault is open (another check, another subject) sends nothing until everything clears. co-status keeps `variables` opaque, so it can't tell a new finding from the same one.

**Suggested change:** send a fault key the consumer controls, as `metadata.fault` (any JSON value). An `alert` whose `metadata.fault` differs from the open fault's is a new fault, and reports at once. co-status compares the value and never reads into it. A good key here is the sorted list of `check:subject` from `findings`, leaving out `message`: it carries ages and percentages, which change on every run and would report every tick. For example:

```python
# post_checkin, beside "status"
"metadata": {"fault": sorted(f"{f.check}:{f.subject}" for f in findings)},
```

Optional: setting `renotify_seconds` on the monitor (ask co-status) would add a reminder while a fault lasts, e.g. daily.

Design: [the spec](https://github.com/CannObserv/status/blob/c050407b6cdabfdcb722e930f50ef3a9a190355d/docs/specs/2026-10-09-alert-faults-design.md). item.title: Redis 7.0 is upstream EOL (2024-07-29): decide the broker's next Redis
item.body:
Raised from CannObserv/processor (#43 / #46, 2026-10-10). Processor pins its CI Redis to the broker's version, so the broker's version is what every service tests against.

**The facts:**
- **The broker runs Ubuntu 24.04's apt `redis-server` `5:7.0.15-1ubuntu0.24.04.4`** (`noble-updates/universe`), per `deploy/README.md` and `deploy/redis-acl.conf` ("this broker is 7.0.15").
- **Upstream:** Redis 7.0 reached end of life on 2024-07-29, and 7.0.15 is its last release ([endoflife.date/redis](https://endoflife.date/redis)). Redis 7.2 (still BSD-3) has security support until 2029-12-01. 7.4 and later are RSALv2/SSPL, and 8.x adds AGPLv3 as a choice.
- **Ubuntu is still patching it.** The package changelog shows backports in `noble-security`: CVE-2025-49844 (remote code execution), CVE-2025-32023 (2026-02-12) and CVE-2024-31449 (2026-04-12). So the broker isn't unpatched today. But this is universe, which Canonical maintains on a best-effort basis unless Ubuntu Pro `esm-apps` is enabled, and every fix now depends on someone backporting it to a branch upstream has abandoned.

**Why it's cohort-wide:** every service measures and tests against the broker's exact Redis.
- processor's CI runs `mirror.gcr.io/library/redis:7.0.15` (processor#43). Google's mirror serves only tags it has cached, and an EOL tag can drop out of it (processor#46).
- watcher, replicator and archiver record behaviour "verified on 7.0.15" (OOM, `XAUTOCLAIM`, ACL). archiver's and replicator's `check_redis_floor.sh` enforce `>= 7.0`.

**Known upgrade constraint:** from 7.2, redis-py sends `CLIENT SETINFO`, so `+client|setinfo` becomes a required ACL grant. The grant is rejected on 7.0.15 (`deploy/redis-acl.conf`, `docs/RESTART-WINDOW.md`), so the grant and the upgrade must happen in the same restart window.

**Options (to weigh, not decided):**
1. **Valkey 7.2 from Ubuntu's own archive.** `valkey-server` `7.2.13+dfsg1-0ubuntu0.1` is in `noble-updates/universe`, with `valkey-redis-compat` for the Redis paths and names. It's BSD-licensed, comes from the same apt source and the same security pipeline, and is the smallest jump past 7.0. To check: Valkey's own support window for 7.2, what `INFO server` reports as `redis_version` (the floor checks parse it), and whether the AOF/RDB files load in place.
2. **Redis 7.2 from packages.redis.io:** upstream-supported until 2029 and BSD-licensed, but it adds a third-party apt repository to the broker. To check: whether that repository still publishes 7.2.x for noble.
3. **Redis 8.x from packages.redis.io:** the current line, with the license question above, and the largest behavioural jump.
4. **Stay on Ubuntu's 7.0.15** and rely on Ubuntu's backports (possibly with Pro `esm-apps`). Record the reason, and set a date to revisit.

**Whichever is chosen, the work includes:**
- a restart window (a cohort-wide event);
- the `+client|setinfo` grant in that window;
- a notice to each consumer with the new version to pin. For processor that means `BROKER_REDIS` in `tests/test_ci.py`, the CI service image, and co-processor's scratch `redis-server`.

**Done when:** the option is chosen and recorded with its reason. If it's an upgrade, the window has run and consumers have been told the new version.

Refs CannObserv/processor#43, CannObserv/processor#46.

item.title: RESTART-WINDOW.md: record all five participants' measured reconnects (#67)
item.body:
`docs/RESTART-WINDOW.md`'s table still says *"four since Processor began consuming ... five once Provisioner goes live; Processor's reconnect across a broker restart is untested"*. #67's run (2026-10-13) measured all five, across a Redis restart, a tailscaled restart and a VM reboot:

| | Redis restart 04:17:26Z (down ~0.5 s) | tailscaled restart 04:18:45Z | reboot 04:22:08Z (Redis down ~10.6 s) |
|---|---|---|---|
| archiver | recovered 04:17:32.97Z, 1 cycle | rode through | reconnect ~04:22:20.6Z, 3 cycles |
| watcher | within its 5 s backoff | rode through | ~04:22:23.5Z |
| replicator | recovered 04:17:32.96Z | rode through | recovered 04:22:25.63Z, 3 cycles (bound ~7.5 min, replicator#133) |
| processor | see #67 | rode through | see #67 |
| provisioner (ACL user) | 1 s backoff | rode through | ~04:22:25Z; consumed a post-boot entry |

Sources: each agent's own journald, reported over a Mayfly round and landed on #67; broker's `CLIENT LIST` ages and per-group positions.

To do:
- update the blast-radius row and the *Recovery is bounded* table: replicator's bound and its boot gap (replicator#133), and each consumer's ensure-group-at-boot-from-`$` caveat (all but archiver), which makes the per-group check in step 1d load-bearing;
- note that established connections survive a tailscaled restart (every client's `age=` dated to the earlier Redis restart).

Found by #67.

item.title: CI actions target Node.js 20: bump setup-uv and auth in ci.yml and audit.yml together
item.body:
Every green run on `a6d4470` carries the runner's deprecation annotation [measured: check-run annotations, CI 38417913988 and audit 38417913989, 2026-10-13]:

> Node.js 20 is deprecated. The following actions target Node.js 20 but are being forced to run on Node.js 24: astral-sh/setup-uv@v5, google-github-actions/auth@v2

Pins today:

| Workflow | Action |
|---|---|
| `ci.yml` | `actions/checkout@v5`, `astral-sh/setup-uv@v5`, `google-github-actions/auth@v2` |
| `audit.yml` (#86) | `actions/checkout@v5`, `astral-sh/setup-uv@v5` |
| `context-cadence.yml` | `actions/checkout@v5` (generated by `install-cadence.sh`; re-run it rather than editing) |

Why it matters:
- These are the only annotations on green runs, and they sit where `audit.yml`'s own `uv.lock advisories` warning appears. Noise there hides the one warning #86 relies on.
- The runner also notes that `ubuntu-latest` migrates to Ubuntu 26 from 2026-10-19.

To do:
- Bump `ci.yml` and `audit.yml` together, so the two workflows keep the same pins. `auth@v3` is a WIF step: read its changelog for anything that changes `workload_identity_provider`.
- Optionally add a `github-actions`-only `.github/dependabot.yml`. CannObserv/watcher's is the template: SHA pins with a `# vX.Y.Z` comment, `open-pull-requests-limit: 10`, `commit-message.prefix: chore`, and a test guarding the config. The `uv` ecosystem stays out, for the wheelhouse reason #86 records.

Found by #86's code review (CR 8).

item.title: RESTART-WINDOW.md: replicator's outage bound after CannObserv/replicator#133 deploys
item.body:
#87 (2026-10-13, `b313d57`) wrote replicator's row in `docs/RESTART-WINDOW.md`, *Recovery is bounded*, from CannObserv/replicator#133 while that issue was open:
- "**~11-12 min**, not the 60 min CannObserv/replicator#94 sized": each restart into a broker that is still down exits at its group call;
- "a 2026-09-16 outage would fail replicator's unit today".

#87's close said both lines change when CannObserv/replicator#133 lands. **It closed at 16:02Z the same day** (`e2df4b3..5e77539`). Boot now retries `ensure_group` with the loop's own backoff and ceiling, so a start that boots into a down broker waits instead of exiting. Its close said "Not yet deployed: needs `sudo systemctl restart replicator`".

**Gate:** replicator confirms the deploy. Broker's side [measured 2026-10-13T17:19Z]: all four `user=replicator` connections are aged 1318 s, so they reconnected at 16:57:47Z. That fits a restart for the deploy, but nobody has confirmed it.

To do, once the gate clears:
- Re-derive replicator's bound from CannObserv/replicator#134's floor arithmetic, not from #133's old figures. It gives about 451 s of waits per start, plus about 40 s between starts, so about 57 min against a broker that refuses and about 68 min against an unreachable one. The unit pins 58 min. Cite these as derived, not measured.
- Say whether CannObserv/replicator#134 (a lower-bound test, and possibly `StartLimitBurst=7`) has landed. That changes the figure again.
- Update the row (around line 390), the "would fail" sentence (around line 395), and step 1d's reference (around line 355). Keep the recovery steps: `reset-failed`, then `start`, then `journalctl -t replicator-failure`.

item.title: SHA-pinned actions have no updater: dependabot.yml for github-actions, minus the generated cadence workflow
item.body:
#88 pinned `astral-sh/setup-uv` and `google-github-actions/auth` to commit SHAs with `# vX.Y.Z` comments, as CannObserv/watcher does. setup-uv has had no floating major tag since v8, so nothing moves those pins. A setup-uv security release would go unannounced: there is no floating tag to follow, and no Node.js deprecation annotation to flag it, as there was in #88.

#88's optional `github-actions`-only `.github/dependabot.yml` was deferred for two reasons:
- **It would rewrite a generated file.** Dependabot scans every workflow. watcher's checkout bump (CannObserv/watcher#356) edited its `context-cadence.yml`, which `install-cadence.sh` generates. `docs/SKILLS.md` says to re-run the installer rather than edit that file, and the next re-run would undo Dependabot's change.
- **Its first PR would be `actions/checkout` v5 → v7**, which #88's brief scoped out.

To do:
- Find out whether `dependabot.yml`'s `exclude-paths` applies to the `github-actions` ecosystem and can skip `.github/workflows/context-cadence.yml`. If it can't, decide whether the cadence installer should emit SHA pins itself (that would be a skills issue, not a broker commit).
- Otherwise use watcher's template: `open-pull-requests-limit: 10`, `commit-message.prefix: chore`, no `uv` ecosystem (#86's wheelhouse reason), and a test guarding the config.
- Decide `actions/checkout` at the same time. When a pin moves, check it against its tag with `gh api repos/<owner>/<action>/git/ref/tags/<tag> --jq .object.sha` (see `tests/deploy/test_workflow_pins.py`).

Found by #88's code review (CR 6).

item.title: Bump the vendored skills to cd61b77+ and adopt patching-hosts' Redis fixes before the next run (gregoryfoster/skills#379 to #385)
item.body:
broker's first run under `patching-hosts` (#67) filed six rough edges and its process-log entry upstream. Each is fixed and pushed at `cd61b77` (gregoryfoster/skills plan step 6h, gregoryfoster/skills#379 to gregoryfoster/skills#385). This issue takes them up here before the next scheduled run, in Monday's window.

### 1. Bump the vendored skills
`skills-vendor/gregoryfoster-skills` is at `6a8ce86`. Bump it to `cd61b77` or later, by hand or through the daily bump, and commit. Nothing needs relinking: only `patching-hosts` changed between the two.

### 2. What changes for broker
- **The reboot chain no longer logs in to check ownership** (gregoryfoster/skills#379). It reads which process listens at Redis's address with `ss`, as root, so the 03:00:52Z refusal and its `ACL LOG` entry don't recur. Under an `aclfile` the scripts never try `requirepass`.
  - **broker's Redis runs `appendonly yes`**, so its stop persists it, and the chain needs no `SAVE` and no login at all.
  - **The manual in-guest reboot isn't needed any more:** `reboot-chain.sh` should pass its datastore gate on this host.
- **A save before the backup ships** (gregoryfoster/skills#382). `recovery-point.sh` saves each Redis a `backup` line covers before starting the unit. Without a login it can't, so it reads `dump.rdb`'s own time instead, and refuses one written more than 10 minutes before the run began (`--rdb-within`). The owner's `SAVE` just before the recovery point, as on 2026-10-13, still passes; a 44-minute-old file no longer does.
- **The record says how Redis persists** (`persistence redis redis-server.service aof`), and `next` says what a restore takes under AOF (gregoryfoster/skills#381). The skill's new `references/datastores.md` describes the restore broker's `docs/RECOVERY.md` already performs.
- **`--post-boot` checks Redis from `/var/log/redis/redis-server.log`** (gregoryfoster/skills#380):
  - the previous process's `ready to exit`;
  - then `DB loaded from …` and `Ready to accept connections`;
  - and it fails on `Creating AOF base file … on server start`.

  A held `redis` step that restarts Redis runs the same check.
- **A held step's version against the dry run's** (gregoryfoster/skills#383). A release published since the dry run, as Tailscale's was, is listed under the bulk's `verdict.version_moved` before approval 3(a), and the held step records what it installed.

### 3. Knob changes (gregoryfoster/skills#384)
- **Replace the 24 `quiet HH:00-HH:07` lines** with one: `quiet *:00-*:07`. It records the same 24 ranges.
- **Add `depends redis-server tailscaled`.** The probe checks Redis's `After=` on tailscaled, and `--post-boot` checks tailscaled was active first. Keep `hold tailscale tailscale` and the bind's `health` line: `depends` doesn't stop or hold anything.
- **The fifth participant stays out**, as it is now: knob.md now says a public knob leaves a private caller out.
- **A credential is optional, and the owner's call.** `datastore redis redis-server <user> <key-file>` lets `recovery-point.sh` take its own `BGSAVE` instead of the owner's `SAVE`. The key file is root-only, or a `systemd-creds` credential under `/etc/credstore.encrypted/`, which root decrypts.
  - The scripts use the login only for `LASTSAVE`, `BGSAVE` and `INFO persistence`, since the backup line covers the dump.
  - Without one, nothing else changes: the chain needs none here.
  - If you add one, give it a dedicated ACL user with just those commands rather than `acladmin`, and note its `ACL LOG` rows the way #48 does.

### 4. Verify on the node, read-only
Nothing here restarts Redis or writes outside a scratch directory:
1. `read-knob.sh --host "$(hostname)"`: no malformed lines, 24 `quiet` ranges from one line, one `depends` record.
2. `probe.sh --refresh-into <scratch>`: no `depends:` finding, since `After=` is there, and `impact.depends` reads `after: true`.
3. `reboot-chain.sh --run <a new 0700 run dir>` **without `--approve`**. item.title: provisioner.revisions now re-creates itself from 0 (CannObserv/provisioner#43): RESTART-WINDOW.md and RECOVERY.md still say `$`
item.body:
CannObserv/provisioner#43 (PR CannObserv/provisioner#47, live 2026-10-14, release b50de3f10717) changes what happens when `provisioner.revisions` goes missing. Two broker docs still describe the old behaviour, and one restore step now matters.

**What changed on provisioner's side**
- A read or reclaim that answers `NOGROUP` now logs a WARNING (`bus_nogroup`). It no longer logs ERROR `bus_reply` every 30 s until a restart. The next step re-creates the group.
- The re-create starts from `0` whenever the consumer has run before (it has a `consumer_state` row, or the process is already running). Only a first-ever start uses `$`. So a restart no longer skips what arrived while the group was gone. `content.revisions` is never trimmed, so the replay misses nothing, and entries already done are acked without work. Today that means 903 entries, walked in 0.08 s (measured 2026-10-14).
- `provisioner.revisions` now heals itself the way `archiver.revisions` does, usually within one backoff (1 s), and logs WARNING `group_recreated`.
- provisioner's `ensure-group` command now refuses once the consumer has run. It's for the first deploy only, so a restore procedure can't use it to re-create the group.

**What it asks of broker**
1. **After a restore or a rebuild, don't pre-create `provisioner.revisions` from `$`.** Leave it to the consumer, or create it from `0` (`XGROUP CREATE content.revisions provisioner.revisions 0`). If something else creates it first, the consumer keeps that position, which it can't read (its grants have no `XINFO`). It warns (`group_recreated_elsewhere`) when it saw the loss while running. If it was down at the time, it can't tell. A `$` there silently skips whatever arrived between the loss and the create.
2. **If provisioner logs `group_recreated_elsewhere`,** its runbook will ask broker to run `XGROUP SETID content.revisions provisioner.revisions 0`, because provisioner has no `setid` grant. The replay acks what's done and files what was skipped, once. If the warning carries `own_create_unconfirmed: true`, the group may be provisioner's own create, whose reply was lost; the reset is harmless then too.

**Suggested doc changes**
- `docs/RESTART-WINDOW.md`, *Every group by name*: put provisioner next to archiver: "Archiver and provisioner recreate a missing group, at `0` (provisioner since CannObserv/provisioner#43, 2026-10-14). Processor, watcher and replicator create theirs only at boot, from `$` …". A missing `provisioner.revisions` is then transient, not a fault, as long as `group_recreated` follows in provisioner's journal. Its pending-age exception stays as it is.
- `docs/RECOVERY.md`, *What is exposed*: "Losing it means every group re-provisions at `ensure_group`'s default `$`" still holds for processor, watcher and replicator. Archiver and provisioner re-create from `0` and replay. Add the restore step from point 1.

**Unchanged:** the grants (`+xgroup|create` already covers the re-create, so nothing new is needed), pending-age probing, and no DLQ.

slot.instructions: `epic` is a GitHub issue that tracks a body of work through a checklist of child issues: `epic.goal` says what it covers, `epic.scope` holds its boundary decisions and rules, `epic.children` its checklist lines (done: ticked), and `epic.parked` what waits on a trigger. `item` is an issue filed since the coordinator last looked, with its state now. Which slot does the coordinator give `item` in this epic?

criteria.child: Work this epic covers and that should be done now or in order: it gets its own checklist line, slotted by dependency. A follow-up to a child, a bug in what a child shipped, or a piece split off a child is a child.
criteria.closed-in-fact: Work this epic covers that is already delivered: the item is closed, or a child's merged change already did it, so it is verified, linked and closed with evidence instead of slotted.
criteria.split: The item mixes work this epic covers with work it doesn't, so the epic's part is filed as its own issue and the rest is left out.
criteria.out of epic: Not this epic's work: another skill, service, area or epic, a record or notice with no action, or tooling around the epic rather than its work. It is said so plainly and cross-linked only where it changes a remaining step.
criteria.duplicate: The same work as an existing child or another open issue, so it is closed in favour of that one.
criteria.park: This epic's concern, but not to be done yet: it waits on a trigger (another repo, a decision, a date, an event) and goes in the parked table with that trigger.

item.title: RECOVERY.md's verification loops skip content.persist, content.process and content.derived: 3 of 9 groups unchecked after a restore
item.body:
Found while shipping #97. `docs/RECOVERY.md` hardcodes stream lists in its verification loops, and they predate three streams that now carry groups. A restore verified by the runbook as written never checks three of the nine groups.

**What the loops miss** [measured 2026-10-15, as `acladmin`: `SCAN` plus `XINFO GROUPS` on each stream]

| Loop | Where | Missing |
|---|---|---|
| `XLEN` | step 4, `docs/RECOVERY.md:253` | `content.persist`, `content.process`, `content.derived` |
| `XINFO GROUPS` | step 4, `:257` | `content.persist` (`replicator.persist`), `content.process` (`processor.process`), `content.derived` (`watcher.derived`) |
| `XINFO GROUPS` | *Verifying a backup by hand*, `:355` | the same three |

The live streams that have groups: `content.fetch`, `content.revisions` (two groups), `content.artifacts`, `content.replicate`, `content.blobs`, `content.persist`, `content.process` and `content.derived`. That makes nine groups, the same nine that `docs/RESTART-WINDOW.md` step 1d names. The loops cover six of them. Step 4 says "The checks that must be exact are the `XLEN` and `XINFO GROUPS` lines", so the three it skips are exactly the checks that matter.

**Why it drifted.** `content.persist` went live 2026-10-01 (#64, #76), and the processing pair arrived with #62. Each change updated the restart runbook, and nothing tied this one to them.

**Suggested fix.** Either works:
- Name all the streams, and add a test that fails when a stream with a consume grant in `deploy/redis-acl.conf`, or a group in `docs/STREAMS.md`, is missing from the loops. That is the same guard pattern the other runbook tests use.
- Or derive the list instead of spelling it, with `rcli acladmin --scan --type stream`, then `XINFO GROUPS` on each. `acladmin` holds `+scan`. This can't drift, but a stream missing after a restore would then pass silently, so the stated list still needs to sit somewhere to compare against.

item.title: Adopt the coordinating-epics skill for #80
item.body:
`coordinating-epics` v1 shipped in gregoryfoster/skills (gregoryfoster/skills#348, `fef0611`). It packages the protocol #80's coordinator has run by hand, and several of its rules came from #80's own findings (99, 100, 128, 145, 147). This issue moves #80 onto it.

**What v1 brings**
- `epic-edit.sh`: one guarded call per body edit. It refuses foreign edits against a saved baseline (a tick you have verified passes with `--accept-ticks`), anchors each operation by ref, derives checkbox counts, lints refs, placeholders and secrets, compare-and-swaps before the PATCH, and reads the body back.
- `scan.sh`: the three re-scan cursors (number watermark, updated-since, and the commit range attributed to children), the epic's own new comments, and cross-repo ref states, as JSON.
- `assets/epic-template.md`: the header cursor lines both scripts read.

**Steps**
1. **Vendor it.** `skills-vendor/gregoryfoster-skills` is at `85caed2`, one commit before the skill. Bump it to `fef0611` or later, then symlink `skills/coordinating-epics` and `.claude/skills/coordinating-epics` (managing-skills, Step 2/2b). The auto-refresh hook bumps the pointer but creates no symlinks.
2. **Adopt at the next check-in, as that check-in's one write** (SKILL.md, "Adopt an epic that exists"). Run `scan.sh --repo CannObserv/broker --epic 80 --watermark 97 --from-sha <last verified SHA>`; its `since` comes from the header's `Last check-in`. Then make one `epic-edit.sh --repo CannObserv/broker --epic 80 --adopt-live --lint-all --scan <report> --ops <file>` call, dry-run first, with `header` ops for `Last check-in` (`{checked}`), `Last issue seen` (`{last_seen}`), `Next` and `Last verified SHA`.
3. **After that,** every body edit goes through `epic-edit.sh`, and each check-in starts with `scan.sh`.

**What a dry run on today's body found** (a copy of the body, run against the fake `gh` in the skill's tests; nothing was written):
- **The header holds three fields in one paragraph.** A `header` op on `Last check-in` rewrites that whole line, so `Last issue seen` and `Next` need their own `header` ops in the same call; they are added as list lines below it. The call applies cleanly.
- **`--lint-all` flags one line,** "Sibling epic #92" under "Waiting on others": `#94` and `#95` each follow another repo's qualified ref. They mean broker's own, which is how GitHub links them, but the lint asks for `CannObserv/broker#94` and `CannObserv/broker#95` written out. That line leads with no ref, so fix it with a `replace-section` on "Waiting on others" in the same call. Or drop `--lint-all`, and the line is linted the next time it changes.

**Known limits in v1:** CI by job is still checked by hand (gregoryfoster/skills#394), and comments are not linted before posting (gregoryfoster/skills#395).

**When the run ends:** journal it in the skill's process log. The skill is vendored here, so draft the entry in this repo and file it upstream as an issue on gregoryfoster/skills ("Adding an entry" in `references/process-log.md`).

item.title: AOF replay silently drops MULTI/EXEC blocks while default is the -@all tombstone (7.0.15 and Valkey 7.2.13)
item.body:
Found by #85's off-node rehearsal, 2026-10-15. Live today on 7.0.15, and Valkey 7.2.13 behaves the same way, so the engine swap neither causes it nor fixes it.

## The finding [measured]

**With `default` tombstoned `off ... -@all` (live since #52), the AOF replay drops every `MULTI`/`EXEC` block in the incr file.** Mechanism, inferred and not measured: the AOF-loading client runs `EXEC`'s ACL re-check as `default`. The measured part is the contrast below, where the same file replays whole once `default` is open. Each queued command fails with `-NOPERM ACLs rules changed between the moment the transaction was accumulated and the EXEC call`, and the server logs `== CRITICAL ==` once per command and finishes loading. It does not abort.

There are two sources of these blocks. Both are lost:
- **Explicit transactions:** redis-py `pipeline(transaction=True)` around `XADD`s.
- **Engine-wrapped propagation:** when one command propagates more than one op, the engine wraps the ops in `MULTI`/`EXEC`. That covers an `XREADGROUP` delivering more than one entry (one `XCLAIM` per entry) and an `XAUTOCLAIM`/`XCLAIM` moving more than one entry.

Minimal repro on a throwaway loopback server: `appendonly yes`, a writer user with `+@all`, then 1 plain `XADD`, a 2-`XADD` transaction, and `XREADGROUP COUNT 3`, then restart.

| binary | `default` | before restart (xlen, last-delivered, pending) | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| redis-server 7.0.15 | `off resetchannels -@all` | 3, `<id>-1`, 3 | **1, `0-0`, 0** (5 CRITICAL lines) |
| redis-server 7.0.15 | `on nopass ~* &* +@all` | 3, `<id>-1`, 3 | 3, `<id>-1`, 3 |
| valkey-server 7.2.13 | `off resetchannels -@all` | 3, `<id>-1`, 3 | **1, `0-0`, 0** (5 CRITICAL lines) |
| valkey-server 7.2.13 | `on nopass ~* &* +@all` | 3, `<id>-1`, 3 | 3, `<id>-1`, 3 |

## Why nothing has been lost yet [measured]

- **The live incr holds no `MULTI`.** Today's `appendonly.aof.3.incr.aof` (2026-10-05T23:22Z to 2026-10-15T22:50Z, 16.2 MB) contains 0. That fits participants that read `COUNT 1`, claim one entry at a time and use no transactions, but only provisioner's client has been read off source (`deploy/redis-acl.conf`); for the rest it is inferred from the count.
- **Replay matched live exactly.** Replaying a copy of it on 7.0.15 reproduced every live `entries-added`, `last-generated-id` and `last-delivered-id`.
- **Planned restarts are covered.** `docs/RESTART-WINDOW.md` step 1a-bis (`BGREWRITEAOF` first) folds the AOF into a base RDB, which carries no `MULTI`.
- **Unplanned restarts are not.** A crash, an OOM kill, or a patching reboot (#67, 2026-10-13) replays the raw incr.

**So this is latent:** the first consumer that batches reads or claims, or publishes in a transaction, starts writing entries that only an unplanned restart will drop. The log line is the only signal, and nothing reads it.

## Options (to weigh, not decided)

1. **Give the tombstone the commands it needs, keeping it `off`.** An `off` user cannot authenticate, so its grants are unreachable by a client. It is the AOF client's identity, though, and `-@all` was chosen as defence in depth if anyone ever flips it `on` (CLAUDE.md, #52). Needs a rehearsal of which grant is the minimum.
2. **Keep the tombstone; keep `MULTI` out of the incr.** Pin "no transactions, `COUNT 1`" as a cohort contract, and/or have the probe watch the AOF for `MULTI`. The probe has no file access today.
3. **Find the upstream fix.** A quick search did not find an upstream report. Check Redis 7.2+/8.x and Valkey 8.x before choosing 1 or 2.

Refs #85 (where it was found), #52 (the tombstone).

item.title: Valkey pre-window changes on 7.0: backup.py reads valkey-ver and valkey-check-rdb, the probe sends no CLIENT SETINFO, acl_server finds valkey-server (#85 P1, P1b, P2)
item.body:
#85's rehearsal (its 2026-10-15T23:03Z comment, *Window plan*) names three code changes that must be merged and live **on 7.0, before the Valkey window**. Each is engine-agnostic, so it changes nothing today. Without them, the first backup after the swap records no version or fails, the probe fills `ACL LOG`, and the throwaway-server tests skip.

**P1: `src/broker/backup.py`** [measured in the rehearsal]
- Valkey's RDB carries `valkey-ver = '7.2.13'` and no `redis-ver`. `backup.py` reads `report.get("redis-ver")`, so every Valkey-era backup would record `redis_version: ""`, and `restore.py --list` would show it blank. `tests/deploy/test_backup_restore_rehearsal.py:156` (`assert state["redis_version"]`) fails on it.
- Valkey writes RDB v11, and 7.0.15's `redis-check-rdb` rejects it (exit 1). `backup.py` resolves `redis-check-rdb` from `PATH`.
- **Change:** take the version from `redis-ver` or `valkey-ver`, and resolve `valkey-check-rdb` before `redis-check-rdb`. TDD, with a test for each report shape.

**P1b: `src/broker/bus_health.py`** [measured]
- `Redis.from_url(...)` keeps redis-py's default `driver_info`, so the probe sends `CLIENT SETINFO`. On Valkey without a grant, that's 2 `client|setinfo` denials per tick as `brokeradmin`.
- `test_the_probe_holds_only_what_it_issues` keeps `brokeradmin` from holding a grant `src/broker/` never calls.
- **Change:** `Redis.from_url(..., driver_info=None)`. Measured against Valkey with no grant: 0 `ACL LOG` entries, against 1 with the default. On 7.0 it drops only a call the server already ignores.

**P2: `tests/deploy/conftest.py`'s `acl_server`** [measured]
- It looks up `redis-server` only. Valkey ships no binary of that name (nor does the compat package), so after the swap every throwaway-server test on the node would skip rather than run.
- **Change:** find `valkey-server` as well as `redis-server`.

**Done when:** all three are merged and live on 7.0.15, with CI and audit green and the node's `tests/deploy -rs` unchanged (baseline 450 passed, 4 skipped, the DLQ four). Optionally, re-run the three against the extracted Valkey binary, as #85 did, and show the backup rehearsal test passing.

**Not here:** P3 (native paths) and P4 (the `+client|setinfo` grants). Both merge in the window itself, gated on #95.

Filed by #80's coordinator from #85's report.

item.title: audit_lock.sh reports 'did not run' under uv < 0.13: --preview-features audit-command is unknown to older uv (CI unaffected)
item.body:
From CannObserv/usa-wa#499, where usa-wa ported `scripts/audit_lock.sh` and its test. A cross-check, not an outage: **broker's CI audit works.** It is affected only when the script is run by hand on a host with an older uv.

## What happens

`scripts/audit_lock.sh` runs `uv audit --frozen --preview-features audit-command`. uv 0.11.16, the usa-wa host's version, doesn't know that feature name:

```
$ uv audit --frozen --preview-features audit-command
error: invalid value 'audit-command' for '--preview-features <PREVIEW_FEATURES>': Unknown feature flag
$ echo $?
2
```

Exit 2 takes the script's `*)` branch: `::warning title=uv audit did not run::`. So on any host whose uv predates the feature name, the by-hand run the header promises ("run by .github/workflows/audit.yml and by hand") never audits. It also reports that clearly, so this isn't a silent false clean.

**CI is unaffected:** `audit.yml` installs uv 0.13.1 through `setup-uv` (run 38923300370, 2026-10-16), and that run printed "Found no known vulnerabilities … in 46 packages".

## Options
- Pin a floor: `[tool.uv] required-version = ">=0.13"` (or whichever release introduced `audit-command`), so an older uv refuses with a clear message.
- Or detect support: try with the flag, and retry without it on exit 2 with "Unknown feature flag". usa-wa's port calls `uv audit --frozen` without the flag; on 0.11.16 that works and reports normally.

`tests/deploy/test_lock_audit.py` pins the flag, so whichever option you pick will need a test change.

Not filed separately: two other usa-wa#499 notes, (1) a stale PyPy-only urllib3 1.26 in the lock and (2) Dependabot grouped uv updates dropped for dependencies with extras (dependabot/dependabot-core#16431), **don't apply to broker**. Its lock has only urllib3 2.8.0, and its Dependabot covers github-actions only.

slot.instructions: `epic` is a GitHub issue that tracks a body of work through a checklist of child issues: `epic.goal` says what it covers, `epic.scope` holds its boundary decisions and rules, `epic.children` its checklist lines (done: ticked), and `epic.parked` what waits on a trigger. `item` is an issue filed since the coordinator last looked, with its state now. Which slot does the coordinator give `item` in this epic?

criteria.child: Work this epic covers and that should be done now or in order: it gets its own checklist line, slotted by dependency. A follow-up to a child, a bug in what a child shipped, or a piece split off a child is a child.
criteria.closed-in-fact: Work this epic covers that is already delivered: the item is closed, or a child's merged change already did it, so it is verified, linked and closed with evidence instead of slotted.
criteria.split: The item mixes work this epic covers with work it doesn't, so the epic's part is filed as its own issue and the rest is left out.
criteria.out of epic: Not this epic's work: another skill, service, area or epic, a record or notice with no action, or tooling around the epic rather than its work. It is said so plainly and cross-linked only where it changes a remaining step.
criteria.duplicate: The same work as an existing child or another open issue, so it is closed in favour of that one.
criteria.park: This epic's concern, but not to be done yet: it waits on a trigger (another repo, a decision, a date, an event) and goes in the parked table with that trigger.

item.title: Bump co-core from 0.19.6 to the newest release, ahead of #93's headless-Watcher streams
item.body:
broker runs **co-core 0.19.6** (`pyproject.toml`: `co-core>=0.19.6,<0.20`; `uv.lock`). The local wheelhouse already holds releases up to **0.34.0**. #93, which inventories, grants and probes `info.watch-events` and `info.watch-check`, needs the co-core release that defines those streams. That's CannObserv/cannobserv#568 ("Release co-core with the headless-Watcher contracts", open). CannObserv/cannobserv#563 and CannObserv/cannobserv#564 merged to `main` at `6212c0d7` on 2026-10-16 without a release.

broker derives group names and stream kinds from co-core rather than spelling them (AGENTS.md, *Mirrored constants*). So #93 can't land on 0.19.6, and doing a 15-minor-version jump inside #93's thread would hide a contract change inside a grant change.

**What broker uses from co-core** [measured at `3c8257c`]: the twelve topic constants (`CONTENT_*`, `INFO_CHANGES`, `INFO_REGISTRY`, `INFO_WATCH_STATUS`), `group_name(topic, service, purpose=None)` and `stream_kind()`, all from `co_core.pure.adapters.bus.streams`. All three are present in 0.34.0, and `group_name` has the same signature [read from the wheel]. The full diff still needs reading: `_STREAM_KINDS`, the group-name derivation, anything the probe's units or tests pin.

**To do**

Burn down broker's open backlog. The goal: **technical correctness and operational stability first, to the point where feature work can go on safely.** One coordinator thread holds this epic. The rule (operator, 2026-10-05): correctness and operational stability first, and **issues where another repo is waiting on our reply go first.** Within a tier: smaller first, and a dependency outranks size.

item.title: #22 C1: the probe and backup report the REVISION they ran (dev until releases)
item.body:
Child **C1** of epic #22. Design: [`docs/plans/2026-10-17-22-release-deploy.md`](https://github.com/CannObserv/broker/blob/main/docs/plans/2026-10-17-22-release-deploy.md), D5 and B7. **No unit change.** It ships the way every change ships today: merged into `~/broker`, live at the next tick.

The probe and the backup report the code they ran, so the first release (C2) is visible on its first tick.

## Scope
- **Reading `REVISION`.** A small reader for the `REVISION` file at the project root (`Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]`). It returns the file's stripped contents, or `dev` when the file is absent.
- **The probe:**
  - adds `revision` to the `Bus health summary` line;
  - adds it to the co-status check-in's **`variables`**. **Never** to `metadata`: `metadata.fault` is what co-status compares (#84), and a revision there would report every deploy as a new fault.
- **The backup:** writes `revision` into `state.json` on success and on failure, and logs it.
- **Tests first:**
  - absent → `dev`;
  - present → its contents;
  - the payload carries `variables.revision`, and `metadata` stays `{"fault": [...]}` only;
  - the summary line still matches `.skills/patching-hosts`' `health` grep (`"finding_count": 0`).
- **Docs:** `deploy/README.md`'s check-in payload, and `docs/BUS-HEALTH.md` if it describes the summary line.

## Verify (live)
- [ ] The next tick's `Bus health summary` has `"revision": "dev"` and 0 findings.
- [ ] The knob's `health` command exits 0.
- [ ] The tick's check-in landed: no check-in failure is in the journal, and co-status shows the tick.
- [ ] The next hourly backup's `/var/lib/broker-backup/state.json` has `"revision": "dev"`, and the probe raises no `backup` finding.
- [ ] `ACL LOG`, read as `acladmin` and never reset, has no new entry.
- [ ] CI is green by job. `tests/deploy` passes on the node with the env sourced.
