item.title: Adopt the coordinating-epics skill for #598
item.body:
`coordinating-epics` v1 shipped in gregoryfoster/skills (gregoryfoster/skills#348, `fef0611`). It packages the protocol #598's coordinator has run by hand, and several of its rules came from this run's findings (54–60). This issue moves #598 onto it.

**What v1 brings**
- `epic-edit.sh`: one guarded call per body edit. It refuses foreign edits against a saved baseline (a tick you have verified passes with `--accept-ticks`), anchors each operation by ref, derives checkbox counts, lints refs, placeholders and secrets, compare-and-swaps before the PATCH, and reads the body back.
- `scan.sh`: the three re-scan cursors (number watermark, updated-since, and the commit range attributed to children), the epic's own new comments, and cross-repo ref states, as JSON.
- `assets/epic-template.md`: the header cursor lines both scripts read.

**Steps**
1. **Vendor it.** `skills-vendor/gregoryfoster-skills` is at `6a8ce86`, which predates the skill. Bump it to `fef0611` or later, then symlink `skills/coordinating-epics` and `.claude/skills/coordinating-epics` (managing-skills, Step 2/2b). The auto-refresh hook bumps the pointer but creates no symlinks.
2. **Adopt at the next check-in, as that check-in's one write** (SKILL.md, "Adopt an epic that exists"). Run `scan.sh --repo CannObserv/power-map --epic 598 --since <the last check-in, with a zone> --watermark <the last number the epic accounts for> --from-sha <last verified SHA>`. Then make one `epic-edit.sh --repo CannObserv/power-map --epic 598 --adopt-live --scan <report> --ops <file>` call, dry-run first, with `header` ops for `Last check-in` (`{checked}`), `Last issue seen` (`{last_seen}`) and `Last verified SHA`. The epic has no cursor lines yet, so `scan.sh` needs all three cursors passed this once.
3. **After that,** every body edit goes through `epic-edit.sh`, and each check-in starts with `scan.sh`.

**What a dry run on today's body found** (a copy of the body, run against the fake `gh` in the skill's tests; nothing was written):
- **The epic has no header cursor lines yet.** The three `header` ops add them as a list after the opening paragraph, and the call applies cleanly.
- **There is no `## Log` section.** The `log` op writes only to a section headed "Log", and "Re-triage log" isn't one. Add "Log" with `add-section`, passing the adoption's log line as its text, and keep or retire the old section.
- **Every checklist item leads with its ref,** so `tick`, `note` and `set-line` can reach each one.
- **`--lint-all` would flag 15 lines,** all short refs such as `usa-wa#412`, which GitHub does not link. The steps above leave `--lint-all` out. Each line is then linted the first time it changes, and must be fixed then (check-in.md, "A lint refusal on a line you only ticked").

**Known limits in v1:** CI by job is still checked by hand (gregoryfoster/skills#394), and comments are not linted before posting (gregoryfoster/skills#395).

**When the run ends:** journal it in the skill's process log. The skill is vendored here, so draft the entry in this repo and file it upstream as an issue on gregoryfoster/skills ("Adding an entry" in `references/process-log.md`).

scope.text:
- A correctness bug on a surface being kept stays open, even when nothing uses it today. An enhancement or policy question on an unused surface closes with a reopen trigger, or shrinks to a docs-only "decided: no". Decided 2026-10-01 (#481 kept; #485, #507 and #513 closed).
- Producer-owned data is fixed upstream or pinned through the overlay, never by a bare `UPDATE` the applier reverts. Data guards are ratchets against a baseline. Decided 2026-10-10 (#506, #639).
- Every outbound notification goes through Notifier, and co-status is the watchdog. Decided 2026-10-12 (#566).
- Each release gets a `v<version>` tag on the deployed commit. The implementer pushes it, and the coordinator verifies it and pushes it when missed (the operator approved this 2026-10-09). #631's timer is the backstop.
Every open issue numbered #481 or higher, and every issue filed during the run, is closed, parked with a written trigger, or in the Ops lane waiting on the operator. #490 closes with #651.

item.title: Text Postgres cannot store (NUL, lone surrogates) 500s across the API — one boundary rule, 422 everywhere
item.body:
## Problem
Text that Postgres can't store reaches asyncpg unchecked, and the request fails with an unhandled **500**. Two kinds of text do this:
- a **NUL** character (U+0000, `%00` in a URL, `\^@` in JSON) raises `CharacterNotInRepertoireError: invalid byte sequence for encoding "UTF8": 0x00`;
- a **lone surrogate** (U+D800–U+DFFF, e.g. `"\ud800"` in JSON, which Python's `json` accepts) raises `UnicodeEncodeError` or asyncpg `DataError` ("surrogates not allowed").

Nothing has to be wrong with the caller's intent for this to happen: one stray byte in an id or a search string is enough. Any 500 also wakes the alerting path.

## Evidence (test DB, 2026-10-15, found while working on #654)
I probed every public `GET` route under `/api/v1`, putting `x%00y` into each path parameter and `x\x00y` into each query parameter, with a savepoint around each request. Results across 61 inputs:
- **17 raised** (a 500 in production);
- 25 answered 422 (enum or int validation fails before any SQL runs);
- 17 answered 403 (scope-gated routes, so the probe never reached their SQL);
- 2 answered 404.

The 17 that raised:
```
QUERY /api/v1/assignments ?person_id
QUERY /api/v1/assignments ?role_id
PATH /api/v1/assignments/{assignment_id} [assignment_id]
QUERY /api/v1/jurisdictions/resolve ?slug
QUERY /api/v1/jurisdictions ?type
PATH /api/v1/jurisdictions/{jurisdiction_id} [jurisdiction_id]
PATH /api/v1/jurisdictions/{jurisdiction_id}/relationships [jurisdiction_id]
PATH /api/v1/jurisdictions/{jurisdiction_id}/lineage [jurisdiction_id]
QUERY /api/v1/orgs/search ?q
QUERY /api/v1/orgs/search ?jurisdiction
PATH /api/v1/orgs/{org_id} [org_id]
PATH /api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/events [org_id]
QUERY /api/v1/people/search ?q
PATH /api/v1/people/{person_id} [person_id]
PATH /api/v1/people/{person_id}/events [person_id]
QUERY /api/v1/roles ?organization_id
PATH /api/v1/roles/{role_id} [role_id]
```
Lone surrogates raise in the same places: I confirmed `GET /orgs/search?q=%ED%A0%80`-style input (`q="\ud800"`) raises `UnicodeEncodeError`, and `POST /orgs/batch-get {"ids": ["\ud800"]}` raises `DataError`.

**Not probed yet:** the routes gated on the 403 scopes (embeddings), every `POST` / `PATCH` body (the observation writes in particular), and the **admin** dashboard's path, query and form inputs. They take the same unchecked strings and very likely fail the same way. Separately, the request-log middleware stores the raw path, so its capture write for a `%00` path would fail too. It's fire-and-forget and logs a WARNING, so this needs checking rather than assuming.

## Current inconsistency
#654's `POST /orgs/batch-get` (branch `feat/654-batch-org-read`, unmerged) has a route-local guard: a NUL-bearing id answers `not_found`. It does nothing for lone surrogates, so that batch still returns a 500 on `"\ud800"`. A guard on one route is exactly the pattern this issue should replace. **Decide here how the batch handles both values**, and drop that local guard in favour of the API-wide rule.

## Proposed rule (one rule, every input surface)
> Text Postgres can't represent (NUL, lone surrogates) never reaches the database. The API rejects it at the boundary with **`422`** and the standard validation body, on path params, query params, JSON bodies and admin form fields alike. Never a 500, never a route-local special case.

- **422, not 404 or `not_found`.** A request carrying such text is malformed. It isn't a lookup of an id PM happens not to have. A single status works for ids, free text and writes, with no per-field judgement. For the batch, a NUL or surrogate id fails the envelope with a 422, the same as a non-string id does today. "One bad id must not fail the batch" (#654) still holds for well-formed strings that aren't orgs.
- **Admin:** a 422 or an error flash, whichever matches the admin's existing validation conventions (`docs/ADMIN.md`). It must not be a 500.

## Decisions to make here
1. **Mechanism.** Options:
   - (a) ASGI middleware that checks the decoded path and query, plus a body check for JSON and form payloads;
   - (b) a validated string type on every `str` input, enforced by a sweep test so none is missed;
   - (c) an exception handler that maps asyncpg's encoding errors to 422.

   **Recommendation:** (a) as the rule, plus (c) as a narrow backstop. The backstop maps only `CharacterNotInRepertoireError` and asyncpg `DataError` / `UnicodeEncodeError` that come from argument encoding, never every `UnicodeEncodeError`, and it logs whenever it fires, because firing means (a) missed a surface. (b) alone depends on every new field remembering to use the type.
2. **Response body:** the FastAPI `HTTPValidationError` shape, with `loc` naming the offending field where it's known. Everything is published as one schema (`src/api/openapi.py`).
3. **Batch:** confirm the whole call gets a 422 (recommended) rather than a per-id `not_found`, and remove the #654 local guard.
4. **Request log:** sanitize the stored path and query (e.g. escape NUL) so the capture write can't fail on the same bytes.

## Tests
- **A sweep test:** the probe above, generalized. It covers every `/api/v1` route and method, every path, query and body string field, both values, plus the admin routes, and asserts no 5xx and a 422 with the standard body. It derives the routes from `app.routes`, so a new route is covered automatically.
- **Unit tests** for the middleware's decoding: `%00`, `%ED%A0%80`, `\^@` and `\ud800` in JSON, a valid surrogate pair (`😀`), which must pass, and a literal backslash-u sequence (`"\\^@"`), which must also pass.

## Docs
- `docs/CONVENTIONS.md`: the input rule.
- `docs/PUBLIC_API.md`: what a caller gets back.
- `docs/API_ORGS.md` § Batch read: the batch outcome, once decision 3 is made.

slot.instructions: `epic` is a GitHub issue that tracks a body of work through a checklist of child issues: `epic.goal` says what it covers, `epic.scope` holds its boundary decisions and rules, `epic.children` its checklist lines (done: ticked), and `epic.parked` what waits on a trigger. `item` is an issue filed since the coordinator last looked, with its state now. Which slot does the coordinator give `item` in this epic?

criteria.child: Work this epic covers and that should be done now or in order: it gets its own checklist line, slotted by dependency. A follow-up to a child, a bug in what a child shipped, or a piece split off a child is a child.
criteria.closed-in-fact: Work this epic covers that is already delivered: the item is closed, or a child's merged change already did it, so it is verified, linked and closed with evidence instead of slotted.
criteria.split: The item mixes work this epic covers with work it doesn't, so the epic's part is filed as its own issue and the rest is left out.
criteria.out of epic: Not this epic's work: another skill, service, area or epic, a record or notice with no action, or tooling around the epic rather than its work. It is said so plainly and cross-linked only where it changes a remaining step.
criteria.duplicate: The same work as an existing child or another open issue, so it is closed in favour of that one.
criteria.park: This epic's concern, but not to be done yet: it waits on a trigger (another repo, a decision, a date, an event) and goes in the parked table with that trigger.

item.title: Flaky: test_identify_batch_groups_match_single_identify — HNSW returns < top_k under dead index entries (iterative_scan off)
item.body:
## Symptom
`tests/api/public/test_embeddings.py::test_identify_batch_groups_match_single_identify` (#638) failed once in a full integration run (`-m "integration and not browser"`, 2026-10-15→16, branch `feat/654-batch-org-read`, 3723 passed / 1 failed):

```
AssertionError: assert [{'embedding_...00000Z', ...}] == [{'embedding_...00000Z', ...}]
Right contains one more item: {'embedding_id': '01M50ZS8G2SKE4KNWQ074W8GHB', ... }
```

The single `/identify` call returned **one more match** than the `identify-batch` group did for the same random query vector (`top_k=3`, five seeded rows).

- It passed in that branch's previous full run.
- It passed 3 of 3 times when `test_embeddings.py` was run alone.
- That branch doesn't touch embeddings.

## Probable mechanism (evidence, not proof)
Both routes use the HNSW index (`person_embeddings_pyannote_community_1_embed_hnsw`, `m=16, ef_construction=64`, partial `WHERE archived_at IS NULL`). Approximate search can return **fewer than `top_k`**, and the count can change between two calls.

Test DB state after the run:
- **pgvector 0.8.1**, `hnsw.ef_search = 40`, `hnsw.iterative_scan = off`.
- **The index is full of dead entries.** The table has 0 live rows, yet the index is 296 kB. Every embedding test seeds rows through the rollback client, and a rolled-back insert leaves an index entry that only vacuum removes. A scan collects `ef_search` = 40 candidates and then drops the invisible ones. When dead entries crowd out the five live rows, fewer than 3 come back.
- **Autovacuum runs mid-suite.** `autovacuum_count = 56`, and `last_autovacuum = 2026-10-16 00:05:07 UTC` falls inside that run. A vacuum between the batch call and the single call changes the candidate set, so the two calls can disagree. That fits a test that fails only now and then and never in isolation.

## Production relevance (to decide)
Prod doesn't roll back. But archiving an embedding is an `UPDATE`, so the old version stays in the index as a dead entry until vacuum. With `iterative_scan = off`, `/identify`, `/identify-batch` and `/verify*` can briefly return fewer than `top_k` live matches after churn. pgvector 0.8's `hnsw.iterative_scan = relaxed_order` (or `strict_order`) keeps scanning until it has enough rows.

## Options
1. **Test only:** run the comparison under exact search (`SET LOCAL enable_indexscan = off` on the shared connection), or under `SET LOCAL hnsw.iterative_scan = strict_order`, so both calls are deterministic. Keep a separate test that the index path is actually used.
2. **Product:** set `hnsw.iterative_scan` (and maybe `ef_search`) for the identify and verify queries, in the session or per transaction. Then the "fewer than `top_k`" case disappears in production too, and the test becomes deterministic as a side effect. This needs a latency check.
3. Both.

**Recommendation:**
- First, confirm the mechanism: reproduce by seeding, rolling back many times, then comparing the two calls with and without a `VACUUM` in between.
- Then take option 2 if the latency cost is negligible at prod's row counts, otherwise option 1.

Found while working on #654.

slot.instructions: `epic` is a GitHub issue that tracks a body of work through a checklist of child issues: `epic.goal` says what it covers, `epic.scope` holds its boundary decisions and rules, `epic.children` its checklist lines (done: ticked), and `epic.parked` what waits on a trigger. `item` is an issue filed since the coordinator last looked, with its state now. Which slot does the coordinator give `item` in this epic?

criteria.child: Work this epic covers and that should be done now or in order: it gets its own checklist line, slotted by dependency. A follow-up to a child, a bug in what a child shipped, or a piece split off a child is a child.
criteria.closed-in-fact: Work this epic covers that is already delivered: the item is closed, or a child's merged change already did it, so it is verified, linked and closed with evidence instead of slotted.
criteria.split: The item mixes work this epic covers with work it doesn't, so the epic's part is filed as its own issue and the rest is left out.
criteria.out of epic: Not this epic's work: another skill, service, area or epic, a record or notice with no action, or tooling around the epic rather than its work. It is said so plainly and cross-linked only where it changes a remaining step.
criteria.duplicate: The same work as an existing child or another open issue, so it is closed in favour of that one.
criteria.park: This epic's concern, but not to be done yet: it waits on a trigger (another repo, a decision, a date, an event) and goes in the parked table with that trigger.

epic.title: Burn-down: open issues ≥ #481 after the #490 cutover
epic.goal: Burn-down of every open issue ≥ #481, re-triaged after the #490 dataset-subscription cutover (#501, applied 2026-09-18). Bugs and small workstreams come first. Each issue gets its own agent thread; this epic is checked off from the coordinating thread, which re-triages any new issues each time it is updated.

scope.text:
- A correctness bug on a surface being kept stays open, even when nothing uses it today. An enhancement or policy question on an unused surface closes with a reopen trigger, or shrinks to a docs-only "decided: no". Decided 2026-10-01 (#481 kept; #485, #507 and #513 closed).
- Producer-owned data is fixed upstream or pinned through the overlay, never by a bare `UPDATE` the applier reverts. Data guards are ratchets against a baseline. Decided 2026-10-10 (#506, #639).
- Every outbound notification goes through Notifier, and co-status is the watchdog. Decided 2026-10-12 (#566).
- Each release gets a `v<version>` tag on the deployed commit. The implementer pushes it, and the coordinator verifies it and pushes it when missed (the operator approved this 2026-10-09). #631's timer is the backstop.
Every open issue numbered #481 or higher, and every issue filed during the run, is closed, parked with a written trigger, or in the Ops lane waiting on the operator. #490 closes with #651.

item.title: Root disk keeps hitting 98% — cap pytest basetemps, prune VS Code server builds, add a headroom alert
item.body:
## Problem
The VM's root filesystem (`/dev/root`, 19G, shared by `/`, `/home` and `/tmp`) keeps filling up. Each time, manual pruning buys a few days.

| Date | Peak | Effect | Recovery |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-09-25 | 100% | every shell call failed; `git commit` exit 128 | pruned pytest basetemps + VS Code server builds → 75% |
| 2026-10-14 | 98% | a unit run died with ENOSPC | basetemps + VS Code builds → 81% |
| 2026-10-15 | 98% (480M free) | two pre-commit unit runs failed (a git-fixture test's `git commit` exited 128), which looked like a code failure | basetemps only → 90% |

**Today's baseline, with no pytest basetemps, is ~16G of 19G (90%).** One full unit run (the pre-commit hook included) leaves ~480M in `/tmp/pytest-of-exedev/pytest-N`, and pytest keeps three runs (~1.4G). So two or three commits in one session are enough to reach 98%. This is the **production** VM: a full root disk also starves `power-map.service`, its timers and journald, not only agent sessions.

## Where it goes (2026-10-16, `du -xsh`)
| Path | Size | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `/usr` | 4.1G | system (`/usr/lib` 1.6G, `/usr/share` 0.8G, `/usr/local` 0.8G incl. the system Claude Code, #542) |
| `~/.vscode-server` | **4.9G** | `cli/servers` 2.6G = **4 server builds × ~650M**, of which only `Stable-07f806f9` is running. The others are `16507d91` (10-14), `6d62b1d5` (10-15) and `7baac39e` (10-13). Plus `extensions` 1.5G, `data` 765M, and two `code-*` CLIs. A new build lands with every VS Code update (~weekly), and nothing removes the old ones. |
| `~/.npm` | 2.0G | npm cache |
| `~/.cache` | 2.0G | `uv` 1.4G, `ms-playwright` 656M (needed by the browser tier) |
| `~/power-map` | 1.3G | main checkout + each worktree ~0.8G (its own `.venv` + `node_modules`, #450/#554) |
| `~/.claude` | 915M | session transcripts / scratchpads |
| `~/.socraticode` | 457M | left after #568 moved the store to co-index. Check whether it's still needed. |
| `/tmp/pytest-of-exedev` | 0–1.4G | grows by ~480M per unit run, three runs kept |

## Proposed fix (decide here)
1. **Pytest basetemps:** set `tmp_path_retention_count = 1` (or `tmp_path_retention_policy = "failed"`) in `[tool.pytest.ini_options]`. That's ~1G back immediately and permanently, and nothing relies on old basetemps. Also find out why one unit run writes ~480M: the mapping tier's dbt builds are ~8.5M each, and many of them make up most of it.
2. **VS Code server builds:** a scheduled prune that keeps the running build, found via `readlink /proc/*/exe` and never process args (see #586 / the secret-handling notes), plus the newest one, and removes the rest along with their `code-*` CLIs. That's about 1.3G today, and it stops the ~650M-per-week growth. Run it as a weekly user timer, or as a step in an existing maintenance unit.
3. **Caches:** a periodic `npm cache clean --force` / `uv cache prune` (uv's prune keeps what the lockfiles need). Ask before the first run, because both slow the next install.
4. **Alert before the disk is full:** a disk-headroom guard, like the uptime guards (#347/#410), that check-ins through co-status/notifier (#566) when `/` passes 85%. Today the first signal is a failing agent session.
5. **Longer term:** grow the root volume (DO resize) if the baseline stays above ~80% after 1–3.

Out of scope: production data. The DB is on DO (#579), so nothing in `/var/lib` here grows with the data.

## Acceptance
- With 1–3 in place, the baseline is at or below 75% and survives a week of normal sessions.
- A full unit run, or three in a row, never takes `/` above 85%.
- The guard in 4 fires on a test threshold.

item.title: Trusted Sources admits an exe.dev egress IP that other VMs may share
item.body:
## A hazard to weigh, not a measured exposure on this host

From the cohort image repo's migration-runbook work, 2026-10-16.

**Measured 2026-10-15, on throwaway exe.dev VMs:**
- Two VMs created together reported the **same** public egress IP.
- A third VM on the same account reported a different one.

So exe.dev's outbound NAT is shared between VMs, at least sometimes. The 2026-08-09 outage here (#410) fits that too: the egress IP rotated with no change on the VM's side.

**Not measured:**
- whether power-map's own egress IP is shared with any other VM, ours or anyone else's;
- how exe.dev assigns egress addresses.

## Why it matters here

`co-pm-db-1`'s Trusted Sources admits power-map's egress IP. If other VMs leave through the same address, the allowlist admits them too, at the network layer. What still stands between them and the database is its credentials and TLS. DigitalOcean's managed Postgres requires both by default; this cluster's settings weren't read.

So Trusted Sources isn't a per-VM boundary, and an audit or threat model shouldn't count it as one.

## Options to weigh

- **Record it:** note in `docs/RUNBOOK_DB_TRIAGE.md` (or `docs/AUDITS.md`) that the allowlist admits a NAT address other VMs may share, and that the credentials and TLS are the boundary.
- **Strengthen what's behind it:**
  - the app connects with `sslmode=verify-full` against DigitalOcean's CA;
  - its role holds only what it needs;
  - its password is strong, and rotation is documented.
- **Measure:** from a throwaway VM, compare its egress IP with power-map's. `power-map-egress-ip` already reads power-map's own every 5 minutes.
- **Ask exe.dev** whether a VM can have a dedicated egress IP, and how the pool is shared.

## For the migration onto the cohort base image

The cohort's migration runbook admits the new VM's egress IP before cutover, and keeps the old one admitted until the old VM retires. The new VM may share its address with other VMs as well. power-map's assessment under the deployment epic carries this issue.

slot.instructions: `epic` is a GitHub issue that tracks a body of work through a checklist of child issues: `epic.goal` says what it covers, `epic.scope` holds its boundary decisions and rules, `epic.children` its checklist lines (done: ticked), and `epic.parked` what waits on a trigger. `item` is an issue filed since the coordinator last looked, with its state now. Which slot does the coordinator give `item` in this epic?

criteria.child: Work this epic covers and that should be done now or in order: it gets its own checklist line, slotted by dependency. A follow-up to a child, a bug in what a child shipped, or a piece split off a child is a child.
criteria.closed-in-fact: Work this epic covers that is already delivered: the item is closed, or a child's merged change already did it, so it is verified, linked and closed with evidence instead of slotted.
criteria.split: The item mixes work this epic covers with work it doesn't, so the epic's part is filed as its own issue and the rest is left out.
criteria.out of epic: Not this epic's work: another skill, service, area or epic, a record or notice with no action, or tooling around the epic rather than its work. It is said so plainly and cross-linked only where it changes a remaining step.
criteria.duplicate: The same work as an existing child or another open issue, so it is closed in favour of that one.
criteria.park: This epic's concern, but not to be done yet: it waits on a trigger (another repo, a decision, a date, an event) and goes in the parked table with that trigger.

item.title: prune_disk.py: add a recently-touched grace window — liveness alone can delete an install in progress
item.body:
Follow-up to #665. `scripts/prune_disk.py` (deployed 2026-10-16, PR #668) decides what is prunable by **liveness only**: a path survives if a running process has it as its exe, cwd, a mapped file or an open fd. That misses one case usa-wa's `scripts/disk-gc.sh` already handles with a grace window (`DISK_GC_GRACE_MINUTES=60`, see CannObserv/usa-wa#394 / #485): **a tree that is being written right now.** Nothing names it yet, because the process that will run from it hasn't started.

## The window [code]
- **npx:** a session start whose `SOCRATICODE_SPEC` differs from both pinned values writes a ~460M `~/.npm/_npx/<hash>/` before the server execs from it. A prune at that moment deletes the half-written install. The pinned specs are exempt, so this needs a re-pin or an `@latest` launch.
- **VS Code server:** a client update downloads `cli/servers/Stable-<new>/`. Until the download finishes, `lru.json` may still name the previous build first, so the new dir is neither the newest nor live, and the prune removes it. The download's own fds cover part of the window, but not the gap between extraction and the server's exec.
- **Extensions:** a dir that is mid-install is not normally in `.obsolete`, so this is low risk.

The timer fires at Sun 05:30 UTC, a quiet hour, so this is unlikely, not impossible. Nothing detects or repairs a partial tree afterwards.

## Fix
- TDD, red first in `tests/scripts/test_prune_disk.py`: add a `recently_touched(path, minutes)` keep rule using the newest mtime under the path (bounded walk). The default is 60, like disk-gc's.
- Withheld paths are logged as `withheld: recently touched`, so they show in the plan.
- An unreadable mtime keeps the path (fail safe).

Coordination: this may be superseded by a shared cohort GC owned by Provisioner (issue to follow, cross-linked here). If so, fix it there and retire `prune_disk.py`.

Each issue gets its own agent thread; this epic is checked off from the coordinating thread, which re-triages any new issues each time it is updated.

scope.text:

item.title: Adopt usa-wa 2.1.0 seat model: role_periods capacity, membership_type, D7 occupancy audit
item.body:
## Context

usa-wa is preparing one additive release, "2.1.0" (CannObserv/usa-wa#501; spec in CannObserv/usa-wa#511, `docs/specs/2026-10-17-release-2-1-0-seat-model-design.md` at `f665eac4`). It gives us what #506's seat-occupancy ratchet lacks: per-role, per-period seat capacity, and a way to tell substitutes from principals. power-map reviewed the shape on 2026-10-17 and accepted it. The review is recorded at https://github.com/CannObserv/usa-wa/issues/501#issuecomment-6227412020.

What changes upstream:

| Dataset | Today | After | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| `role_periods` | — | **1.0.0** (new, conformed, publish-only) | key `(role_key, valid_from)`; `valid_to` (the last day, **inclusive**; `null` = open), `max_holders` (`null` = no limit), `max_holders_basis` (`kind`\|`roster`). Dense across all 312 roles; periods tile with `next.valid_from = prev.valid_to + 1 day`. |
| `assignments` | 1.7.0 | **1.8.0** | appended: `start_basis`, `end_basis`, `valid_from_latest`, `valid_to_earliest`, `membership_type` (`principal`\|`substitute`\|`ex_officio`\|`acting`) |
| `persons` | 2.0.0 | **2.1.0** | appended: `name_own` |
| `roles` | 1.3.0 | 1.3.0 | unchanged: same 312 `role_key`s, same `contract_hash` |

The shared occupancy predicate (spec D7): for role R and instant t inside a period with `max_holders = m` (not null), the number of `principal` assignments with `valid_from ≤ t < coalesce(valid_to, ∞)` is ≤ m. `assignments.valid_to` is a handoff date, read as exclusive; `role_periods.valid_to` is inclusive. The two conventions differ on purpose.

## Effect on the ratchet

Prod on 2026-10-17 read `55 pairs, at baseline 55` (`power-map-seat-occupancy`, 00:01Z):
- **20** are the lawful multi-member 1889–90 Senate: LD-19 10, LD-2 3, LD-5 3, LD-18 3, LD-8 1, which is exactly C(m,2) for usa-wa's capacities 5/3/3/3/2. None of these seats goes over its m.
- **35** are producer pairs (usa-wa#489). Three of them are military substitutes: Marlo Braun (LD-20 2017), Lela Kreidler (LD-22 1991) and Jon Wyss (LD-6 2005).

When this issue ships, BASELINE goes **55 → 32**. Until then, the count stays 55 on and after usa-wa's release night.

## Work

1. **Re-pin on release night.** `persons` and `assignments` both move `contract_hash`. The puller refuses both (`contract changed within major … review it, then re-pin`, exit 1) and, per #535, every night counts as inputs-behind, so no execute opens for any dataset until the re-pin merges. We can't pre-pin, because a pin to the new hash refuses today's versions. usa-wa has committed to announcing the release date here ahead of time. Stage the re-pin PR, then fill in both values from the refusal log line on the night. The staging models select named columns, so the appended columns need no model change.
2. **Pin and stage `role_periods`.** A `sources.yml` pin, `stg_usa_wa__role_periods.sql`, and a `PM_SRC_ROLE_PERIODS` env line (the #592 `org_lineage` precedent).
3. **Land capacity.** A PM table for per-role capacity periods, a `desired_*` mart joined through the roles mapping on `role_key`, and applier support. Schema rules apply: an idempotent reconciliation `DO` block, and the parity timer.
4. **Land `membership_type`** on `role_assignments`: a column with a CHECK on the closed enum, the mapping, and applier ownership. Decide whether `/api/v1` exposes it. We don't need a `substitutes_for` edge. If usa-wa ever publishes one, #301's RA→RA relationships are where it would go.
5. **Move the audit onto D7.** Count `principal` holders at each principal's start instead of counting pairs. Capacity is `max_holders` where a period covers t, else the `role_types.occupancy` default (`single` → 1, `shared` → no limit). Keep `role_types.occupancy`: it is jurisdiction-wide, it is public on `/role-types`, and the fallback covers legacy and admin-edited rows that sit outside usa-wa's periods. Use the outer bounds only (`start_date`/`end_date`). That makes our ratchet usa-wa's *may* tier. Then lower BASELINE to the measured count, expected 32.
6. **Cross-check.** usa-wa's may-tier gate will list its span_key pairs (dbt `store_failures`). Diff that list against ours after the release. PM overlay pins, such as #639's Robinson truncation, are a legitimate cause of difference.

Out of scope: `persons.name_own` (no PM mapping decided), and the interval tiers (`valid_from_latest`/`valid_to_earliest`), which PM doesn't store.

## Done when

- [ ] The re-pin has merged, and the nightly pull and build are green on 2.1.0.
- [ ] `role_periods` is pinned, staged and landed. The capacity table on prod has a row for every published period.
- [ ] `membership_type` is landed, with exactly 3 `substitute` rows on prod.
- [ ] The audit reads capacity and principals, and BASELINE equals the measured count, expected 32.
- [ ] usa-wa#501 has a comment with our post-release count and the pair-list diff.

Related: #506, #639, #536, #535, #592, usa-wa#489, usa-wa#360.

item.title: package-lock.json root version stuck at 0.31.0 — version sync doesn't cover the lockfile
item.body:
## Symptom
`package-lock.json` declares `"version": "0.31.0"` both at its root and in `packages[""]`. `pyproject.toml`, `package.json` and `clients/python/pyproject.toml` are at 0.65.x.

## Cause
- The last commit to touch the lockfile's version was `305a4bd4` (the 0.31.0 bump).
- Later bumps edited `package.json` by hand and never regenerated the lockfile.
- `scripts/check_version_sync.sh`, the `check-version-sync` pre-commit hook, compares only `pyproject.toml`, `package.json` and `clients/python/pyproject.toml`. It never reads the lockfile, and the lockfile isn't in the hook's `files:` pattern.

## Impact
This is a cosmetic mirror drift. `npm ci` doesn't fail on a mismatched root version, but anything that reads the version from the lockfile gets a stale value.

## Options
1. Add `package-lock.json` (both version fields) to `check_version_sync.sh` and to the hook's `files:` pattern, and make the bump procedure run `npm install --package-lock-only`.
2. Drop the version from the lockfile's concern by documenting that `package.json` is the JS source of truth.

Found during the code review of #664 (finding 7, held as outside that branch's scope).

slot.instructions: `epic` is a GitHub issue that tracks a body of work through a checklist of child issues: `epic.goal` says what it covers, `epic.scope` holds its boundary decisions and rules, `epic.children` its checklist lines (done: ticked), and `epic.parked` what waits on a trigger. `item` is an issue filed since the coordinator last looked, with its state now. Which slot does the coordinator give `item` in this epic?

criteria.child: Work this epic covers and that should be done now or in order: it gets its own checklist line, slotted by dependency. A follow-up to a child, a bug in what a child shipped, or a piece split off a child is a child.
criteria.closed-in-fact: Work this epic covers that is already delivered: the item is closed, or a child's merged change already did it, so it is verified, linked and closed with evidence instead of slotted.
criteria.split: The item mixes work this epic covers with work it doesn't, so the epic's part is filed as its own issue and the rest is left out.
criteria.out of epic: Not this epic's work: another skill, service, area or epic, a record or notice with no action, or tooling around the epic rather than its work. It is said so plainly and cross-linked only where it changes a remaining step.
criteria.duplicate: The same work as an existing child or another open issue, so it is closed in favour of that one.
criteria.park: This epic's concern, but not to be done yet: it waits on a trigger (another repo, a decision, a date, an event) and goes in the parked table with that trigger.

item.title: Deeply nested JSON bodies 500: the 422 handler's jsonable_encoder recurses past the limit
item.body:
## Problem
A deeply nested JSON body gives a **500** on any route that takes a body. It happens with any leaf value, unstorable text or not.

The body parses. Pydantic rejects it, so the request should be a 422. But the 422 handler then encodes the echoed `input` with `fastapi.encoders.jsonable_encoder`, which recurses once per nesting level. It hits Python's recursion limit (1000) and raises `RecursionError`, so the error response itself crashes.

## Evidence
Measured in-process on `fix/663-unstorable-text-422` with the DB mocked. The handler shape is the same as on `main`, so this predates #663.
- Request: `POST /api/v1/orgs/batch-get` with `{"ids": [[[ … "ok" … ]]]}`.
- Depth up to 971 answers 422 (`string_type`, `loc: ["body","ids",0]`). From **972** levels it's a 500.
- The traceback ends in `fastapi/encoders.py` `jsonable_encoder`, repeated, called from `validation_error_response` (`src/api/validation.py`).
- Our own walks (`_sanitize_nonfinite`, `escape_unstorable_deep`, `find_unstorable`) recurse the same way. They run after `jsonable_encoder` or only on a pre-screen hit, so they'd fail at a similar depth once it's fixed.

## Why it matters
One small request (about 2 KB) triggers a 500, and a 500 wakes the alerting path (#663). No data is at risk.

## Options
1. **Bound the echoed `input`.** The 422 handler replaces any `input` deeper than N levels (say 32) with a placeholder before encoding, and the other walks get the same bound. This is the smallest change and keeps the standard body.
2. **Reject depth at the boundary.** `reject_unstorable_text` already sees the parsed body; a depth check there (e.g. > 64) answers a 422 `json_too_deep` before Pydantic runs. It's one rule in the place #663 put request-shape rules.
3. Both: (2) as the rule, (1) as the backstop for whatever (2) misses.

## Tests
- A depth sweep that asserts no 5xx at 10, 500, 971, 972, 5000.
- The 422 renders, the same assertion #663 makes.

item.title: write-db-secrets.sh: reproduce the per-database CONNECT allowlist (#667 follow-up)
item.body:
Follow-up to #667.

## Live since 2026-10-20 (applied by hand, as doadmin)
Each database admits only its own roles:

| Database | CONNECT |
|---|---|
| `co_pm_db_production` | `co_pm_db_production_user`, `co_pm_db_production_migrations`, `_doadmin_monitor` |
| `co_pm_db_test` | `co_pm_db_test_user`, `_doadmin_monitor` |

- `PUBLIC` no longer has CONNECT on either database.
- `doadmin` keeps CONNECT as the databases' owner.
- `_doadmin_monitor` is DO's metrics role (a member of `pg_monitor`), granted CONNECT explicitly so DO's monitoring keeps working.
- `defaultdb` is unchanged.
- Verified: `has_database_privilege` for every role, and real cross-database connections are refused (`InsufficientPrivilegeError`).

## Gap
`scripts/write-db-secrets.sh` doesn't reproduce this, so a freshly provisioned cluster (or a DR restore, #582) comes up with the PostgreSQL default, `PUBLIC` CONNECT.

## To do
- [ ] Add the `REVOKE CONNECT … FROM PUBLIC` and the per-database `GRANT CONNECT` to the writer's two grant runs (they already run with `ON_ERROR_STOP`), with a test in `tests/scripts/test_write_db_secrets.py`.
- [ ] State it in `docs/RUNBOOK_DB_TRIAGE.md` § Connection boundary → Target state.
- [ ] Consider a check in an existing daily audit that the ACLs still hold. It's unknown whether DO's control plane ever resets database ACLs.

Rollback, if ever needed: `GRANT CONNECT ON DATABASE <db> TO PUBLIC`.

item.title: Outcome log records no digests: add input_digest, output_digest, size, empty and stored to every command outcome
item.body:
## Problem

The first live shadow command (2026-10-03T18:39:37Z, `command_id` 01M41H10MS8H92WXP2V8JTH0F0) was a match. But Processor's journal couldn't show **what** it produced. The outcome record carries `command_id`, `info_source_id`, `reason`, `detail` and timings (`src/processor/consumer.py` `_log`, from `handler.Disposition`), and no digest:

```
{"message": "ack: complete", "message_id": "1791052776110-0", "attempt": 1, "reason": "complete", "command_id": "01M41H10MS8H92WXP2V8JTH0F0", "info_source_id": "01KRYSPTN633JZ8582NHHSAH9A", "read_ms": 292.5, "extract_ms": 544.7, "store_ms": 122.3, "publish_ms": 2.0, "total_ms": 962.2}
```

To answer Watcher's "what was your `output_digest`?", the coordinator had to list `gs://co-gcs-processor` and infer the answer. Nothing new had been written, so the output must have been an existing object, and only one exists. That works for one command in a near-empty bucket. It won't work during a shadow window when a mismatch needs explaining from Processor's side. Watcher records the digest from the fact, but Processor should be able to say what it published without asking Watcher.

## Proposal

Add to every outcome record whatever of these the command has:
- `input_digest`
- `output_digest`, `output_size_bytes`, `empty`, `stored` (written, or already present)
- `processor_version`
- for failures, the input the failure was about

`Disposition` grows the fields, and `_log` emits them. No change to the bus contract.

## Done when

- [ ] A `complete` record carries `input_digest`, `output_digest`, `output_size_bytes`, `empty` and whether the write was new or a no-op. A terminal failure record carries `input_digest` when the command decoded.
- [ ] Tests pin the fields for complete, empty, and a terminal failure.
- [ ] Spec §4's "Every outcome logs …" line and DEPLOYMENT.md's operating notes list the fields.
- [ ] Deployed: the unit is restarted after the merge, and a shadow command's record shows the digests.

Found during the go-live coordination with Watcher (CannObserv/watcher#325). Refs #1, epic #24.

item.title: Consumer: a re-run at the cap after the failure fact went out re-extracts instead of dead-lettering
item.body:
Found in #20's review (CR 7, PR #27). A behaviour question, not a contract bug: Watcher's first-fact-wins rule makes the outcome harmless.

**What happens.** At the cap, `Consumer._process` publishes the give-up `extraction_error` fact (#17), then dead-letters the entry. If the dead-letter is refused, transiently or not, the entry stays pending (a non-transient refusal escapes from inside `_process`'s except block, so the transient check never sees it) with `_strikes` at `max_attempts - 1`. The next reclaim runs `handle` again as attempt 3 ([consumer.py:184](https://github.com/CannObserv/processor/blob/main/src/processor/consumer.py#L184)). If that run now succeeds, Processor stores the output, publishes `processing_complete` and acks. The entry never reaches the DLQ.

This was confirmed with a throwaway test against the scratch Redis: `handle` raises three times, the first `dead_letter` raises `RedisConnectionError`, and then `handle` succeeds. Facts: `[ProcessingFailedEvent(extraction_error), ProcessingCompleteEvent]`, and the DLQ length is 0. A second throwaway test, in #20's review round 2 (CR 10), gave the same result with the first `dead_letter` raising a non-transient `ResponseError` (WRONGTYPE).

**Consequences.**
- Watcher keeps the failure (first terminal fact per `command_id`) and drops the success. The stored output is orphaned, which is harmless because outputs are write-if-absent and never deleted.
- The DLQ holds no record of the give-up, although its fact said `dead-lettered: …`.
- A dead-letter refused every time (e.g. WRONGTYPE on `content.process.dlq`) with a `handle` that keeps failing repeats attempt 3 on every reclaim, about every 11 min: it re-runs the extraction, publishes nothing new (`_fact_out`), and never leaves the PEL. Spec §4's table says the 3rd attempt dead-letters the entry; with a broken DLQ it never does. (Added in #20's review round 3, CR 16.)
- `test_a_failed_dead_letter_at_the_cap_keeps_the_count` says "still at the cap: straight to the DLQ, not attempt 1 again". The count is kept, but `handle` does run again; the test's always-raising handler hides that.

**Decide.** When an entry's fact is already out (`message_id in _fact_out`) and the cap is reached, should a re-run skip `handle` and go straight to the dead-letter? If yes: TDD, and fix the test comment. If no: correct the test comment so it doesn't say "straight to the DLQ". A restart still loses `_fact_out` either way; spec §4 (as amended by #20) documents that edge.

Refs #17, #20.

item.title: Take co-core's XML and feed extractors in step with Watcher, and re-run parity with a feed fixture
item.body:
CannObserv/cannobserv#523 adds XML and feed extractors to co-core, and routes `text/xml`, `application/xml`, `application/rss+xml` and `application/atom+xml` to them. Processor already dispatches through co-core: `src/processor/processors/extract.py` calls `extractor_for_essence(media_type)` with `extraction_config_from_spec`. So the extractors arrive with the pin.

**Ask**

1. **Take the co-core release with #523 in the same step as Watcher** (CannObserv/watcher#342), which keeps both on one version through shadow mode.
2. **Don't hand-bump `LOCAL_GENERATION`.** Its comment reserves the bump for Processor's own logic. The routing change is co-core's, and `processor_version`'s co-core half carries it.
3. **Re-run the parity corpus** against Watcher on the new version (#16). Add a feed fixture, such as Tailscale's security bulletins (`https://tailscale.com/security-bulletins/index.xml`), so the comparison covers the new essences.

Note that #523 also stops `xpath`, `regex` and `jsonpath` from silently meaning the whole page: an algorithm the dispatched extractor can't honour is refused. A live spec that relied on that fallback would now fail its extraction. Check for that in the parity run.

Refs: CannObserv/cannobserv#523, CannObserv/watcher#342, CannObserv/watcher#222, gregoryfoster/skills#313.

item.title: deploy.sh: gate a deploy on the commit's CI (status#11's CI gate)
item.body:
Deferred from #2 (the plan's step 7), following the cohort's release standard.

**What:** before building, `scripts/deploy.sh` checks that the commit's CI passed. That means the newest `push` run of `ci.yml` on `main` for exactly that commit, with every job `success`, and `lint` and `test` among them. Status shipped this as status#11, and its DEPLOYMENT § The CI gate covers the edge cases: a pending run is waited for, up to a bound; a commit with no run, a cancelled run, and a re-run each have a rule. An `--skip-ci` flag, logged, is the escape hatch.

**Why:** today a commit on `origin/main` deploys whether or not CI passed. CI is the only place the suite runs fully contained on a second kernel (Landlock ABI 7).

**Notes:** processor is public, so the Actions API answers without a token, and there's no credential to manage. Reuse Status's tested logic rather than re-deriving it, which ties in with the cohort-skill feedback (plan, point 11).

item.body:
Deferred from #2 (the plan's step 7), following the cohort's release standard.

**What:** a periodic check that `/srv/processor/live/REVISION` has no runtime diff from `origin/main`, over `src/`, `deploy/`, `scripts/deploy.sh`, `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock`. It alerts once code has waited past a threshold since its push. Status shipped this as status#12: an hourly timer plus a healthchecks.io check.

**Why:** pushed is not deployed. Since #2, a merge changes nothing that runs until `scripts/deploy.sh`, and nothing reports a merge that was never deployed.

**Open:** whether processor gets a healthchecks.io check like Status's or reports through the broker probe. That is the cohort's decision (broker#22, goal 4).

item.title: JSON: take co-core's JsonExtractor (cannobserv#354) and add a jsonpath parity fixture
item.body:
**Moved from CannObserv/watcher#212**, which closes as superseded. JSON extraction is no longer Watcher's concern.

## The problem (verified on co-core 0.10.0, still true on 0.19.7's table)

`application/json` isn't in co-core's `EXTRACTOR_BY_ESSENCE`, so it falls back to `HtmlExtractor`. That extractor ignores a `jsonpath` spec and fingerprints the **whole document**:

```python
raw = b'{"items": [{"title": "Rule 5", "status": "active"}]}'
HtmlExtractor().extract(raw, {"algorithm": "jsonpath", "selector": "$.items[*].title"})
# -> one chunk, text = the entire document. Selector ignored.
```

The chunks aren't empty, so the empty-extraction guard never trips. Any unrelated field, such as a timestamp or a counter, then reads as a change. Archiver's schema allows `{json: jsonpath}`, so a JSON source can legitimately carry such a spec.

## Why it lands here

- **The extractor** is CannObserv/cannobserv#354.
- **Essence resolution** (whether `application/*+json` joins the json family) is co-core's `resolve_dispatch_essence`. Watcher only re-exports it.
- **Dispatch:** Watcher reads co-core's table since CannObserv/watcher#342 Ask 1. After CannObserv/watcher#326's flip, Watcher doesn't extract at all, so Processor's `extractor_for_essence` is the only dispatcher.

## Ask (when CannObserv/cannobserv#354 releases)

- [ ] Take that co-core release **in lockstep with Watcher** (as with CannObserv/processor#29). It may be the same bump.
- [ ] Add a JSON fixture with a `jsonpath` spec to the parity corpus, and assert that it narrows the canonical text to the selected nodes.
- [ ] Add a `+json` vendor-type fixture if co-core maps that family.

**Exposure today: none.** All 4 production items are `text/html`, measured 2026-10-05 on CannObserv/watcher#342.

Refs: CannObserv/cannobserv#354, CannObserv/watcher#212, CannObserv/watcher#342.

item.title: Liveness check-in for processor run (co-status monitor co-processor-live)
item.body:
Suggested by CannObserv/status#24, where the operator decided on 2026-10-07: **yes to a liveness monitor, created once this issue settles its design.** Raised in this repo's #35 hand-off as out of scope there.

## Why

Since 2026-10-06T21:35Z (CannObserv/watcher#326), Processor's output decides Watcher's production results. A quiet Processor shows up only in Watcher's own health, and nothing alerts the operator directly. `co-processor-drift` (status#24) doesn't cover it: its `missing` means the drift check isn't reporting, not that `processor run` has stopped consuming.

## What co-status provides

A monitor `co-processor-live` on the existing `co-processor` tenant, with the **same key** as the drift check (`/etc/processor/status-checkin.key`). It uses the same contract: `POST http://status:9000/api/v1/monitors/{id}/checkin`, with `{"status": "ok"|"alert", "variables": {...}}` and `X-API-Key`. Alerts go to the same Mailgun + Slack pair. Silence past interval + grace goes `missing`, then `recovered` on the next check-in.

co-status creates the monitor once the table below is filled in, and posts its id here.

## To decide here

| Field | Question |
|---|---|
| `interval_seconds` | N: how often `processor run` checks in |
| `grace_seconds` | How much silence is normal: restarts, deploys (`scripts/deploy.sh` restarts the unit), slow batches |
| `renotify_seconds` | Daily, as the drift monitor? |
| `title_template` / `body_template` | Only if `alert` is ever sent; they render `variables` |
| variables | What each check-in carries (opaque to co-status; every check-in should carry all the template uses) |

## Design questions

1. **What does a check-in prove?** If it fires only after work was done, an empty queue reads as an outage, a false alarm. A check-in from the consume loop on a timer, whether or not there was work, proves the loop is alive. Which does "live" mean for Processor?
2. **`ok` only, or `alert` too?** E.g. consuming but failing every item. Each `alert` check-in sends its own report, with no dedupe on co-status's side, so an `alert` every N minutes is one notification every N minutes.
3. **A co-status outage must not affect Processor** (#35's trap 4). The drift check stays out of `processor run`'s path. A liveness check-in can't, so it needs a short timeout, must never block or slow consumption, and never retries in a loop. A failed check-in logs and moves on.
4. **Deploys:** a restart longer than the grace pages. Size the grace for it, or accept the page.

## Done when

- `processor run` checks in on its cadence, and a stubbed slow or failing co-status provably doesn't stall consumption (tests).
- The table above is posted on CannObserv/status#24, so co-status can create the monitor.
- Live: the monitor goes `pending` → `ok`. Stopping `processor.service` past the grace sends "has stopped reporting", and starting it sends "has recovered", confirmed by the operator.

scope.text:
The operator gave no rule this time. The coordinator applied the following; challenge it here.

1. **Time windows first.** The window before shadow closes when Watcher flips `WATCHER_EXTRACT_MODE=shadow`. Work that is cheapest with the bus empty goes in it.

4. **Then agent tooling**, which has no effect on production.
5. **Blocked items stay parked**, each with a re-entry test.

item.title: Flaky: test_an_entry_that_raises_does_not_strand_the_ones_behind_it (0.6 s sleep against 500 ms idle), and since #34 a flake blocks deploys
item.body:
Found in #35's full runs (PR #38): `tests/test_consumer.py::test_an_entry_that_raises_does_not_strand_the_ones_behind_it` failed once in a full run. It passes 5/5 alone and with the modules before it, and the failure predates #38.

**Cause (suspected):** wall-clock timing. The test sleeps `asyncio.sleep(0.6)` (around line 409) against `reclaim_min_idle_ms=500` (line 425), a 100 ms margin, under a loaded runner or a slow scratch Redis.

**Why it matters now:** since #34, `scripts/deploy.sh` refuses any commit whose `main` push run isn't green. A flake on a push run blocks the deploy until someone re-runs CI. Since watcher#326's switch (2026-10-06T21:35Z), a blocked deploy can be a blocked production fix.

**Done when:**
- The test no longer depends on a wall-clock margin: it advances idle time deterministically (or waits on the condition with a bound), and still proves that one claim per entry keeps the tail from stranding (the comment at lines 401–403).
- A loop of the file (e.g. 50 runs) passes on `co-processor` and in CI.
- A sweep of `tests/` for other `sleep`-against-threshold margins under ~2×, each fixed or listed.

Refs #34, #35 (PR #38's body), #28.

item.title: CI pulls redis:7.0.15 from Docker Hub unauthenticated; since #34 a Hub outage or rate limit blocks deploys
item.body:
From #39's closing comment (2026-10-09): CI's Redis service container is pulled from Docker Hub without credentials. On 2026-10-09 that failed twice in one day, first on Hub's anonymous pull rate limit and then during the incident "Hub Registry Authenticated Actions Failing". #39 needed re-runs before it could merge, and `main`'s push run gated the deploy.

**Why it matters:** since #34, `scripts/deploy.sh` deploys only a commit whose `main` push run is green. A Docker Hub problem therefore blocks deploys, including a production fix (Processor has decided Watcher's results since watcher#326). The escape is `--skip-ci`, which deploys untested.

**Options (to weigh, not decided):**
- Install `redis-server` 7.0.15 from apt on the runner, pinned to the broker's version. Check that the runner's distro has a 7.0.x build, since #8 chose 7.0.15 over 7.2 for `CLIENT SETINFO`.
- Pull the image from a mirror: `mirror.gcr.io/library/redis:7.0.15` (Google's Hub mirror) or GHCR.
- Authenticate the pull with a Docker Hub token: a secret to manage.
- Add a retry around the service start (helps rate limits, not outages).

**Done when:** CI's Redis no longer depends on anonymous Docker Hub pulls (or the choice to keep it is recorded with its reason). The suite still runs against the broker's Redis version, and CI stays green.

Refs #34, #39, #8.

item.title: test_liveness flakes: a check-in thread can still be alive just after its tick returns
item.body:
Follow-up to #39, found on #44's first CI run (38008871788, 2026-10-10).

**Symptom:** `tests/test_liveness.py::test_ok_is_logged_on_the_first_and_after_a_failure_only` failed with `assert [20, 20] == [20, 20, 20]`. The captured log ends:

```
INFO     liveness check-in
WARNING  consume loop stale; not checking in
WARNING  previous check-in still in flight; skipping this tick
```

It passed on re-run and has passed locally.

**Cause:** `Heartbeat._in_thread`'s thread hands its result to the loop with `loop.call_soon_threadsafe(settle, …)` and then returns. `settle` can run, and the tick can finish, before that thread has exited, so `self._thread.is_alive()` stays true for a moment. The test's 5th tick (stale) returns without awaiting anything. That lets the 6th tick run right after the 4th tick's check-in, and it sees the 4th tick's thread still alive and skips (`src/processor/liveness.py`, the `is_alive()` check in `tick`).

**Impact:** test-only in practice. At `interval_s=300` a finished thread has long since exited, and a falsely skipped tick would be absorbed by the monitor's 900 s grace anyway. But a red `main` push run blocks `scripts/deploy.sh` (#34), so a flake in the suite is a deploy hazard (#43 had the same problem with image pulls).

**Fix options (to weigh):**
- Code: "in flight" means the post hasn't returned yet, not that the thread is alive. For example, `target` clears a flag (or `self._thread`) before it calls `call_soon_threadsafe`. A timed-out post still counts as in flight, so trap 1 of #39 (no piled-up threads) still holds.
- Test-only: wait for the previous thread to finish before the next tick. This hides the race rather than removing it.

**Done when:** a test reproduces the race deterministically (for example, a `post` that doesn't let its thread exit until the loop has seen the result), the fix makes it pass, and the existing in-flight/timeout tests still pass.

Refs #39, #44.

item.title: Close out the cutover: spec §6 step 5 done, and re-decide D5 (lockstep pin, Watcher-generated goldens) now that Watcher doesn't extract
item.body:
**Trigger:** CannObserv/watcher#350 closed 2026-10-10T01:52Z (`207e9be..bb1b1f9`). Watcher deleted its local extraction, the `WATCHER_EXTRACT_MODE` variable, the shadow leg, and its `co-core[extract]` extra. Since watcher#326 (switch 2026-10-06T21:35:24Z; soak passed 2026-10-09), Processor is the only extractor.

**Now stale in this repo:**
- **Spec §6, cutover order step 5:** "Watcher #326 switches on zero mismatches…". It happened; mark it done, with links (#326's gate and soak verdicts, #350).
- **#1** (the umbrella) closes on that, per epic #24's re-entry test.
- **Spec D5 (line 87) and AGENTS.md line 21:** "co-core pinned exactly, matched to Watcher … lockstep". The reason for lockstep was the shadow comparison (both sides extracting must agree). With no Watcher extractor, what does the pin need to match? Watcher still uses co-core for contracts (`content.process` / `content.derived` models, `resolve_dispatch_essence`, `canonical_text` semantics), so a contract-level coordination may remain while the extractor-level lockstep doesn't.
- **AGENTS.md line 55, `scripts/gen_parity_goldens.py`:** "Parity goldens come from Watcher's own code, never from Processor's." Watcher's extraction code no longer exists on its `main`. Options to weigh:
  - (a) freeze the current goldens as the record of the v1 contract, and at a co-core bump regenerate them from **co-core directly** (not from Processor's wrapper), with every changed digest listed in the bump note (a deliberate re-baseline; Watcher's Option A re-baselines silently on a `processor_version` change);
  - (b) keep generating from Watcher's last extracting commit, pinned (a historical oracle that can't follow a bump);
  - (c) something else.
- **The real corpus** (`tests/fixtures/parity/real/`, #16) is Watcher's export verbatim, and stays as is.

**Affects:** #29 (XML/feed extractors) and #37 (JSON extractor). Both say "in lockstep with Watcher", and their parity steps assume Watcher-generated goldens. Their re-entry tests get rewritten from this decision.

**Decide with:** the operator. Optionally ask Watcher (a drafted, approved comment) whether it still needs advance notice of a co-core bump that moves `processor_version` (it re-baselines), and of one that changes the contract models.

**Done when:** spec §6 step 5 is marked done; D5 and AGENTS.md (lines 21 and 55) state the post-#350 rule; `gen_parity_goldens.py`'s role is settled (and its docstring updated or retired); #29 and #37 have their re-entry tests restated; #1 is closed with links.

Refs #1, #29, #37, epic #24, CannObserv/watcher#326, CannObserv/watcher#350.

item.title: Adopt the coordinating-epics skill for #24
item.body:
`coordinating-epics` v1 shipped in gregoryfoster/skills (gregoryfoster/skills#348, `fef0611`). It packages the protocol #24's coordinator has run by hand, and several of its rules came from #24's own findings (F101, F122, F129, F134, and parking-lot mode from F135, F137 and F138). This issue moves #24 onto it.

**What v1 brings**
- `epic-edit.sh`: one guarded call per body edit. It refuses foreign edits against a saved baseline (a tick you have verified passes with `--accept-ticks`), anchors each operation by ref, derives checkbox counts, lints refs, placeholders and secrets, compare-and-swaps before the PATCH, and reads the body back.
- `scan.sh`: the three re-scan cursors (number watermark, updated-since, and the commit range attributed to children), the epic's own new comments, and cross-repo ref states, as JSON.
- `assets/epic-template.md`: the header cursor lines both scripts read.

#24 is in parking-lot mode, with #21 and #37 parked. The skill's `close-out.md` ("Parking-lot mode") covers that: a check-in runs only on a trigger, and `scan.sh` is its first step.

**Steps**
1. **Vendor it.** `skills-vendor/gregoryfoster-skills` is at `5ff7a82`, older than the skill. Bump it to `fef0611` or later, then symlink `skills/coordinating-epics` and `.claude/skills/coordinating-epics` (managing-skills, Step 2/2b). The auto-refresh hook bumps the pointer but creates no symlinks.
2. **Adopt at the next triggered check-in, as that check-in's one write** (SKILL.md, "Adopt an epic that exists"). Run `scan.sh --repo CannObserv/processor --epic 24 --watermark 51 --from-sha <last verified SHA>`; its `since` comes from the header's `Last check-in`. Then make one `epic-edit.sh --repo CannObserv/processor --epic 24 --adopt-live --scan <report> --ops <file>` call, dry-run first, with `header` ops for `Last check-in` (`{checked}`), `Last probe`, `Last issue seen` (`{last_seen}`) and `Last verified SHA`.
3. **After that,** every body edit goes through `epic-edit.sh`, and each check-in starts with `scan.sh`.

**What a dry run on today's body found** (a copy of the body, run against the fake `gh` in the skill's tests; nothing was written):
- **The header holds three fields in one paragraph,** each with a note in parentheses. A `header` op on `Last check-in` rewrites that whole line, so `Last probe` and the watermark need their own `header` ops in the same call, and the notes belong in that call's log line. The call applies cleanly.
- **`Last number seen` becomes `Last issue seen`.** That is the name `scan.sh` reads; until then it finds no watermark.
- **`--lint-all` would flag 33 lines,** nearly all short refs such as `watcher#326`, `broker#85` and `cannobserv#536`, which GitHub does not link. Rewriting 33 lines in the adoption call is a large edit, so the steps above leave `--lint-all` out. Each line is then linted the first time it changes, and must be fixed then (check-in.md, "A lint refusal on a line you only ticked"). Add `--lint-all` if you'd rather fix them all at once.

**Known limits in v1:** CI by job is still checked by hand (gregoryfoster/skills#394), and comments are not linted before posting (gregoryfoster/skills#395).

**When the run ends:** journal it in the skill's process log. The skill is vendored here, so draft the entry in this repo and file it upstream as an issue on gregoryfoster/skills ("Adding an entry" in `references/process-log.md`).

item.title: Follow the broker to Valkey 7.2 (CannObserv/broker#85): CI image, scratch server, 7.0.15-only claims
item.body:
**Parked until CannObserv/broker#85's post-window notice.** The broker decided on 2026-10-15 to move from Redis 7.0.15 to **Valkey 7.2.13** (Ubuntu `7.2.13+dfsg1-0ubuntu0.1`). The window is gated on CannObserv/broker#95 closing and isn't scheduled yet. The decision record is in [broker#85's comment of 2026-10-15T23:03Z](https://github.com/CannObserv/broker/issues/85). Filed by burn-down epic #24's coordinator, 2026-10-16.

## Processor's part, from the decision's notice list

1. **The CI service image.** It is `mirror.gcr.io/library/redis:7.0.15` today (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:94`, and `BROKER_REDIS` in `tests/test_ci.py:16`). The notice names `valkey/valkey:7.2.13` and says there is **no** `library/valkey`, so `mirror.gcr.io/library/...` doesn't carry over. `mirror.gcr.io` serves it as of 2026-10-15 `[stated: broker#85]`. Keep #43's rule: never pull anonymously from Docker Hub, so the image is `mirror.gcr.io/valkey/valkey:7.2.13`. Check this resolves before relying on it.
   - CI waits on `redis-cli ping` (#43). Check whether the valkey image ships `redis-cli` or only `valkey-cli` `[unknown]`.
   - The comments in `ci.yml` (lines 79–90) and `tests/test_ci.py:11-12` give the reason as "not 7.2: redis-py sends CLIENT SETINFO there, which the broker's ACL cannot grant". After the window, the broker grants it, so rewrite those comments rather than delete them.
2. **The scratch `redis-server` on co-processor** (`localhost:6379`, tests and smoke runs only; 7.0.15 today).
   - **Trap, from broker#85's package survey `[stated]`:** `valkey-server` **Conflicts/Replaces** `redis-server`. When `/var/lib/redis` exists, its postinst copies the config with a blanket `s#redis#valkey#g`, moves `/var/lib/redis` to `/var/lib/redis-old`, and touches `/etc/valkey/REDIS_MIGRATION`, which keeps the unit from starting.
   - The scratch server holds no data worth keeping. So purge `redis-server` first, then install `valkey-server` clean, then check that `valkey-server.service` is active on `localhost:6379`.
   - This is a host step for the operator: name the exact commands on this issue.
3. **Re-verify the claims checked only on 7.0.15:** `OOM command not allowed` and `NOPERM` as transient `ResponseError`s (spec §4), `XAUTOCLAIM` reclaim, and the ACL behaviour the integration tests exercise. Run the integration suite against the new scratch server, `uv run pytest -m integration`.
4. **Docs:** AGENTS.md's Infrastructure table (the CI row, "redis:7.0.15 … the next is broker#85's call"), DEPLOYMENT.md where it names the engine, and the spec where it states the broker's version.

## The broker's pre-window ask (already answered by measurement, not yet posted)

The broker asks each consumer whether its client sends `CLIENT SETINFO`. **Processor's does** `[traced from source, 2026-10-16]`:
- `src/processor/consumer.py:78` builds the client with `Redis.from_url(...)` and no `driver_info`;
- in redis-py 7.4.1 (the locked version), `driver_info` defaults to a sentinel that sends `CLIENT SETINFO`, and only an explicit `None` disables it.

So `processor` needs `+client|setinfo` in the broker's P4, in the window, and Processor needs no code change for it. A reply on broker#85 needs the operator's approval (cross-repo policy). It is drafted on epic #24.

## Ordering hazard

The new grant and the engine land in the same broker window. Until then, a 7.0 aclfile must never carry `+client|setinfo` (7.0 refuses the whole file), so nothing on Processor's side moves first. CI on 7.2 before the window would test against an engine production doesn't run yet. **Do steps 1–4 after the notice, not before.**

**Re-entry:** the broker's post-window notice on broker#85, saying Valkey 7.2.13 is live.

**Done when:**
- CI runs against the valkey image, and `BROKER_REDIS`'s pin test passes;
- the scratch server is Valkey 7.2.13 and `pytest -m integration` passes against it;
- the 7.0.15-only claims are re-verified, or the bump note lists them as moved;
- the docs name the new engine;
- live: Processor's first commands after the broker's window complete with `NRestarts=0`, and the broker's `ACL LOG` shows no `client|setinfo` row for `processor` (the broker reads that).

No deploy unless `src/` changes. Nothing here changes Processor's runtime, unless a re-verification fails.

slot.instructions: `epic` is a GitHub issue that tracks a body of work through a checklist of child issues: `epic.goal` says what it covers, `epic.scope` holds its boundary decisions and rules, `epic.children` its checklist lines (done: ticked), and `epic.parked` what waits on a trigger. `item` is an issue filed since the coordinator last looked, with its state now. Which slot does the coordinator give `item` in this epic?

criteria.child: Work this epic covers and that should be done now or in order: it gets its own checklist line, slotted by dependency. A follow-up to a child, a bug in what a child shipped, or a piece split off a child is a child.
criteria.closed-in-fact: Work this epic covers that is already delivered: the item is closed, or a child's merged change already did it, so it is verified, linked and closed with evidence instead of slotted.
criteria.split: The item mixes work this epic covers with work it doesn't, so the epic's part is filed as its own issue and the rest is left out.
criteria.out of epic: Not this epic's work: another skill, service, area or epic, a record or notice with no action, or tooling around the epic rather than its work. It is said so plainly and cross-linked only where it changes a remaining step.
criteria.duplicate: The same work as an existing child or another open issue, so it is closed in favour of that one.
criteria.park: This epic's concern, but not to be done yet: it waits on a trigger (another repo, a decision, a date, an event) and goes in the parked table with that trigger.

item.title: Co-core bump rule: resolve_dispatch_essence is notice, not coordination
item.body:
## Problem

The co-core bump rule names `resolve_dispatch_essence` as part of the contract. A change to the contract needs coordination with Watcher first, not just notice. But Processor never calls `resolve_dispatch_essence`: `grep -rn resolve_dispatch_essence src/` returns nothing on `540975e`. Watcher resolves the essence on its own co-core pin and puts it on the command. Processor dispatches whatever essence arrives and never re-resolves it (spec §3, cannobserv#486 D1).

So a change to `resolve_dispatch_essence` can't change Processor's behaviour on its own, and the rule asks for coordination it doesn't need. It has happened twice:
- **#29 (0.32.0):** `.xml` / `.rss` / `.atom` → the XML essences. Coordinated on CannObserv/watcher#366, and Watcher's acknowledgement gated the deploy. The spec's own §5 reasoning says either order was safe.
- **#37 (0.38.0):** `.json` → `application/json`. Treated as notice, with the either-order reasoning in the bump note (https://github.com/CannObserv/processor/issues/37#issuecomment-6283411824). That contradicts the rule as written.

The argument both times:
- An old Watcher keeps sending the ambiguous essence, which reaches the same extractor as before.
- A new Watcher's resolved essence reaches the old extractor on an old Processor, and the new one on a new Processor.
- The moved-digest list in the notice already covers what Watcher sees when the dispatch map changes for an essence Watcher sends today.

## Where the rule is stated

- `AGENTS.md:21`: "coordinated with Watcher only if it changes the contract: … or `resolve_dispatch_essence`"
- `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md:461`, "Bumping co-core" step 4
- the spec: D5 (`:134`) and §5 (`:507-509`)

## Proposal

1. Drop `resolve_dispatch_essence` from the contract list in all four places. The contract becomes the `content.process` / `content.derived` models and `canonical_text` semantics.
2. Say why, once, in §5. Essence resolution is the issuer's, on its own pin, and Processor never re-resolves. So a change to it is **notice**, carrying the either-order reasoning and the moved digests. It is never coordination.
3. **Guard the premise with a test,** so the rule can't silently go stale. Assert that nothing under `src/processor/` imports or names `resolve_dispatch_essence` / `extension_media_type`, the same way `gen_parity_goldens.py`'s import test works. If Processor ever starts resolving essences itself, the test fails, and the rule has to come back with it.
4. **Amend the spec** (an amendment entry), noting that #29's coordination was more than the rule needed. The history stays as written.

## Out of scope

- Watcher's own pin and its handling of the tiebreak.
- Changes to `EXTRACTOR_BY_ESSENCE`. Those already reach Watcher as moved digests in the notice, which stays required on every bump.

Found while shipping #37.

item.title: Drift check-ins carry no metadata.fault: a change of kind inside one fault waits for the daily reminder
item.body:
**Suggested by co-status (CannObserv/status#51), found by broker-agent while building CannObserv/broker#110.**

## What

`post_checkin` sends `{"status", "variables"}` and never `metadata`, so the drift check's `alert`s carry no `metadata.fault`. [code: `src/processor/checkin.py:68` @ `540975e`]

Since CannObserv/status#28, co-status groups a run of `alert` check-ins into one fault. A change of `metadata.fault` opens a new fault and reports **at once**. Without the key, every `alert` carries `null` alike, so co-status can't tell one fault from the next. [code: CannObserv/status `src/core/monitors.py` `opens_fault` / `report_due` @ `16102ea`]

## Effect on `co-processor-drift`

- **Still works:** a fault opens and reports, reminds once a day (`renotify_seconds` 86400), and *has cleared* on the next `ok`. Nothing goes silent.
- **Doesn't work:** a change of `kind` inside one fault, say `lag` → `off_main` or `unstamped`, is **not reported until the next reminder**, up to about 23.5 h later. The most urgent verdicts (`off_main`, `unstamped`) are the ones that can be held back this way.
- A `--test-alert` sent while a real fault is open doesn't report either.

[measured, read-only on co-status, 2026-10-20] `co-processor-drift` (`01M4BHMGGTXWQ16J3G5WWDQRYQ`) has one `alert` on record, 2026-10-07T16:16:43Z, which predates #28. `fault_key` is `null` and the monitor is `ok`, so nothing has been lost so far.

## Suggested fix

Send `"metadata": {"fault": kind}` on every `alert`, and no `metadata` on an `ok`. That is the contract `co-archiver-drift` and `co-broker-drift` follow (CannObserv/status#32, #51). For example, give `post_checkin` an optional `metadata: dict[str, str] | None` and have the drift command pass `{"fault": verdict.kind}` when `status == "alert"`. Broker's tests for the same contract, as models: `tests/test_drift.py::TestVerdict::test_every_alert_s_fault_is_its_kind` and `::test_an_ok_carries_no_metadata` (CannObserv/broker#110).

`metadata.fault` is compared, never interpreted: any stable string per fault works. No change is needed on co-status's side, or to the monitor row.

The liveness check (`src/processor/liveness.py`) uses the same `post_checkin`. If it ever sends an `alert` with more than one cause, the same applies there.

item.title: Replace the brainstorming override with a vendor symlink and an AGENTS.md preference
item.body:
## Problem

`skills/brainstorming` is a committed copy of `obra-superpowers/brainstorming`, kept only to change one path: upstream's `docs/superpowers/specs/` becomes `docs/specs/` (docs/SKILLS.md § Overrides). Since the 2026-10-21 submodule bump, `.skills/doctor.sh` warns that the override has fallen behind:

- **Upstream has been rewritten.** The override was synced from v6.4.2 (`8ca22db`); the vendor is now at v7.0.0+ (`b739a8a`). `SKILL.md` was rewritten end to end, so re-syncing means reapplying the path change to a new document, not merging a small diff.
- **The override now hides upstream files.** Upstream dropped `spec-document-reviewer-prompt.md` and added `builder-check-prompt.md`, which v7's `SKILL.md` dispatches ("Builder check"). The override still ships the old prompt and doesn't link the new one. Until it's re-synced, our copy runs v6.4.2's process.
- **The override isn't needed any more.** v7's `SKILL.md` says where the design doc goes (`docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md`), then: "Your human partner's preferences override both." A stated preference in `AGENTS.md` does what the fork does, and needs no re-sync.

## Proposal

1. Replace `skills/brainstorming/` with a vendor symlink, `../skills-vendor/obra-superpowers/skills/brainstorming`, like the other 11 superpowers skills. `.claude/skills/brainstorming` already points at `../../skills/brainstorming`, so it needs no change.
2. Add a short `AGENTS.md` section on brainstorming preferences. At minimum:
   - Design docs go in `docs/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<issue>-<slug>.md`, not `docs/superpowers/specs/`.
   - Plans go in `docs/plans/`, by gregoryfoster's `writing-plans`, as now (docs/SKILLS.md:43).
   - Any other preference the current override or docs/SKILLS.md implies. Check v7's flow, including the builder check, against the spec-first practice here.
3. docs/SKILLS.md: remove the `brainstorming` row from § Overrides (and the section, if it ends up empty), change line 39's "11 + override" to 12 links, and update the `AGENTS.md` Detail Docs line that mentions "the brainstorming override".
4. Tests and comments that name the override:
   - `tests/test_skills.py` keeps passing. `test_skills_are_vendor_links_or_declared_overrides` and `test_override_links_resolve` then have no overrides to check. Keep them, so a future override is still held to the rule.
   - `tests/test_socraticode_config.py:74`'s comment calls `skills/brainstorming` "an upstream copy with one path changed": update it.
   - `tests/test_drift.py:115` uses `skills/brainstorming` only as a non-runtime path. Check that it still reads right.

## Out of scope

- Other cohort repos that use the same Observo pattern. Note it as a cross-repo finding (for the operator to route), if useful.
- Changes to upstream superpowers.

## Done when

- `skills/brainstorming` is a symlink, and `bash .skills/doctor.sh` no longer reports override drift.
- `AGENTS.md` states the preferences, and docs/SKILLS.md has no stale override text.
- The full suite and ruff pass. No deploy: `skills/`, `docs/` and `AGENTS.md` aren't runtime.

Found in the review of #60 (CR round 1, #61).

slot.instructions: `epic` is a GitHub issue that tracks a body of work through a checklist of child issues: `epic.goal` says what it covers, `epic.scope` holds its boundary decisions and rules, `epic.children` its checklist lines (done: ticked), and `epic.parked` what waits on a trigger. `item` is an issue filed since the coordinator last looked, with its state now. Which slot does the coordinator give `item` in this epic?

criteria.child: Work this epic covers and that should be done now or in order: it gets its own checklist line, slotted by dependency. A follow-up to a child, a bug in what a child shipped, or a piece split off a child is a child.
criteria.closed-in-fact: Work this epic covers that is already delivered: the item is closed, or a child's merged change already did it, so it is verified, linked and closed with evidence instead of slotted.
criteria.split: The item mixes work this epic covers with work it doesn't, so the epic's part is filed as its own issue and the rest is left out.
criteria.out of epic: Not this epic's work: another skill, service, area or epic, a record or notice with no action, or tooling around the epic rather than its work. It is said so plainly and cross-linked only where it changes a remaining step.
criteria.duplicate: The same work as an existing child or another open issue, so it is closed in favour of that one.
criteria.park: This epic's concern, but not to be done yet: it waits on a trigger (another repo, a decision, a date, an event) and goes in the parked table with that trigger.
