item.title: Tailscale 1.104.2 for TS-2026-013 (eMudhra intermediates)
item.body:
**Tailscale security bulletin [TS-2026-013](https://tailscale.com/security-bulletins/#ts-2026-013)** (published 2026-10-21; tracked on CannObserv/provisioner#77). The private keys for eight eMudhra TLS intermediates leaked. Tailscale's client trusts the OS root store, so anyone holding one of those keys could pass as a TLS site "with no warning". **The fix is Tailscale v1.104.2 or later.** It's built with Go 1.27.3, which distrusts those intermediates even when they're still in the system store. No workaround is given. Mesh traffic (WireGuard, node keys) isn't affected.

**The same compromise, beyond Tailscale:** exe.dev's advisory (https://exe.dev/security/emudhra-compromise, 2026-10-20) comes with a remediation command, `ssh exe.dev remediate-emudhra-compromise`, run from the Mac. It fixes the system store and the tools that bundle their own roots (uv, claude, opencode, headless-shell). It doesn't reach a Python venv's **certifi**, which httpx and requests use instead of the system store. On `co-provisioner` that certifi still trusted the emSign chain afterwards (CannObserv/provisioner#79; fix at certifi ≥ 2026.10.19, per CannObserv/address-validator#343). A process started before the fix keeps the old trust until it restarts. This upgrade restarts `tailscaled`.

## For this host

- **The canary.** co-processor goes first. Its result clears the service nodes to go.
- co-processor is a bus participant: afterwards, check its consumer reconnected, and ask broker for a bus-health reading.
- **No `.skills/patching-hosts` knob** in this repo (read 2026-10-22), so this is a hand run of `tailscale` alone, provisioner#60's shape:
  ```bash
  tailscale version --daemon                       # before
  sudo apt-get update
  apt-get install -s --only-upgrade tailscale=1.104.2   # expect: tailscale alone
  sudo NEEDRESTART_MODE=l apt-get install --only-upgrade tailscale=1.104.2 </dev/null
  tailscale version --daemon; systemctl show tailscaled -p MainPID,ActiveEnterTimestamp
  ```
  The version is pinned and `-y` is left out, so apt aborts rather than doing more than the simulation showed.

## What to expect (measured on `co-provisioner`, provisioner#60 and #77)

- The package's postinst restarts `tailscaled`. The tailnet was down for about 2 s: 2.0 s for 1.102.4 → 1.104.1, and 2.2 s for 1.104.1 → 1.104.2.

- `NEEDRESTART_MODE=l` keeps needrestart from restarting anything else. PID1's own lines may be missing from the journal (provisioner#62), so prove the restart from `systemctl show tailscaled -p MainPID,ActiveEnterTimestamp`.

- [ ] `tailscale version --daemon` reports 1.104.2 or later for client and daemon, and Go 1.27.3 or later.
- [ ] The host's health checks pass afterwards.
- [ ] A comment on CannObserv/provisioner#77 gives the version before and after and the UTC time. That issue's closing table is built from them.

The order across the cohort is in provisioner#77: co-processor first, as the canary; then each service node, each checked with the broker's bus-health probe; co-broker last.

item.title: certifi ≥ 2026.10.19: the live venv still trusts the eMudhra-compromised emSign G3 chain
item.body:
**Filed by the burn-down epic #24's coordinator, 2026-10-22, while assessing #65.** This is the same eMudhra compromise, but outside Tailscale: Processor's own venv still trusts the compromised chain.

## Measured on `co-processor`, 2026-10-22T23:2xZ

- **The system store is fixed.** exe.dev's remediation ran here (apt `libnss3-tools` at 2026-10-22 18:14:00; `ca-certificates` `20260816ubuntu0.24.04.1`). System `curl` **rejects** the advisory's test host `https://dv-g3b-noct-emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com/` (exit 60, `ssl_verify_result=20`).
- **The live service's venv doesn't use the system store.** `/srv/processor/live/.venv` has **certifi 2026.07.22** (`uv.lock:45-46`), whose bundle still holds `emSign ECC Root CA - G3`. `requests.get` on the same host from that venv returns **HTTP 200: it trusts the chain.**
- **certifi 2026.10.19** (the latest on PyPI) drops `emSign ECC Root CA - G3`. Its `cacert.pem` has 0 matches. It keeps emSign G1 and C3, which aren't in the compromised chains. This matches CannObserv/address-validator#343 (PYSEC-2026-4320) and CannObserv/provisioner#79, where the same certifi in co-provisioner's live venv was measured trusting the chain.

## Exposure

These TLS clients take certifi's bundle, not the system store:
- **GCS** (`google-cloud-storage` / `google-auth` over `requests`): input reads from `gs://co-gcs-blobs` and writes to `gs://co-gcs-processor`.
- **GitHub** (`processor.drift`, `requests`): the hourly drift check's `api.github.com` calls.

Status's check-ins are plain HTTP on the tailnet (`http://status:9000`), so certifi doesn't apply to them. The extraction child has no sockets at all (seccomp), so it is unaffected. An attack needs a network position between this VM and Google or GitHub, plus one of the leaked intermediate keys.

## Ask

1. Move certifi to `>=2026.10.19` in `uv.lock`, for example with `uv lock --upgrade-package certifi`. The diff should move certifi alone. **Never `uv lock --upgrade`:** co-core's pin must not move.
2. **A guard test,** so a later lock can't bring the root back: certifi's bundle has no `emSign ECC Root CA - G3`, and certifi is at least 2026.10.19.
3. Deploy (`uv.lock` is a deploy path). The restart is what picks up the new bundle, since a running process keeps its old trust.
4. **Live check:** from `/srv/processor/live/.venv`, `requests.get('https://dv-g3b-noct-emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com/')` must raise `SSLError`. Then the next GCS read/write and the next drift run (`ok`/202) still succeed.

## Out of scope

- Tailscale (#65).
- The system store, which is already fixed.
- Other cohort hosts: for the operator to route. CannObserv/provisioner#77's rollout table is the place.

Refs #65, CannObserv/provisioner#79, CannObserv/address-validator#343. Advisory: https://exe.dev/security/emudhra-compromise

item.title: Second tailnet flap (2026-10-22 04:13–04:15Z): ridden out; decide the flap rule
item.body:
**Filed by the burn-down epic #24's coordinator, 2026-10-22, under the epic's re-entry rule** (set at the first flap, 2026-10-10): "a second flap, or any delayed command, gets an issue." This is the second flap. No command was delayed.

## What happened: 2026-10-22, about 04:13:38Z to 04:15:30Z

- **tailscaled saw the host's network change under it.**
  - At 04:13:46Z, `magicsock: endpoints changed` (STUN `32.185.164.108`, `16.145.19.221`).
  - At 04:14:51Z, `LinkChange: major, rebinding`, then `closing connection to derp-10 (rebind-ping-fail), age 443h21m16s`, and a reconnect to derp-10 (sea).
  - 14 `open-conn-track` timeouts in 04:13–04:15.
  - `16.145.19.221` is the shared NAT that both peers sat behind in the first flap (2026-10-10 02:26–04:12Z).
- **Processor rode it out with no restart** (`NRestarts=0`):
  - 6 × `consumer loop error; backing off`: one `Timeout reading from broker:6379` (04:13:38Z), then 5 × `Timeout connecting to server` up to 04:15:17Z;
  - one `liveness check-in failed` (timed out after 10.0 s, 04:14:44Z);
  - the next liveness check-in was `202` at 04:19:34Z, inside Status's 900 s grace, so nothing paged;
  - the next command acked at 04:25:02Z.
- **No command was delayed.** Each command around the gap acked about 1 s after its XADD (stream IDs `…03:24:01`, `…04:25:01`, `…04:58:01` were acked at `…:02`), and none was issued during it.

## Ask (S, docs or a decision; no code expected)

1. **Find the cause, if it can be seen.** Did the broker and other cohort nodes see the same window (a cohort-wide exe.dev network event, or a host migration), or was it this VM alone? Ask on the broker side only with the operator's approval (cross-repo).
2. **Decide the rule.** The consumer and liveness behaved as designed both times. The coordinator recommends replacing the rule with: "a flap that delays a command, pages, or lasts past liveness's 900 s grace gets an issue; others are logged on the epic." Then document the expected signature in DEPLOYMENT.md, as the epic does for the broker's patch window.
3. #65's planned tailscaled restart is a controlled version of the same event. Its journal is a useful comparison: expect a seconds-long version of the signature above.

Refs #24, #65.

slot.instructions: `epic` is a GitHub issue that tracks a body of work through a checklist of child issues: `epic.goal` says what it covers, `epic.scope` holds its boundary decisions and rules, `epic.children` its checklist lines (done: ticked), and `epic.parked` what waits on a trigger. `item` is an issue filed since the coordinator last looked, with its state now. Which slot does the coordinator give `item` in this epic?

criteria.child: Work this epic covers and that should be done now or in order: it gets its own checklist line, slotted by dependency. A follow-up to a child, a bug in what a child shipped, or a piece split off a child is a child.
criteria.closed-in-fact: Work this epic covers that is already delivered: the item is closed, or a child's merged change already did it, so it is verified, linked and closed with evidence instead of slotted.
criteria.split: The item mixes work this epic covers with work it doesn't, so the epic's part is filed as its own issue and the rest is left out.
criteria.out of epic: Not this epic's work: another skill, service, area or epic, a record or notice with no action, or tooling around the epic rather than its work. It is said so plainly and cross-linked only where it changes a remaining step.
criteria.duplicate: The same work as an existing child or another open issue, so it is closed in favour of that one.
criteria.park: This epic's concern, but not to be done yet: it waits on a trigger (another repo, a decision, a date, an event) and goes in the parked table with that trigger.

item.title: Keep a memory history on co-processor, so the next balloon pause is answerable
item.body:
**Filed by the burn-down epic #24's coordinator, 2026-10-23, from #67's open list.** That list was moved here from CannObserv/broker#118 and now sits only in a comment on the closed #67: "If it recurs, on any VM: turn on a memory history first … Without one, 'was the guest tight?' can't be answered."

## Why before it recurs

A history can't be turned on after the fact. #67 found that the 2026-10-22 04:13Z event was an exe.dev host reclaiming memory through the virtio balloon (`Out of puff` 04:13:26–38Z here), followed by a pause of about 33 s. But nothing on any cohort VM recorded memory over the window, so whether the guest was tight stays unknowable. The balloon's size isn't visible in the guest either (no `STATS_VQ`; `MemTotal` doesn't move under `DEFLATE_ON_OOM`; broker#118's measurements, quoted on #67).

**On co-processor, measured 2026-10-23:** `sysstat` 12.6.1-2 is installed but `ENABLED="false"`, with `sysstat` and `sysstat-collect.timer` disabled and no `/var/log/sysstat`. The merged DEPLOYMENT.md § Tailnet flaps doesn't mention memory history.

## Ask (S, ops plus one docs paragraph; no service code)

1. **Keep a memory history fine enough to see a seconds-long event.** sysstat's default collection is every 10 min, which would miss a 12 s balloon burst. Pick one, your call:
   - sysstat with a 1-min `sysstat-collect.timer` override, so `sar -r` keeps `kbavail` and `kbcommit`;
   - a tiny timer unit logging `MemAvailable`, `MemFree` and the balloon-relevant `/proc/vmstat` counters to the journal every 30–60 s.

   Keep the cost negligible, and never touch `processor.service` or its memory limits.
2. **DEPLOYMENT.md § Tailnet flaps:** one paragraph on where the history lives and the command that reads a window around a flap, beside the triage commands.
3. **Show it works:** read back the last hour's samples.

## Out of scope

- asking exe.dev about the balloon target (the operator's open step from CannObserv/broker#118);
- other VMs (each owner's call; #67's comments list them);
- any change to the flap rule (decided on #67).

Refs #67, #24.

item.title: Viewport capture: consume the capture command, render headless, store, publish the stored-capture fact
item.body:
**Requested by CannObserv/archiver**, which is splitting archiver#5's old fetch settings into one issue each. Operator direction (2026-10-14): viewport screenshots live on **Replicator, as the byte manager**, answering a **dedicated command stream** and **publishing a fact after storage**. The contracts are in the cannobserv issue linked from the comments; archiver's side is in the archiver issue linked there too.

## Scope
- Consume the capture command, using the competing-consumer group pattern.
- Render the page in a headless browser at the requested viewport, honouring `full_page` and the wait condition, within the existing fetch-timeout ceiling.
- Store the image in the blob store, content-addressed, with the same retention machinery as fetched blobs.
- Publish the stored-capture fact **only after storage succeeds**. On failure, publish the failure variant.
- Deduplicate on `command_id`, so a redelivered command does nothing.

## Notes
- **This doesn't conflict with #69's ruling** that the blob store holds nothing Replicator can't rebuild. Replicator renders and stores these bytes itself, so the process that addresses an object is still the one that writes it.
- **Share the browser runtime with #63** (the headless-browser fetch path), but keep the code paths separate. A capture is not a fetch occasion: it produces no `content.blobs` event, and nothing fingerprints it.
- The memory and CPU cost of a browser on the worker host needs a cap on concurrency, separate from HTTP fetch concurrency.
- **Order:** the cannobserv contracts, then broker's stream and ACLs, then this, then archiver's issuance.

item.title: Drop the unused co-core [extract] extra
item.body:
Raised by #140, CR finding 3.

`pyproject.toml` has pinned `co-core[extract]` since #1 (`73981ba`). The extra brings in five parser libraries:

- `beautifulsoup4`
- `html5lib`
- `lxml`
- `openpyxl`
- `pypdf`

Nothing in Replicator uses them. At 0.36.0, these modules of `co_core.pure.extract` are the only ones that import those libraries, and none of them is in the worker's import closure:

- `html`
- `csv_excel`
- `pdf`
- `xml_feed`

The closure is 57 files, walked by AST for #140. The worker does reach `extract.canonical`, through `changes.py`, but that path imports none of the parser libraries.

**Why it matters.** Replicator fetches arbitrary public URLs. An unused HTML/XML/PDF/XLSX parser installed in its venv adds attack surface (lxml and pypdf both have a history of CVEs), install weight, and security-update churn, all for nothing.

**Proposed change.** Pin `co-core>=…` with no extra. Then:

- Prove the worker still imports with a clean install: the CI import smoke and the full suite.
- Check that no test imports a parser.
- Check that the CI `co-core import smoke (extras wired)` step doesn't assert `[extract]`. Update that step if it does.

**Out of scope for #140.** That issue is a no-behaviour-change pin catch-up, and this is a dependency change.

item.title: After F1: state the fetch-policy producer as Archiver, retire the "until F1" wording
item.body:
**Blocked by:** CannObserv/watcher#374 (F1, which stops Watcher's `content.fetch-policy` producer). **Parent:** CannObserv/watcher#368. **From:** #137's build report (the post-F1 note), held out of #137's scope by its brief.

#137 made the producer wording phase-aware, so today the docs say "Watcher until F1, Archiver after it". Once F1 is done, that's history. This issue states the post-F1 case plainly. It's docs only unless the question at the end says otherwise.

## Sites (on `main` at `1c53ea4`)

**`docs/contracts/replicator-boundaries.md`**
- `:70` (the per-host politeness worked example): "in Watcher's `Domain` table until the flip F1, in Archiver after it". After F1 it becomes "in Archiver".
- `:171` (**Producer:**): "Watcher, from its `Domain` table, until the headless-Watcher flip F1 … Archiver after it". After F1 it becomes "Archiver", and the Watcher era is kept as one past-tense clause.
- `:183` (*The fallback default*): "Watcher's own `DEFAULT_MIN_INTERVAL`". That constant is in watcher `src/core/models/domain.py` today and goes when Watcher drops its `Domain` code. Keep it as provenance, but in the past tense.
- **The doc is 9726 of 10000 tokens (exact, 2026-10-18).** Measure before editing. Anything that grows it may need a split first (curating-context).

**`docs/POLITENESS.md`**
- `:66`: "After F1 the producer is Archiver". This becomes present tense.
- `:72`: "**Without one** (all of Watcher's frames)". After F1 that's frames published before F1, plus any Archiver frame built without a `generation`.
- `:126`: "`… for a host that holds one` is a Watcher still publishing after F1, or an Archiver frame built without its `generation`". Check this still reads right once the broker has revoked Watcher's grant (B3).
- `:185`: "1.0 is Watcher's own `DEFAULT_MIN_INTERVAL`". Past tense, the same as the boundaries doc's `:183`.

**`src/worker/policy.py`**
- The module docstring (`:12-26`, "The producer moves at the headless-Watcher flip F1 …").
- The comments at `:241` ("so Watcher's frames behave exactly as they did before #136") and `:362` ("After F1 this is a Watcher that did not stop …"). `:319`'s "Watcher cutover" is Phase 4 history, so it stays.

  The ratchet itself stays. A replay from `0-0` can still return Watcher's pre-F1 frames until retention trims them.

**Keep:** past-tense history such as `replicator-boundaries.md` *"The stream was a precondition of the Phase 4 cutover"* (watcher#245, watcher#272). It's history, not a phase claim.

## A question to settle when this is picked up
When can the **unordered** path go, meaning the `occurred_at` guard for frames without a `generation`?
- Not before cannobserv#579 requires `generation` on `FetchPolicyEmit`.
- Not while `FetchPolicyState` still decodes `generation: None`. #579 keeps that, for replay.
- Not before retention has trimmed Watcher's last frame off `content.fetch-policy`.

If the answer is "not yet", this issue stays docs only.

## Done when
- No doc or docstring above describes F1 as future.
- `tests/test_boundaries.py` is green.
- `measure-context.sh --exact` shows both docs under 10000 and no dead links or anchors.
- If a manifest `description` changed, `codebase_update` runs after the merge.

item.title: Keep the co-core import-closure diff as a script, not a rebuild per pin move
item.body:
`docs/DEPLOYMENT.md` requires a diff of co-core's whole import closure before any multi-minor pin move. That came from #140, which found that a module list misses `extract.canonical`, loaded transitively through `changes.py`. #140 and #136 each rebuilt the walker from scratch: an AST walk from `src/` through every co-core module reached, then a docstring-stripped AST comparison between two wheels. #136's CR 4 suggested keeping it, and the suggestion was held back.

**Proposed:** `scripts/co_core_closure_diff.py <old-version> <new-version>`. It reads both wheels from `.wheelhouse`, walks the closure from `src/`, and prints each file's verdict: identical, docstrings only, or code changed (with a diff). DEPLOYMENT.md's pin section then points to it, and the next bump records its output in the pin comment.

**Done when:**
- The script reproduces #136's result for 0.36.0 → 0.37.0: 57 files at each version, and six changed (three `__init__` `__version__` bumps, `envelope.py`, `streams.py` and `changes.py`).
- It's tested against a fixture pair.
- `docs/COMMANDS.md` doesn't grow, because that doc is already over budget (see the curation follow-up). Document the script in DEPLOYMENT.md's pin section instead.

From #136's build report ("For a later chore"). Not part of epic #135.

item.title: init-socraticode: pin the session too — SOCRATICODE_SPEC refutes the "cannot pin the session" limitation (gregoryfoster/skills#327)
item.body:
## Why

#389 pinned the driver at **1.14.0**. Its closing notes, and this repo's docs, carry the upstream "Known limitation": pinning the driver cannot pin the *session*, because Claude Code cannot override a plugin's MCP command.

**That is refuted for this plugin** ([gregoryfoster/skills#327](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/issues/327), shipped in `gregoryfoster/skills@e82ccf9`). Since upstream SocratiCode [`0c33776`](https://github.com/giancarloerra/socraticode/commit/0c33776) (2026-09-20), the plugin's live manifest `.claude-plugin/mcp.json` launches `npx -y --prefer-online ${SOCRATICODE_SPEC:-socraticode@latest}`, so the repo's settings `env` block pins the session's server too. CannObserv/replicator#99 measured it off the process table: `npm exec socraticode@1.14.0`.

So this host is **half pinned**. The driver (health hook, `index`, `verify`) runs the pre-install, while every session start still runs `@latest` through npx. On a day the package moves, that is an install at session start: the [gregoryfoster/skills#295](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/issues/295) memory peak on the host #389 measured as needing protection.

## What to do

1. **Bump `skills-vendor/gregoryfoster-skills`** to `e82ccf9` or later (pinned at `d521f81` today). Then run `bash skills-vendor/gregoryfoster-skills/skills/init-socraticode/scripts/preflight.sh --check`, which now reports both pins.
2. **If preflight says the installed plugin never reads `SOCRATICODE_SPEC`, update the socraticode plugin first.** The variable shipped after the 1.14.0 release without a version bump, so a plugin install labelled 1.14.0 can predate it.
3. **Pin the session to the driver's version** in `.claude/settings.json`:
   ```json
   { "env": { "SOCRATICODE_SPEC": "socraticode@1.14.0" } }
   ```
   Merge it into the existing `env` block if there is one. It reaches only sessions started afterwards.
4. **Verify what launched, never a manifest.** The plugin ships three manifests, and the two at its root still hardcode `@latest`. Use `claude mcp list` (the `plugin:socraticode:socraticode:` line prints the command) or `ps -eo args | grep socraticode`, and expect `socraticode@1.14.0`. preflight should then print *Plugin session launches socraticode 1.14.0 …, as the driver pin does — no launch installs*.
5. **Correct the docs that restate the limitation:**

| File | Lines | Says |
|---|---|---|
| `docs/SOCRATICODE.md` | 422-425 | **It does not pin the session.** Claude Code cannot override a plugin's MCP command, so the plugin keeps launching `@latest`… |
| `scripts/disk-gc.sh` | 441-443 | the comment giving the npx-cache sweep's reason: "Claude Code cannot override a plugin's MCP command, so the plugin keeps launching @latest and minting a fresh ~457 MB tree per release" |

   Replace the limitation with the variable, the version it is pinned to, and how to verify it. Re-pinning now means changing both the pre-install and `SOCRATICODE_SPEC`.

On `scripts/disk-gc.sh`: once the session is pinned, the plugin stops minting a new npx tree for each release, which was the stated reason for the sweep. The sweep is still worth keeping for caches a pin does not cover (old hashes, the driver's own history). Correct the reason in the comment, not the code; `scripts/tests/test_disk_gc.py` matched the same wording in the code search, so check it too.

## Not in scope

The daily health hook's own launch is still uncapped upstream; that is tracked in [gregoryfoster/skills#330](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/issues/330). A repo that caps it locally should know that an `init-socraticode` re-run replaces a hand-written hook command (details in gregoryfoster/skills#330).

## Closing this

Close it once `claude mcp list` shows the session launching the pinned version and the docs above no longer call it impossible. If preflight shows this host's plugin cannot read the variable and updating it isn't possible yet, record that and leave this open.

item.title: Roster PDF: a newly archived edition never reaches the #302 raw store
item.body:
Follow-up from #237 (CR 2 on #420).

## The gap

The #237 monthly re-check tells an operator when a new roster edition is published. The runbook's answer is to archive it with `python -m usa_wa_adapter_legislature.roster_pdf.harvest --revision <new>`. That archive lands **in Postgres only**: `AdapterRunner.archive_only` writes `FetchEvent` + `RawPayload` and never touches the #304 raw store.

The #302 pipeline doesn't read Postgres for the roster. It stages from the raw store:
- `usa_wa_pipeline/staging/roster.py` parses the newest `legroster:<revision>` there by `fetched_at`.
- That feeds `stg_roster_members` and `parity_spans`.

Nothing writes the roster to the raw store on a schedule. `pipeline-nightly.sh` runs three `raw_harvest` CLIs (WSL SOAP, PDC, SOS), and none of them covers the roster PDF.

Checked in prod on 2026-09-24: `raw/usa_wa_legislature_roster/latest.json` has one entry, `legroster:2025-06-05`, with `run_id` `20260903T062255-4b7c1a`. That is the one-shot `clearinghouse_core.raw_export` (#305).

**Consequence:** a new edition archived by the runbook stays invisible to the pipeline and the published datasets, and nothing says so. Right now the #237 runbook states this gap and points here.

## Options

1. **A roster raw harvest.** Add `roster_pdf` to the raw tier as a fourth `raw_harvest`, or run it on demand after a new edition, so the edition lands in the raw store with its own manifest.
2. **The roster harvest dual-writes.** It also records the fetch into the raw store (`RawStore.record_fetch`), the way the three raw harvests do.
3. **Re-run `raw_export`.** Its resumable cursor moves every payload-bearing `FetchEvent` since 2026-09-03, across all sources, not just the roster. Only safe if that is confirmed harmless (the export docstring says `latest.json` can't regress). Not verified here.

With #314 retiring the provenance tables, the roster's Phase A has to reach the raw store eventually anyway. Option 1 or 2 is the durable shape.

## Done when

- Archiving a new roster edition makes it the newest `legroster:` object in the raw store without a manual export.
- The #237 runbook in `docs/COMMANDS-ROSTER.md` § Roster PDF drops its pointer to this issue.

item.title: Establish a nightly backup regime for the production Postgres
item.body:
## Why

usa-wa's production Postgres has **no backup regime**. #430 found this during the OS patch run (2026-09-26), and its brief asks for the gap to get an owner, the way CannObserv/archiver#233 ("Establish nightly backup regime to GCS") gives archiver's one.

What #430 measured [2026-09-26]:
- `/var/backups` was **empty** before the run, and `dpkg-db-backup.timer` is inactive.
- The only recovery points that exist are the ones #430 made by hand:
  - `/var/backups/usa_wa-20260926T224310Z.dump`, which the owner copied off the node with `scp` (sha256 verified);
  - `usa_wa-20260926T231113Z.dump`, on the node only;
  - `pg-globals-20260926T224310Z.sql`, on the node only, because it holds role password hashes.
- Size and cost: `usa_wa` is 73 MB on disk, and `pg_dump -Fc` produces **13.2 MB in 2.2 s**. `pg_dumpall --globals-only` is 1.8 kB.
- Access: both dumps run as the local `postgres` superuser over peer auth, so a unit needs no DB credentials.
- The 5 `*_test` databases are disposable and are out of scope.

## Scope

Follow the patterns established by Broker and Watcher, as archiver#233 does:
- a nightly `pg_dump -Fc usa_wa` to GCS, in a new bucket (e.g. `co-gcs-usa-wa-backup`; the name is the owner's call);
- a retention policy;
- a restore drill, documented and actually run once.

Constraints from this repo:
- **Schedule outside the daily chain.** The chain runs 05:45Z–08:00Z, the pipeline from 08:00Z, the Sunday integrity sweep at 08:01Z, and the roster recheck on the 1st at 09:02Z. logrotate runs at 00:00Z.
- **A systemd unit + timer under `deploy/`,** carrying the #87 `assert-main-checkout.sh` and #279 `assert-venv-integrity.sh` `ExecStartPre=` guards if it runs repo code, plus `OnFailure=` alerting (#49). `test_unit_ordering.py` enforces the guards.
- **Keep the globals dump separate** (role password hashes): encrypted, or kept on the node only.
- Document it in `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md` (the unit table) and `docs/DEPLOYMENT-HOST.md`.

## Out of scope

- OS patching cadence: gregoryfoster/skills#313 D4.

item.title: exe-init: sessions already at oom_score_adj 0; replacement binary staged in /tmp, no action needed
item.body:
**Low priority, informational.** exe.dev confirmed on 2026-09-29, answering CannObserv/status#5, that some `exe-init` builds start agent sessions at `oom_score_adj` **-1000**. The kernel and earlyoom never kill a -1000 process. So under memory pressure the host's services are killed first, and the sessions most likely to have caused the pressure survive. exe.dev's workaround: copy `/exe.dev/bin/exe-init` from a new VM and restart.

| | Measured 2026-09-29 (exe.dev HTTPS API, `ssh usa-wa`) |
|---|---|
| `exe-init --version` | `b862c44` (sha256 `2855b2df245c…`, built 2026-05-23) |
| Session `oom_score_adj` | **0** |
| Layout | newer: `pgrep -x exe-init` finds `exe-init op-ssh` + `exe-init memd` (root, children of PID 1, both `oom_score_adj` 0) |

**This VM is not affected:** its `exe-init` build starts sessions at 0. A replacement was staged anyway, as part of a cohort-wide copy: `/tmp/exe-init.14fd603`, with `/tmp/exe-init.14fd603.sha256`. It was copied on 2026-09-29 from a VM created fresh for this and since deleted. `exe-init version 14fd603`, sha256 `6403375d4b2f693e260cd210fee072ea73859a390bbf51ba0d249a27195184bf`, and its hash was checked on this VM after the copy. `/tmp` is on disk here, but `systemd-tmpfiles` clears files older than about 10 days. If it's gone, copy the binary from a newly created VM.

**Action:** none. Delete `/tmp/exe-init.14fd603*` whenever convenient. If sessions ever read -1000 after a platform change, see gregoryfoster/skills#313 for the fix.

Related: CannObserv/status#5 (found and fixed on co-status), CannObserv/notifier#88, gregoryfoster/skills#313 (the cohort-wide record).

item.title: Publish committee succession links (dataset) + port INV2
item.body:
## Problem

usa-wa holds **162 operator-attested committee succession links** in `registry.committee_succession_events` (`succeeded_by` / `split_from` / `merged_with`, with year, evidence URL and a supersede chain), but **no published dataset carries them**. The C3 producer that pushed them to power-map as linked-entity events retired with the sync (#314). The published tier never picked them up; `docs/PIPELINE.md` § Ported from the canonical tier lists a succession dataset, and INV2, as **deferred**.

So every link recorded since #314 reaches nobody. The immediate case is Civic Health (#444, #445): power-map minted the re-established body (WSL 36500) but has no producer edge linking it to its predecessor (35341). power-map would have to curate the edge by hand, and repeat that for every future re-key, including the WSL re-keys expected with the 2027 roster.

A second, related gap: `organizations.active` for a Joint/Other body means "met this biennium". A predecessor that expires mid-biennium therefore stays `active=true` until the rollover: 35341 expired in January 2026 but publishes active until 2027-01-01 (power-map#592). Porting INV2 would close that too.

## Scope

1. **Publish the links.** Either a new dataset (e.g. `org_lineage`: subject/linked `entity_id` resolved through `org_crosswalk`, the raw WSL ids beside them, `slug`, `effective_year`, `evidence_url`, `notes`) or columns on `organizations`. A separate dataset seems cleaner: links are many-to-many and carry their own evidence. Only non-superseded links; superseding a link retracts the old row from the next version.
2. **Read path.** The conformed tier reads the registry through `registry_read` (dbt Python model, own engine); a succession read follows the same pattern. Resolve each WSL id to its `entity_id` through merges, like the crosswalk.
3. **Gates.** Each link end resolves to a live published org (a dbt error test), and there are no cycles among `succeeded_by` links.
4. **INV2 as a dbt test** (a succeeded or merged predecessor is `active=false`, `split_from` exempt). Decide whether `organizations.active` should *derive* false for a succeeded predecessor, which fixes 35341, or whether the test should only flag it. Deriving it changes `organizations` values, so it's a contract minor with a PM re-pin (power-map#591 shows the cost).
5. **Contract and docs.** Add the dataset to `PUBLISHED_DATASETS` with its schema version, and update `docs/PIPELINE-PUBLICATION.md`, `docs/PIPELINE-CONFORMED-ENTITIES.md`, and the deferral note in `docs/PIPELINE.md`.
6. **Tell power-map.** Post the new dataset and contract on power-map#592 so their mapping can take the edges.

## Out of scope

- The retired C3 push. power-map pulls published datasets; nothing is pushed.
- Fixing the retired by-hand `lineage_invariants` unit, which reads frozen canonical.

Refs: #444, #445, #124 (lineage design), #314, #412, #428, power-map#592, power-map#591.

item.title: Rollover rehearsal 2: re-run after #412 closes and SOS certifies the 2026 general (before 2026-12-31)
item.body:
Follow-up to #135 item 2. **Due before 2026-12-31. Blocked by #412** (closing) **and by SOS certifying the 2026 general** (~2026-12-03).

## Why a second rehearsal

Rehearsal 1 (2026-10-01, `docs/research/2026-10-01-biennium-rollover-rehearsal.md`) ran too early on two counts:
- **It rehearsed a chain that won't run on Jan 1.** #412 PR F, after the soak, changes the nightly chain.
- **No 2026 ballot existed yet.** So the SOS lookahead failed, and **no House seat reopened** in the partial scenario (0 of 61). A 2027-28 House Position comes only from the 2026 ballot.

#135's acceptance is that "the 2027-01-01 nightly publishes (or refuses) for a reason we predicted in the rehearsal". That prediction has to come from the chain and the data Jan 1 will actually see.

## Steps

- [ ] Confirm #412 is closed.
- [ ] Confirm the certified results are in `raw/`: `sos-legresults:20261103` has a sha256 newer than election night (use the snippet in the research doc).
- [ ] `scripts/rollover-rehearsal.sh empty`, **not during the 08:00 nightly** (the wrapper refuses). Record the outcome lines.
  - If WSL has already published 2027-28 sponsors, this run is the real Jan 1 state. Say so.
- [ ] `scripts/rollover-rehearsal.sh partial`. Record it. **Key check: House seats now reopen** for returning members.
- [ ] Compare both runs with `docs/RUNBOOK-ROLLOVER.md` § 2027-01-01. Update the runbook for any difference, and turn each surprise into a test or a fix.
- [ ] Append "Rehearsal 2" to the research doc.
- [ ] Delete `~/rehearsal/` (~135 MB per run).

item.title: Rollover window: accept or suppress the expected nightly emails from 2027-01-01 until WSL publishes 2027-28 (decide by 2026-12-15)
item.body:
Follow-up to #135. **Decide by 2026-12-15**, so that any implementation can land and be rehearsed (#451) before 2026-12-31.

## The situation

Rehearsal 1 predicts that from **2027-01-01 until WSL publishes 2027-28**, the nightly exits 1 **every night**. The expected email has exactly two failed-stage lines (`docs/RUNBOOK-ROLLOVER.md` § 2027-01-01):

1. `usa_wa_adapter_legislature.raw_harvest (exit 4)`: `GetCommittees(2027-28)` raises a server fault rather than returning an empty list, so the harvest is degraded.
2. `usa_wa_pipeline.build_warnings (exit 1)`: `assignments_chamber_vacancy`. Every 2025-26 span closed at 2026-12-31 and nothing is open yet.

Publishing continues throughout; the data is correct for the moment.

How long this lasts is unknown. `usa-wa-wsl-availability-probe.timer` measures it daily, and if WSL publishes 2027-28 before Jan 1 the window may be zero days. The concern is #333's: a nightly email nobody can act on is how alerting stops being read.

## Options

1. **Accept the emails** (current state). The runbook names the exact two lines, and anything else is real. Cost: one email per night during the window.
2. **A time-boxed acceptance, following the #333 pattern** (`ACCEPTED_OUTAGES` in `usa_wa_adapter_sos/raw_harvest.py`):
   - accept the `committees-roster:<current>` fault while `sponsors:<current>` is still empty;
   - accept `assignments_chamber_vacancy` while the current biennium has no staged sponsors;
   - both expire on their own once WSL publishes (the stale-acceptance mechanism reports the change).
3. **Hybrid:** accept only the harvest fault, and keep the vacancy warning, since it's the signal that WSL hasn't published.

## Inputs

- The availability probe log (`data/research/wsl-availability.jsonl`) as of mid-December. If sponsors and committees are already answering, close this as moot.

item.title: Close out the 2027-28 rollover: record availability dates, retire the probe timer after 2027-02-28, verify #135 acceptance (due 2027-03-07)
item.body:
Follow-up to #135. **Due 2027-03-07**, a week after the availability window closes.

## Steps

- [ ] **Record the dates.** Fill in "Source availability for 2027-28" in `docs/research/2026-10-01-biennium-rollover-rehearsal.md`:
  - WSL from `data/research/wsl-availability.jsonl`;
  - PDC and SOS from the raw manifests (snippet in that doc). Date PDC by its first non-empty cohort, because its hash churns.
- [ ] **Retire the probe timer.** After 2027-02-28, run `sudo systemctl disable --now usa-wa-wsl-availability-probe.timer`. The probe already asks nothing past `--until`. Then mark the timer retired in README's enable block and DEPLOYMENT's tables (the timer-doc drift guard pins both).
- [ ] **Check #135's acceptance, then close it:**
  - [ ] Nov 2026 winners and certified results reached `raw/` within a day of publication (from the dates above).
  - [ ] The 2027-01-01 nightly published, or refused, for a reason rehearsal 2 (#451) predicted — and per the #452 decision on window emails.
  - [ ] No nightly alert from November through February that the runbook didn't anticipate.
- [ ] **Prepare the 2029 rollover.** The unit hardcodes `--biennium 2027-28 --until 2027-02-28`, and README and DEPLOYMENT say "through 2027-02-28". Decide between:
  - deriving the incoming biennium and the window from the date (`lookahead_election_year` already encodes the November boundary), which removes the per-rollover edit; or
  - filing a 2029 rollover issue that lists the edits.
  
  Also carry forward what this rollover taught (runbook, rehearsal tooling).

item.title: Dead-man alert for the nightly backup (a run that never starts is silent)
item.body:
## Why

The nightly backup from #434 (PR #454) emails on failure through `OnFailure=`. It sends nothing when it **doesn't run at all**: the timer gets disabled, the unit is never installed on a new host, or the job is stuck before systemd records a failure. A backup that has silently stopped looks exactly like a healthy one.

CannObserv/watcher closes this gap with a dead-man check-in to co-status. Each run posts `ok` (or `alert`), and a monitor raises an alarm when no check-in arrives within its window (`interval_seconds` 86400 + `grace_seconds` 7200). That's watcher's `src/ops/checkin.py` and `docs/RECOVERY.md` § Provisioning. usa-wa has no co-status integration yet.

## Scope

- A check-in from `usa_wa_api.backup.run`: `ok` with the run's summary, `alert` with the error. The key arrives as a second `LoadCredential=`. As in watcher, the key file must exist even if empty, because systemd 255 refuses to start on a missing credential source.
- A co-status monitor (tenant for usa-wa). Watch it fire once by shortening its window, as watcher's rehearsal did.
- Update `docs/RECOVERY.md` § Design ("Silence is not yet alarmed").

## Out of scope

- The backup itself: #434.

item.title: Backup check-in: log the 202's dispatch ids, so a check-in can be matched to notifier from this side
item.body:
## Why

`usa_wa_api.backup.checkin` (#455) logs only `backup_checkin_sent` with the `status` it sent. httpx's own line adds the status code. co-status's 202 body lists the notifier dispatches the check-in caused under `dispatches`: an `alert`'s rendered report, or the *recovered* notice that ends an outage. Neither log line records them.

In the 2026-10-02 rehearsal, the recovery dispatch id (`01M3Z75Q76P2SAGDM421HMD7EJ`) could only come from co-status's database. Nothing on this side tied that check-in to that dispatch.

## Scope

- Return the parsed `dispatches` ids from the POST seam alongside the status code, and log them on `backup_checkin_sent` (ids only; never the variables or the key).
- A body that is not JSON, or has no `dispatches`, still counts as a landed check-in. Logging must never change the outcome.

Low priority: co-status records every dispatch, so this only adds convenience on our side. Raised on CannObserv/status#17.

item.title: WSL-family overlays log roster-family operator events as inert (54 of #282's 90 seatings are noise)
item.body:
Found measuring #282 (2026-10-02, prod pipeline db).

## What

`build_all_spans` hands **every** operator event to the WSL-family overlays (committee, House, sponsor). Events for roster-family members (minted `<fold>:<year>` ids) can never match there — those spans belong to `build_roster_spans`, which scopes its events to its own members and applies them. The WSL overlays log the misses anyway.

Measured on one conformed rebuild:

- **54 of the 90** `operator_seated_no_span_out_of_biennium` distinct seatings are roster-family members whose span **is** dated — by the roster builder. Pure noise. 7 of them are in the Nov/Dec-of-even-year set #282's body counted as inert (e.g. `alanthompson:1965 senate-18 1982-11-16`, `joetanner:1983 senate-18 1986-12-12`).
- Very likely most of the **716** `operator_departed_no_open_span` lines have the same cause (not yet classified).

## Why it matters

`operator_seated_no_span_out_of_biennium` is the signal #282 was measured on. With ~60% of it noise, a real inert seating is indistinguishable from a miss the roster builder already handled, and the next re-measure will over-count again.

## Suggested fix

Scope the WSL overlays' events to members the WSL family can hold (the mirror of `build_roster_spans`' `scoped = [e for e in events if e.member_id in members]`), or log the miss only when no family owns the member. Pin with a test that a roster-family event logs nothing from `build_all_spans`. Then re-measure both counters.

Related: #282.

item.title: Mover's seated event precedes the vacated that synthesizes its House span — 15814 keeps the biennium floor
item.body:
Found measuring #282 (2026-10-02, prod pipeline db). One live case.

## What

Member **15814**: `seated chamber-house ld-18-position-1 2011-01-05` and `vacated chamber-house ld-18-position-1 2012-06-25` (a #145 chamber mover to Senate LD18). The House span is not built by the wire (mover exclusion); `vacated` **synthesizes** it closed as `[2011-01-01 → 2012-06-25]` (`operator_vacated_synthesized_closed`).

But `apply_operator_events` sorts seat-scoped events by date, so the `seated` (2011-01-05) is processed **before** the `vacated` (2012-06-25) synthesizes the span it should date. It matches nothing, logs `operator_seated_no_span_out_of_biennium`, and the synthesized span keeps the 2011-01-01 floor.

## Expected

`ld-18-position-1:2011-12` for 15814 starts 2011-01-05.

## Suggested fix

Either synthesize mover-closed House spans before the seated pass (a pre-pass over `vacated` events gated on `movers_by_biennium`), or have `_synthesize_closed` honour an earlier `seated` for the same member + seat in that biennium as its `valid_from`. Pin with the 15814 shape in `test_operator_overlay.py`.

Related: #282, #145.

Split from #282's secondary (2026-10-02), which said "settle or drop with the canonical write path's retirement". #282 shipped the overlay fix only; this is still open.

> `operator_cites`, not `operator_events_loaded`, is the **applied** count. … A citation is written only where a boundary really moved.

Following that on this run concludes nothing applied, when four boundaries had.

Either the counter misses the pre-1991 builder's citation writes (`roster_pdf/build.py` ~L292, `cite_operator_events`), or the doc's claim is wrong. item.title: operator_departed_no_open_span is logged per overlay, not per family — 88 of 110 departures are structural noise
item.body:
Found shipping #460 (PR #465). Measured 2026-10-05 on a read-only snapshot of the prod pipeline db plus the current operator events, with main at `d224cdf`.

## What

`apply_operator_events` decides `hit` per call, and `build_all_spans` calls it once per overlay: committee, House (`build_house_spans`) and sponsor (`party` + `chamber-senate`). A `departed` event that closes nothing in **one** overlay logs `operator_departed_no_open_span`, even when another overlay closed the member's spans. After #460, that leaves **191 lines for 110 WSL-family departures**:

| overlays that logged a miss | events | what it means |
|---|---|---|
| House only | 49 | a senator; there is no House seat to close |
| House + committee | 37 | a senator with no open committee span at the date |
| committee only | 2 | a representative with no open committee span |
| **all three** | **22** | nothing open anywhere |

The first three rows (**88 events, ~150 lines**) are structural. The overlay that missed was never going to hold a span for that member, and the sponsor overlay closed the seat and party.

Of the 22 that miss everywhere, about 20 are **term-end departures**: the event is dated on or just after the member's last span end (for example `12082 2014-12-31`, last span end 2014-12-31; `21520 2025-01-04`, last span end 2024-12-31). `_is_open_through` needs `valid_to > date`, so a span the wire already closed at the end of the biennium is not "open through" the date. The event is redundant, not a miss.

Two don't fit and are worth checking against the roster PDF:
- `321` departed **1997-01-15**, but holds spans through 2012-12-31. Did they leave and come back, with no span open at the date?
- `656` departed **1996-05-13**, but their last span ends **1994-12-31**. That is a 16-month gap: either a 1995-96 tenure is missing or the event is misdated.

## Why it matters

`operator_departed_no_open_span` is the overlay's only "this event did nothing" signal (CR finding 10). At ~191 lines per rebuild, the two real anomalies above can't be seen, which is the same problem #460 fixed for `operator_seated_no_span_out_of_biennium`.

## Suggested fix

1. **Report a departure miss per family, not per overlay.** Have `apply_operator_events` return or expose which `departed` events it applied. `build_all_spans` then logs one `operator_departed_no_open_span` for an event that no WSL overlay applied, and each overlay's own miss drops to DEBUG. `build_roster_spans` keeps its own reporting; it is one call.
2. **Separate the redundant term-end case.** If the member's span in this family closed on or before the date and nothing is open after it, log `operator_departed_already_closed` (INFO). Keep `operator_departed_no_open_span` for the rest.
3. Pin both with tests: a senator's departure logs nothing from the House overlay, and a departure dated on the span end logs `already_closed`. Then re-measure. The expected result is about 2 genuine misses, then check 321 and 656.

Related: #460, #282, #107 (CR finding 10).

item.title: Operator event for member 656 (Jim Springer) is Betty Sue Morris's 1996 resignation, mis-resolved
item.body:
Found re-measuring #466 (PR #467). After that change, 656 is one of the two WSL-family `operator_departed_no_open_span` lines left.

## What
Current operator events:
- `294` (Betty Morris, House LD18, 1991–96): `departed 1996-05-13` ✔
- `656` (James Springer, House LD18, **1993-94 only**): `departed 1996-05-13` ✘

The roster PDF has one matching row: 1995, House LD18, `Betty Sue Morris — Resigned May 13, 1996;` (successor Farley Maxwell, appointed June 19, 1996). Springer has no 1995-96 row and no annotation. So the same resignation was projected onto two members of the same district seat. 656's event closes nothing, because his last span ends 1994-12-31.

## Fix
1. Supersede 656's `departed 1996-05-13` event.
2. Find out why the backfill resolved Morris's annotation onto Springer too (same LD + chamber, adjacent biennium). Then check whether other events have the same shape: a `departed` on a member with no span in the event's biennium, while a same-seat member holds an identical event.

Related: #466, #226.

item.title: Lt. Governor's ex-officio Senate Rules rows build legislator committee spans (Brad Owen, 1999–2012)
item.body:
Found re-measuring #466 (PR #467). 321 is one of the two WSL-family `operator_departed_no_open_span` lines left.

## What
`321` is Brad Owen: Senate LD35 through 1995-96. The roster records him as "Resigned Jan. 15, 1997; Elected Lt. Governor November 5, 1996". The `departed 1997-01-15` event is correct. His Senate seat span already ended 1996-12-31, so the event is a term end.

It still logs a miss, rather than `operator_departed_already_closed`, because 321 has **committee** spans from 1999-01-01 to 2012-12-31. `stg_wsl_committee_members` lists him on Senate **Rules** in every biennium from 1999-00 to 2011-12. The Lt. Governor presides over the Senate and sits on Rules ex officio. He was not a legislator in those years.

## Question
Should a non-legislator's ex-officio committee row become a legislator committee-membership span (and be published in `assignments`)? If not, exclude it at the committee projector, and check the other Lt. Governors (Denny Heck, Cyrus Habib) for the same shape.

Related: #466.

item.title: Publish shrink gate compares to the previous night only; nothing watches absolute counts since #412
item.body:
`usa_wa_pipeline.publish` refuses a publish when a dataset shrinks more than `--max-shrink` (default 10%) **against the previous publish**. Its own comment (`publish.py` ~784) names the gap: decay just under the threshold compounds unseen, about 50% a week at 10% a night. Until now that was accepted because the parity probes watched **absolute** counts against the canonical tier. They retired in #412 PR E, and the tier itself was dropped in PR F (#470), so nothing watches absolute counts any more.

## The failure it allows

A slow upstream degradation, or a parser regression that drops rows a few percent at a time, ships every night with green gates. Retraction-by-absence then retracts those rows downstream. `registry_coverage` checks that the spans which exist are registered, not that the right number exist. `parity_citations` checks citation integrity, not volume.

## Options

1. **A windowed baseline:** compare against the max (or median) of the last N publishes. The catalog keeps every version, so N=7 sees a week of decay as one shrink. This is the upgrade path the comment names.
2. **Absolute floors per dataset:** a committed minimum (for example persons ≥ 3,000, assignments ≥ 8,000), reviewed when a real contraction happens. They're blunt but independent of history.
3. **Both:** the window catches decay, and the floors catch a slow drift that never trips a window.

Whichever is chosen, it needs a test with a synthetic history of nightly 9% shrinks: today's gate passes it, and the new one must refuse it.

- Gate: `packages/usa-wa-pipeline/src/usa_wa_pipeline/publish.py`, `DEFAULT_MAX_SHRINK`. Contract doc: `docs/PIPELINE-PUBLICATION.md`.
- First raised in #412's PR F review as a risk created by retiring the parity probes.

item.title: Periodic dead-code scan: run vulture across the codebase
item.body:
Follow-up from #471 / PR #474.

## Problem
#471 was found by hand: a reviewer noticed that #412 PR F (#470) left helpers with no production caller. The hand scan (`rg -w`, skipping each symbol's defining file) got several cases wrong in both directions:
- It listed `Clause`, `ParsedDate` and `IdentityReport` as dead. They are live, because live functions return them.
- It listed `match_house_member` and `find_confirming_senator` as live. They were dead, because only `pdc.observations` called them.
- It missed cascades. `probe_surname` was reachable only through `split_name`, which was reachable only through the deleted `identity_seatings`.

Dead code inflates the whole-tree coverage figure (#413's concern), and the MODULES docs keep describing it as live. Nothing catches it between large retirements.

## Proposal
Run [vulture](https://github.com/jendrikseipp/vulture) over production code on a schedule. Report candidates, and never fail a build on them.

- **Scope:** `packages/*/src`, `scripts/*.py` and `packages/usa-wa-pipeline/dbt`. dbt Python models are real callers, so vulture must see them.
- **Allowlist:** a checked-in whitelist module, so known false positives stay quiet and each entry carries its reason. Known false positives:
  - FastAPI route handlers (`health`, `list_persons`, …), which are registered by decorator.
  - Pydantic/dataclass fields.
  - `clearinghouse_core.testing` fixtures.
  - Entry points named in `pyproject.toml` `[project.scripts]` and systemd units.
  - Deliberate keeps recorded in #471: `run_job(role="owner")` and `configure_{wsl,sos,results}_rate_limit`.
- **Cadence:** pick one of three options:
  - a monthly systemd timer, alongside the existing weekly/monthly ones;
  - a step in `scripts/pre-ship.sh`, as a warning only;
  - a step in the weekly `curating-context` maintenance pass.
- **Output:** any new candidate opens or updates a GH issue listing the symbol, its file and line, and the commit that removed its last caller (`git log -S`).
- **Triage rule (from #471):** a docstring reference is not a caller, but a dbt Python model is. Before deleting, check for cascades: delete, then re-run until nothing new appears.

## Seed backlog
These were flagged at 60% confidence on #474's branch and fall outside #471's scope. None has been checked for dbt, entry-point or dynamic callers yet:
- `roster_pdf.audit.audit_roster`
- `roster_pdf.normalize.parse_district_pages`
- `roster_pdf.resources.revision_from_resource_id`
- `sos.{filings,results}.resources.election_year_from_resource_id`
- `sponsors.roster_hygiene.stale_member_ids`
- `committees.succession_store.superseded_events`
- `committees.probe_extent.probe_floor`
- `meetings.windows.parse_meetings_resource_id`
- `committee_succession.find_succession_cycles`
- `source_coverage.known_gaps`
- `database.reset_engine`
- `logging.ColorMessageFilter`
- `jurisdictions.wa_jurisdiction_facts`
- `parties.tally_party_tokens`
- `seats.ld_slug`
- `backup.raw_mirror.local_inventory` / `unrecognized_files`
- `serving.load.datapackage_fields` / `ensure_serving_schema`
- `api.v1.schemas.parse_ulid_path`

## Done when
- vulture is a dev dependency, with a whitelist that holds the known false positives and the reason for each.
- A scheduled or ritual run exists and is documented in `docs/COMMANDS.md`.
- The seed backlog is triaged: each entry is deleted or allowlisted with a reason.

item.title: Model the Lt. Governor's Senate roles (President of the Senate, ex-officio chair of Senate Rules)
item.body:
Split from #469.

## What
The Lt. Governor is President of the Senate and chairs Senate **Rules**, which decides which bills reach the floor. That is real legislative power. We don't model it.

#469 excludes the only place it reached the published data: WSL `GetCommitteeMembers` listed Brad Owen (member id 321) on Senate Rules from 1999-00 through 2011-12, under his old senator record ("Senator Owen", LD 35), as a plain member. That source can't support the role:

- **Patchy coverage.** Owen held the office from 1997-01 to 2017-01. WSL lists him only for 1999–2012: our harvest starts at 1999, and WSL stopped listing him in 2013-14 and 2015-16 while he was still in office. Habib (2017–21) and Heck (2021–) never appear.
- **No title field.** The wire has `Id, Name, LongName, Agency, Acronym, Party, District, Phone, Email`, so it can't say "chair" or "Lt. Governor".

## Scope
1. **Who held the office.** Lt. Governor tenures 1889–present. Possible sources: SOS statewide results (staging is filtered to legislative races today, so no Lt. Gov row exists), PDC winners for the same office, or an operator attestation for the historical list. Audit coverage first (ARCHITECTURE.md).
2. **Model it.** Per ONTOLOGY.md § 5:
   - a role, e.g. `president_of_senate` (the Senate org) and/or a Lt. Governor role (an executive org; `org_type` has no `executive` today);
   - a new `role_type`, which is a gated vocabulary, so it's a contract bump;
   - a span kind and a citation rule.
3. **The ex-officio chair of Senate Rules.** Derive it from holding the office, not from WSL roster rows: a `committee_chair`-style assignment on org 209 (and its predecessors/successors via `org_lineage`) for the whole tenure.
4. **Related gap.** We publish no committee leadership for anyone: chair, vice chair, ranking member. `GetCommitteeMembers` doesn't carry it. Decide whether this issue covers it or a sibling does.

## Not in scope
#469's exclusion guard: a roster row whose member is in no sponsor roster that biennium isn't a legislator membership.

item.title: disk-gc: keep the pinned SocratiCode npx tree — liveness-only pruning reinstalls it uncapped at session start
item.body:
## Why

#415 (PR #484) pinned the SocratiCode session: `SOCRATICODE_SPEC=socraticode@1.16.0`, with its npx tree warmed deliberately under the memory cap. Verified 2026-10-09: the session's server launched as `npm exec socraticode@1.16.0` and preflight says *no launch installs*.

`scripts/disk-gc.sh --prune` runs daily (`usa-wa-disk-gc.timer`, ~05:45 UTC). It judges `~/.npm/_npx/*` by **liveness only** (`consider` → `is_live`, then the 60-min `recently_touched` grace). If no session holds the pinned tree when the timer fires, it deletes it. The next session start then reinstalls it **uncapped**: the gregoryfoster/skills#295 / #389 memory peak that the pin exists to prevent. On this host (7.7 GiB, no swap, prod co-tenant) that is the failure the whole #389/#415 chain guards against.

The #415 comment above the npx loop states this residual risk; this issue fixes it.

## Evidence that the tree is identifiable

npx names a single-package cache dir by `sha512(<spec>)[:16]`. Checked on this host:

| Spec | `sha512(spec)[:16]` | Dir on disk |
|---|---|---|
| `socraticode@1.16.0` | `482399b050c27a22` | `~/.npm/_npx/482399b050c27a22/` ✓ |
| `socraticode@latest` | `e467c9db50cb633b` | `~/.npm/_npx/e467c9db50cb633b/` ✓ |

Both trees' `package.json` read `{"dependencies":{"socraticode":"^1.16.0"}}`, so contents can't tell them apart. The spec hash can.

## Proposed

- Read the pinned spec from the declared value, `env.SOCRATICODE_SPEC` in `.claude/settings.json` (plain bash/python3, no venv: disk-gc's rule 3). Optionally also read `~/.vscode-server/data/Machine/settings.json` `claudeCode.environmentVariables`, the launch mechanism.
- Compute `sha512(spec)[:16]` and never consider that dir a candidate. Report it as `kept: pinned` so the exemption is visible rather than silent.
- Fail safe: an unreadable or absent spec means no exemption, the same behaviour as today. Never treat it as permission to prune more.
- Superseded pins and `@latest` trees stay prunable. That is the sweep's remaining job.

TDD in `scripts/tests/test_disk_gc.py`:
- an idle tree named by the pinned spec's hash survives `--prune`
- an idle `@latest` tree beside it does not
- a missing or garbled settings file exempts nothing

## Open question

Should the key be the declared value (`.claude/settings.json`) or what actually launched? A re-pin that updates one place but not the other would exempt the wrong tree. Possibly exempt the hash of every spec found in either place.

## Not in scope

The health hook's own uncapped launch is gregoryfoster/skills#330.

item.title: co-status#28: co-usa-wa-backup gains a 'has cleared' notice; failed nights still each report
item.body:
**From co-status ([CannObserv/status#28](https://github.com/CannObserv/status/issues/28)): what `co-usa-wa-backup` sends changes slightly.** It's reviewed and goes out in co-status's next deploy. Nothing to change in code; `RECOVERY.md` says `renotify_seconds` spaces *missing* alerts only; it now also spaces reports, which changes nothing for a nightly job.

A run of `alert` check-ins is now **one fault**. It reports when it opens, then once per `renotify_seconds`, and the next `ok` ends it. For `co-usa-wa-backup` (86400 / 7200 / renotify 86400):

- **Every failed night still reports.** The reminder is due from renotify minus half the interval (12 h here). So two runs 23h50m apart, as `RandomizedDelaySec=10min` allows, both report.
- **New:** the first good night after a failure sends **"[co-status] co-usa-wa-backup has cleared"**, with how long the failure lasted.
- A disabled monitor still reports, de-duplicated the same way.
- A check-in that sends no report still gets a 202 and is recorded, with `dispatches: []`.

**For usa-wa#458** (logging the 202's dispatch ids): a nightly failure is always due a report, so an empty `dispatches` on its `alert` still means nothing went out. notifier never took it, and `GET /api/v1/monitors/{id}` shows `last_report_status: not_accepted`. The one new case is a repeat: a second `alert` within 12 h of a reported one, such as a hand-run retry the same day. That is recorded and sends nothing by design.

Design: [the spec](https://github.com/CannObserv/status/blob/c050407b6cdabfdcb722e930f50ef3a9a190355d/docs/specs/2026-10-09-alert-faults-design.md). Behaviour: [monitors.md § Faults](https://github.com/CannObserv/status/blob/c050407b6cdabfdcb722e930f50ef3a9a190355d/docs/reference/monitors.md#faults).

slot.instructions: `epic` is a GitHub issue that tracks a body of work through a checklist of child issues: `epic.goal` says what it covers, `epic.scope` holds its boundary decisions and rules, `epic.children` its checklist lines (done: ticked), and `epic.parked` what waits on a trigger. `item` is an issue filed since the coordinator last looked, with its state now. Which slot does the coordinator give `item` in this epic?

criteria.child: Work this epic covers and that should be done now or in order: it gets its own checklist line, slotted by dependency. A follow-up to a child, a bug in what a child shipped, or a piece split off a child is a child.
criteria.closed-in-fact: Work this epic covers that is already delivered: the item is closed, or a child's merged change already did it, so it is verified, linked and closed with evidence instead of slotted.
criteria.split: The item mixes work this epic covers with work it doesn't, so the epic's part is filed as its own issue and the rest is left out.
criteria.out of epic: Not this epic's work: another skill, service, area or epic, a record or notice with no action, or tooling around the epic rather than its work. It is said so plainly and cross-linked only where it changes a remaining step.
criteria.duplicate: The same work as an existing child or another open issue, so it is closed in favour of that one.
criteria.park: This epic's concern, but not to be done yet: it waits on a trigger (another repo, a decision, a date, an event) and goes in the parked table with that trigger.

item.title: Seat occupancy as PM sees it: 56 pairs = your 35 + 20 multi-member 1889 Senate + 1 PM-side (#359)
item.body:
Power-map now carries the consumer-side twin of #359's gate (CannObserv/power-map#506): a daily ratchet over two different people holding one single-seat role (`state_senator`, `state_representative`) over strictly overlapping spans. A same-day handoff is not a finding, matching your `is distinct from` boundary rule. Measured on PM production 2026-10-10: **56 pairs**. This lists them against #359's ratchet. #359 shipped at 91, and the gate's baseline is 35 today.

## The short version

| | pairs | yours? |
|---|---|---|
| producer pairs outside the 1889 multi-member Senate | **35** | yes: the same count as `assignments_seat_occupancy.sql`'s baseline of 35 |
| 1889–90 multi-member Senate (LD-2/5/8/18/19) | **20** | lawful; your gate excludes them via the roster, PM can't (see below) |
| dataset row vs a legacy PM row no dataset anchors | **1** | no: PM's own, CannObserv/power-map#639 |

The snapshots PM has landed (`assignments` v20261004, v20261005, v20261009) each give 55 strict overlaps under PM's rule, which is exactly the 35 + 20 above. So PM's live state matches what you publish, and the gap to your 35 is the multi-member exclusion alone.

## Asks

1. **Confirm the 35 are the same 35.** Count equality is not set equality. If your gate's list differs from the first table below, one of us is mis-scoped.
2. **The multi-member Senate needs a published signal (#362).** Both sides key these as one `seat:senate:ld-N` / one PM `state_senator` role, so PM's type-level `occupancy='single'` reads five lawful senators as ten conflicts. Your gate tells them apart from the roster's annotations, which PM never sees. Any of these would let PM stop counting them: a distinct seat kind (as CannObserv/power-map#302 did for the pre-1965 House with `state_representative_at_large`), a per-seat capacity column, or a flag on the span. Until then they sit in PM's baseline as known non-defects.
3. **As #360 drains, PM's count falls with yours.** PM's ratchet fails only on an increase. A lower count passes and says what to lower the baseline to, so no coordination is needed. A *new* pair fails PM's daily unit, and if your gate is green that night, it means the two predicates have diverged.

item.title: House LD-38 Pos. 1: Robinson's span (and her House committee spans) should end 2020-05-13, not 2018-12-31 / 2020-12-31
item.body:
The assignments snapshot gives June Robinson one House span on `seat:house:ld-38:position-1`: **2013-12-16 → 2018-12-31**. She was re-elected in 2018 and held the seat through the 2019–20 biennium, until the Snohomish County Council appointed her to the Senate on **2020-05-13**. Emily Wicks was appointed to her House seat the same day, and the snapshot's Wicks span (2020-05-13 →) is already correct.

Source: leg.wa.gov, [Members of the Washington State Legislature 1889–2023](https://leg.wa.gov/media/e2sngasv/members-of-the-washington-state-legislature-1889-2023.pdf), District 38:
- House: "2013 … June Robinson (Appointed December 16, 2013 to serve unexpired term)", "2019 June Robinson (Resigned; Appntd to the Senate)", "Emily Wicks (Appointed May 13, 2020)"
- Senate: "2019 John McCoy (Resigned April 17, 2020)", "June Robinson (Appointed May 13, 2020; Elected Nov. 3, 2020 to serve unexpired term)"

The Senate spans for McCoy (→ 2020-04-17) and Robinson (2020-05-13 →) already match.

## Ask

1. Extend Robinson's House LD-38 Pos. 1 span to end 2020-05-13, either as one span or as a separate 2019–20 span.
2. Her House committee memberships run past her resignation, ending 2020-12-31. They should end 2020-05-13 too:
   - House Committee on Appropriations (APP), Member, 2015-01-01 →
   - House Committee on Health Care & Wellness (HCW), Member, 2015-01-01 →
   - House Committee on Environment (ENVI), Member, 2019-01-01 →

   PM has pinned all three to 2020-05-13 in its admin overlay. Once the snapshot carries that end date, the pins agree with the dataset.

The same pattern may apply to other members who left the House mid-biennium, if committee spans are built from roster appearances and run to the biennium's end.

## Related: gap, not overlap

John McCoy's House span on the same seat ends 2012-12-31. Per the same roster he held it into the 2013 term, leaving only on his Senate appointment on 2013-11-27: House "2013 John McCoy (Resigned; Appointed to the Senate)"; Senate "John McCoy (Appointed & Sworn in November 27, 2013; to serve unexpired term)".

## PM side

power-map#639: PM had an older row of its own for this tenure (2019-01-01 → 2020-12-31) that no dataset span anchors. It overlapped Wicks, so PM truncated it to end 2020-05-13. Once your span covers 2019 → 2020-05-13, PM will archive that row as superseded. PM's seat-occupancy ratchet baseline is now 55 (power-map#641), matching the snapshot's own count from usa-wa#489.

item.title: 2003-04 House→Senate movers (Delvin, Carrell, Pflug, Berkey) have no House span at all
item.body:
Follow-up from #490 (PR #491).

#491 extends a House→Senate mover's House tenure into the biennium they switch in. It does this by carrying forward the seat they held in the **previous** biennium. Four movers in 2003-04 have no previous-biennium seat to carry, because 2003-04 is the first biennium with House Positions. So they publish **no `chamber-house` span at all**. Their House tenure from 2003-01-01 to their Senate seating is missing, not just cut short. #491 does date their committees.

| Member | Id | LD | Senate seating (event) | Position evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cheryl Pflug | 3479 | 5 | 2004-01-05 | successor Jay Rodne `seated ld-5-position-1` 2004-01-20 → **P1** |
| Jean Berkey | 6765 | 38 | 2004-01-05 | successor David Simpson `seated ld-38-position-2` 2004-01-07 → **P2** |
| Jerome Delvin | 1574 | 8 | 2004-05-12 | successor Sean McGrath (9951), appointed May 18, 2004 per the roster. No event, no span |
| Mike Carrell | 1586 | 28 | 2004-07-06 | successor Bob Lawrence (9960), appointed July 13, 2004 per the roster. No event, no span |

Every one of the four is listed "Resigned; Appointed to the Senate" for 2003 in the roster PDF.

## Why nothing positions them

- `stg_sos_results` starts at the **2008** general, so no 2002 ballot positions 2003-04. Those seats get a Position only from the #118 back-chain, which carries a Position back along a member's continuous tenure.
- A mover is excluded from the 2003-04 roster (#105 (a)), and their tenure ends in 2004, so the back-chain has no tenure to carry back along.

## Wider than the four

LD-8 and LD-28 have **no 2003-04 House span for anyone**. Hankins (167), Talcott (658) and the successors all start at 2005-01-01 or later, if they have a span at all. LD-5 and LD-38 show partial coverage in 2003-04. Check the size of this before choosing a fix. The likely cause is the 2003-04 Position floor rather than anything to do with movers.

## Options

1. **Position from the successor's seating.** When a `seated chamber-house` successor in the move biennium names the seat, that seat is the mover's. This covers Pflug and Berkey today. It also covers Delvin and Carrell once McGrath's and Lawrence's seatings are recorded, with roster-PDF dates and positions from another source.
2. **Stage the 2002 general** from SOS, if their archive has it, so the elimination positions 2003-04 directly. This would also fix the LD-8 and LD-28 incumbents.
3. **Roster-PDF row order.** It follows seat lineage in 93.1% of district-years (see `docs/specs/2026-08-14-wsl-roster-pdf-source-design.md`), but that is inference, not fact.

## Constraints

- `assignments_seat_occupancy` must not rise above its baseline of 35.
- A minted span's key must be stable across rebuilds.

item.title: Record McGrath (LD-8) and Lawrence (LD-28) 2004 House seatings so Delvin and Carrell get House spans
item.body:
Follow-up from #492 (PR #494).

#494 positions a House→Senate mover with no ballot seat and no prior seat from the seat a successor was appointed to mid-biennium in the mover's LD. Two of #492's four movers are still uncovered, because their successors' seatings are not recorded as operator events:

| Mover | Id | LD | Senate seating (event) | Successor | Appointed (roster PDF) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Jerome Delvin | 1574 | 8 | 2004-05-12 | Sean McGrath (9951) | 2004-05-18 |
| Mike Carrell | 1586 | 28 | 2004-07-06 | Bob Lawrence (9960) | 2004-07-13 |

## Work

1. Find an evidenced **Position** for each successor's appointment, for example a county commissioners' appointment record, a House journal entry, or the 2004 SOS results if they can be found outside the 404'd archive. The roster PDF gives dates but not Positions. Row order is inference, not fact (see #492, option 3).
2. Record `seated chamber-house ld-8-position-N` (McGrath) and `ld-28-position-N` (Lawrence) operator events with their evidence URLs.
3. Next nightly: Delvin and Carrell each gain one `chamber-house` span (2003-01-01 → Senate seating), with `via=successor` in `chamber_move_house_tenure_carried`. No code change is expected.

## Constraints

- `assignments_seat_occupancy` must stay at its baseline of 35.
- The other 2003-04 House member in each LD (Hankins 167 in LD-8, Talcott 658 in LD-28) is unpositioned in 2003-04 today. If either left mid-biennium before the successor was seated, #494's peer-exit guard refuses the inference. Check this before recording the events.
- The wider gap, LD-8 and LD-28 having no 2003-04 House spans at all, is #140's.

item.title: Adopt patching-hosts: commit the knob, then take the first monthly run under the skill (gregoryfoster/skills#313)
item.body:
## Adopting `patching-hosts`: the knob, then the first monthly run under the skill

`patching-hosts` v1 is done (gregoryfoster/skills#313, closed 2026-10-14). Five hosts ran it end to end, and every rough edge they found is fixed upstream:
- replicator (CannObserv/replicator#131);
- wslcb-licensing-tracker (CannObserv/wslcb-licensing-tracker#192);
- co-index (CannObserv/index#9);
- notifier (CannObserv/notifier#113);
- broker (CannObserv/broker#67).

Between them they covered no data store, Postgres, Qdrant and Redis. This host adopts the skill at its first monthly run, the decision recorded on gregoryfoster/skills#313 on 2026-10-13. This issue tracks that adoption. Its step 0 hand-run is #430.

### What's particular to this host
Read in the step 0 run (2026-09-26). Re-read each one, since a month has passed.
- **The May-2026 image.** The probe calls it `may-2026`: it has `exe-setup.service`, but no `/usr/local/bin/exeuntu`. Its boot empties `/tmp` (Ubuntu's `D` rule). `reboot-chain.sh` lists anything staged there before the reboot.
- **A local PostgreSQL 16:** `datastore postgres <unit> <database>...`. It's a held step by default (`postgres`). In step 0 it was down 2.30 s, and the API recovered by itself 0.32 s later. The API uses asyncpg, so it maps no libpq.
- **The backlog:** step 0 selected 185 security updates against lists 71 days old. The skill counts from the dry run's own selection, never from a `grep` of `apt list`.
- **A reboot is likely.** PID 1 had 10 `(deleted)` mappings after step 0's apply.
- **Callers:** a `caller` line for each public repo whose service calls the API. A private one is left out, with a comment, and told by hand.
- **The vendored copy is already at `d5f984e`**, so step 1 is the link, plus a bump to `85caed2` for the plan and README changes. Nothing under `skills/` changed between the two.

### Steps
1. **Vendor the skill.** Bump `skills-vendor/gregoryfoster-skills` from `d5f984e` to `85caed2` or later (upstream `main`), and link `patching-hosts` the way the other skills are linked. Commit, and record the commit you took.
2. **Commit `.skills/patching-hosts`.** Its grammar is the skill's `references/knob.md`, and the lines above are where to start.
   - Set `class production`, `posture scheduled`, and a `window` the owner gives. A window given in Pacific time moves with DST: DST ends 2026-11-01.
   - **Leave out `image-owner`.** This repo is public and the image repo isn't, so the line would publish its name. That waits for gregoryfoster/skills#350. Nothing reads the line yet.
   - Check it with `read-knob.sh --host "$(hostname)"`. It should report no malformed lines, and the host shouldn't be report-only.
   - Pinning the knob's decisions in a test, as broker's `tests/deploy/test_patching_knob.py` does, makes later knob changes red first.
3. **Probe, read-only.** Run `probe.sh --refresh-into <scratch>`, with `--dry-run-into <scratch>` for the exact security count. Settle each finding: fix it, or declare it with `exception <what> <review-by> <reason>`. Record the pending set by class here, the sixth class (language dependencies) included.
4. **The first monthly run, in the window.** Follow the skill's SKILL.md, "The run":
   - the recovery point, attested off the node before the apply;
   - the gated apply, maintenance lane included, with each hold group as its own step;
   - the reboot only through `reboot-chain.sh`, and only if the probe or needrestart calls for one;
   - then `probe.sh --post-boot --run <run dir>`.

   **The owner approves each step in this repo's session.**
5. **File every problem with the skill in gregoryfoster/skills,** with the owner's approval. Give the command, its output and what was expected. Never edit the vendored copy.
6. **Record and log.** Record the run on this issue. Then draft the process-log entry (SKILL.md step 7) and send it upstream as an issue. It holds counts and package families, never versions.

**Done when** the knob reads clean, one monthly run has completed under the skill with its record here, and each problem it found is filed upstream with its process-log entry drafted.

No credentials, passwords, digests or bucket keys go in this issue or its comments.

slot.instructions: `epic` is a GitHub issue that tracks a body of work through a checklist of child issues: `epic.goal` says what it covers, `epic.scope` holds its boundary decisions and rules, `epic.children` its checklist lines (done: ticked), and `epic.parked` what waits on a trigger. `item` is an issue filed since the coordinator last looked, with its state now. Which slot does the coordinator give `item` in this epic?

criteria.child: Work this epic covers and that should be done now or in order: it gets its own checklist line, slotted by dependency. A follow-up to a child, a bug in what a child shipped, or a piece split off a child is a child.
criteria.closed-in-fact: Work this epic covers that is already delivered: the item is closed, or a child's merged change already did it, so it is verified, linked and closed with evidence instead of slotted.
criteria.split: The item mixes work this epic covers with work it doesn't, so the epic's part is filed as its own issue and the rest is left out.
criteria.out of epic: Not this epic's work: another skill, service, area or epic, a record or notice with no action, or tooling around the epic rather than its work. It is said so plainly and cross-linked only where it changes a remaining step.
criteria.duplicate: The same work as an existing child or another open issue, so it is closed in favour of that one.
criteria.park: This epic's concern, but not to be done yet: it waits on a trigger (another repo, a decision, a date, an event) and goes in the parked table with that trigger.
