item.title: Language dependencies: 42 OSV advisories in uv.lock, and no update mechanism (#497)
item.body:
Raised by #497's probe (the patching-hosts skill's sixth class, language dependencies), 2026-10-14.

## What the probe read
`uv audit --frozen` on a copy of `uv.lock` (OSV), as the lockfile's owner: **42 advisories across 9 packages**. The tree serves `usa-wa.service` and every `usa-wa-*` oneshot.

| Package | Advisories |
|---|---|
| urllib3 (1.26 line) | 14 |
| virtualenv | 8 |
| urllib3 (2.x line) | 6 |
| anyio | 4 |
| starlette | 4 |
| pytest | 2 |
| zeep | 2 |
| mako | 1 |
| pydantic-settings | 1 |

Counts and families only; advisory IDs and fixed versions come from `uv audit` on the branch that fixes them. The OS lane patches none of these: a wheel carries its own code.

## The gap
Nothing updates this tree: no Dependabot or Renovate config, no audit gate in CI (`.github/workflows/` holds only `context-cadence.yml`).

## To do
- [ ] Bump each advised package where a fix exists; find what pins urllib3 1.26 (likely `zeep`/`requests` transitive) and whether it can move.
- [ ] `uv audit` gate: in `pre-ship.sh` or CI, failing on new advisories, with a declared allowlist for any that can't move.
- [ ] Decide Dependabot (uv ecosystem) vs. the gate alone.
- [ ] Deploy takes a window: `uv sync --locked` + `systemctl restart usa-wa` is a restart of a declared `service` (the skill's policy.md, decided on notifier). Fold into a monthly window or take an out-of-cycle one for an advisory that warrants it.

item.title: Adopt the coordinating-epics skill for #414
item.body:
`coordinating-epics` v1 shipped in gregoryfoster/skills (gregoryfoster/skills#348, `fef0611`). It packages the protocol #414's coordinator has run by hand. This issue moves #414 onto it.

**What v1 brings**
- `epic-edit.sh`: one guarded call per body edit. It refuses foreign edits against a saved baseline (a tick you have verified passes with `--accept-ticks`), anchors each operation by ref, derives checkbox counts, lints refs, placeholders and secrets, compare-and-swaps before the PATCH, and reads the body back.
- `scan.sh`: the three re-scan cursors (number watermark, updated-since, and the commit range attributed to children), the epic's own new comments, and cross-repo ref states, as JSON.
- `assets/epic-template.md`: the header cursor lines both scripts read.

**Steps**
1. **Vendor it.** `skills-vendor/gregoryfoster-skills` is at `85caed2`, which predates the skill. Bump it to `fef0611` or later, then symlink `skills/coordinating-epics` and `.claude/skills/coordinating-epics` (managing-skills, Step 2/2b). The auto-refresh hook bumps the pointer but creates no symlinks.
2. **Adopt at the next check-in, as that check-in's one write** (SKILL.md, "Adopt an epic that exists"). Run `scan.sh --repo CannObserv/usa-wa --epic 414 --since <the last check-in, with a zone> --watermark <the last number the epic accounts for> --from-sha <last verified SHA>`. Then make one `epic-edit.sh --repo CannObserv/usa-wa --epic 414 --adopt-live --scan <report> --ops <file>` call, dry-run first, with `header` ops for `Last check-in` (`{checked}`), `Last issue seen` (`{last_seen}`) and `Last verified SHA`, a `replace-section` on "Order" and an `add-section` "Log". The epic has no cursor lines yet, so `scan.sh` needs all three cursors passed this once.
3. **After that,** every body edit goes through `epic-edit.sh`, and each check-in starts with `scan.sh`.

**What a dry run on today's body found** (a copy of the body, run against the fake `gh` in the skill's tests; nothing was written):
- **32 of the 42 checklist items lead with an ordinal, not their ref** (`- [x] 12. #447 …`). The editor finds lines by their leading ref, so a `tick #475` is refused as "no checklist item leads with it". Re-lead them in the adoption call with a `replace-section` on "Order", the ref first and the ordinal after it (`- [x] #447 (12) …`). Every line of that section is then linted, so qualify the short refs it holds, such as `power-map#592`, in the same rewrite.
- **#451 leads two checklist items,** one under "Absorbed from #302" and one under "Time-gated", so any op on #451 is refused as ambiguous. Reword one so it doesn't lead with #451.
- **The epic has no header cursor lines yet.** The three `header` ops add them as a list after the opening paragraph, and the call applies cleanly.
- **There is no `## Log` section,** and the `log` op writes only to one. Add it with `add-section` "Log", passing the adoption's log line as its text.

**Known limits in v1:** CI by job is still checked by hand (gregoryfoster/skills#394), and comments are not linted before posting (gregoryfoster/skills#395).

**When the run ends:** journal it in the skill's process log. The skill is vendored here, so draft the entry in this repo and file it upstream as an issue on gregoryfoster/skills ("Adding an entry" in `references/process-log.md`).

slot.instructions: `epic` is a GitHub issue that tracks a body of work through a checklist of child issues: `epic.goal` says what it covers, `epic.scope` holds its boundary decisions and rules, `epic.children` its checklist lines (done: ticked), and `epic.parked` what waits on a trigger. `item` is an issue filed since the coordinator last looked, with its state now. Which slot does the coordinator give `item` in this epic?

criteria.child: Work this epic covers and that should be done now or in order: it gets its own checklist line, slotted by dependency. A follow-up to a child, a bug in what a child shipped, or a piece split off a child is a child.
criteria.closed-in-fact: Work this epic covers that is already delivered: the item is closed, or a child's merged change already did it, so it is verified, linked and closed with evidence instead of slotted.
criteria.split: The item mixes work this epic covers with work it doesn't, so the epic's part is filed as its own issue and the rest is left out.
criteria.out of epic: Not this epic's work: another skill, service, area or epic, a record or notice with no action, or tooling around the epic rather than its work. It is said so plainly and cross-linked only where it changes a remaining step.
criteria.duplicate: The same work as an existing child or another open issue, so it is closed in favour of that one.
criteria.park: This epic's concern, but not to be done yet: it waits on a trigger (another repo, a decision, a date, an event) and goes in the parked table with that trigger.

item.title: SCHEMA_VERSION 2.1.0: one spec and one lockstep release (#384, #369, #362, #360 increment 2)
item.body:
Tracks the one `SCHEMA_VERSION` 2.0.0 → 2.1.0 release the owner decided on 2026-10-13 (#414, "Decisions (2026-10-13)"). Everything in it is additive, and **`role_key`s don't change**. If the spec finds they must, the release becomes 3.0.0, and that is an owner decision.

## Scope (each decision is on its own issue)

| Issue | Adds | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| #384 | `persons.name_own`: a curated adjudication table, 9 non-null rows | https://github.com/CannObserv/usa-wa/issues/384#issuecomment-6150927129 |
| #369 | `assignments.start_basis` + `end_basis` (`dated \| observed \| open`) | https://github.com/CannObserv/usa-wa/issues/369#issuecomment-6151785233 |
| #362 | general seat model (Popolo / OCD `Post` + `Membership`): `roles` gains the districting plan, a seat label and `max_holders`; `assignments.membership_type`; the invariant principals ≤ `max_holders`, read by the clipping too. Absorbs #230 and #479 | https://github.com/CannObserv/usa-wa/issues/362#issuecomment-6154717471 |
| #360 (increment 2) | `assignments.valid_from_latest` + `valid_to_earliest`, dense; a two-tier occupancy gate | https://github.com/CannObserv/usa-wa/issues/360#issuecomment-6155261308 |

## Phases

1. **Spec** in `docs/specs/`: one design for all four, with #369's basis columns and #360's interval columns defined together so they can't contradict each other. **Send it to power-map for review before the shape is fixed**, since `roles` is their matching surface and `max_holders` generalises their `occupancy` type.
2. **While power-map reviews:** #360 part A, the named-pair accepted list and adjudication of the 35. It's a separate child on #414, with no schema change.
3. **Build and one lockstep deploy:** datapackage fields and `serving.*` models together (`verify_contract`), plus `docs/API.md` notes.

**Done when** v2.1.0 datasets are published and served, power-map has acknowledged the release, and #384, #369 and #362 are closed, along with #360 once its part A has also landed.

item.title: usa-wa.service: every restart logs "Failed with result 'exit-code'" (status=143 from the uv run wrapper) — add SuccessExitStatus=143
item.body:
From #499's close-out ("For any future usa-wa.service unit change").

## What happens [measured]

Both `usa-wa` restarts this month logged the stop as a failure:

```
2026-10-16T04:30:15Z usa-wa.service: Main process exited, code=exited, status=143/n/a
2026-10-16T04:30:15Z usa-wa.service: Failed with result 'exit-code'.
2026-10-16T14:03:08Z usa-wa.service: Main process exited, code=exited, status=143/n/a
2026-10-16T14:03:08Z usa-wa.service: Failed with result 'exit-code'.
```

uvicorn shuts down cleanly each time ("Application shutdown complete", "Finished server process"). The 143 (128 + SIGTERM) comes from the `uv run` wrapper in `ExecStart=`, which reports the signal it was stopped with. The same thing was seen on 2026-09-27.

## Why fix it
- **Every restart reads as a failure** in `journalctl` and `systemctl status`, which is noise for anyone reading the log, including the patching-hosts post-boot probe and the coordinator's deploy checks.
- **It's a trap for later:** `usa-wa.service` has no `OnFailure=` today, so nothing alerts. If someone adds one (the #49 alerting chain), every deploy and every patch-window restart would send a failure email.

## Fix
- In `deploy/usa-wa.service`, add `SuccessExitStatus=143` with a comment explaining why (the `uv run` wrapper reports SIGTERM).
- **Check the oneshots too.** Every `usa-wa-*` unit runs through `uv run --frozen --no-sync`. A timer job stopped mid-run (by a patch window or a reboot chain) may log 143 the same way, and those units do have `OnFailure=`. Measure before changing them: a SIGTERM to a oneshot is a real interruption, and might be worth alerting on.
- A test beside `scripts/tests/test_unit_ordering.py` that pins the directive.
- **Host steps:**
  1. `sudo cp deploy/usa-wa.service /etc/systemd/system/`
  2. `sudo systemctl daemon-reload`
  3. `sudo systemctl restart usa-wa`
  4. confirm the stop now logs `Deactivated successfully` instead of `Failed with result 'exit-code'`.

Small, with no behaviour change beyond the log line.

item.title: Cohort disk GC: disk-gc.sh is the proposed starting point for one shared implementation (provisioner#61)
item.body:
**Context:** six cohort hosts each built their own root-disk GC. **CannObserv/provisioner#61** proposes one canonical host-tooling GC + headroom sensor in co-image-base, and **gregoryfoster/skills#425** proposes a skill to adopt it on hosts not yet on the image. This repo's implementation is in the comparison table there, so please weigh in on #61, especially if your rules differ.

**When it lands:** adopt the canonical files and retire the local implementation.

**Here:** `scripts/disk-gc.sh` + `usa-wa-disk-gc.timer`. It is the most rigorous of the six, and provisioner#61 suggests it as the base.

**Worth checking now** (found on another host, may apply here):
- #485's open question (declared vs launched spec) has an answer from power-map: the launch reads the VS Code machine setting, so exempt **both** hashes (CannObserv/power-map#665 CR 2).
- A bare `uv cache prune` **waits forever** while any other uv process holds the cache, e.g. a service run by `uv run`. Reproduced against a scratch cache. The fix is `uv cache prune --force` (CannObserv/power-map#665, CR 1). If yours runs without `--force` beside a long-running `uv run`, it never completes. (Only relevant if a uv-cache tier is added.)

slot.instructions: `epic` is a GitHub issue that tracks a body of work through a checklist of child issues: `epic.goal` says what it covers, `epic.scope` holds its boundary decisions and rules, `epic.children` its checklist lines (done: ticked), and `epic.parked` what waits on a trigger. `item` is an issue filed since the coordinator last looked, with its state now. Which slot does the coordinator give `item` in this epic?

criteria.child: Work this epic covers and that should be done now or in order: it gets its own checklist line, slotted by dependency. A follow-up to a child, a bug in what a child shipped, or a piece split off a child is a child.
criteria.closed-in-fact: Work this epic covers that is already delivered: the item is closed, or a child's merged change already did it, so it is verified, linked and closed with evidence instead of slotted.
criteria.split: The item mixes work this epic covers with work it doesn't, so the epic's part is filed as its own issue and the rest is left out.
criteria.out of epic: Not this epic's work: another skill, service, area or epic, a record or notice with no action, or tooling around the epic rather than its work. It is said so plainly and cross-linked only where it changes a remaining step.
criteria.duplicate: The same work as an existing child or another open issue, so it is closed in favour of that one.
criteria.park: This epic's concern, but not to be done yet: it waits on a trigger (another repo, a decision, a date, an event) and goes in the parked table with that trigger.

item.title: DEPLOYMENT.md lifecycle table: four 'After editing deploy/<unit>' rows omit the sudo cp, so following them deploys nothing
item.body:
From #505's close-out ("Unfiled doc drift"), confirmed and widened by the #414 coordinator on 2026-10-16 [measured on `origin/main` `48e558e`].

`docs/DEPLOYMENT.md`'s lifecycle table says "After editing `deploy/<unit>`", followed by the commands. Units are installed as root-owned **copies** (AGENTS.md: "`sudo cp deploy/<unit> /etc/systemd/system/` before `daemon-reload` — reload alone re-reads the stale copy and deploys nothing"). Four rows leave out the copy, so following them deploys nothing:

| Row | Says today |
|---|---|
| `deploy/usa-wa-integrity-sweep.{service,timer}` | `sudo systemctl daemon-reload && sudo systemctl restart usa-wa-integrity-sweep.timer` |
| `deploy/usa-wa-roster-pdf-recheck.{service,timer}` | `sudo systemctl daemon-reload && sudo systemctl restart usa-wa-roster-pdf-recheck.timer` |
| `deploy/usa-wa-disk-gc.{service,timer}` | `sudo systemctl daemon-reload && sudo systemctl restart usa-wa-disk-gc.timer` |
| `deploy/usa-wa-notify-failure@.service` | `sudo systemctl daemon-reload` (not in #505's list) |

The `usa-wa.service`, `usa-wa-pipeline`, `usa-wa-wsl-availability-probe` and `usa-wa-backup` rows already include `sudo cp …`. #505 fixed `usa-wa.service`'s.

## Fix
- Prefix each of the four with `sudo cp deploy/<unit…> /etc/systemd/system/ &&`, in the same shape as the `usa-wa-backup` row.
- **A guard so it can't drift again:** a test that every "After editing `deploy/X`" row's command contains `sudo cp deploy/X` (or the brace form). `scripts/tests/` already parses `deploy/`; `test_unit_ordering.py` is the nearest template.

Docs and a test only; there are no host steps. Small.

item.title: disk-gc: grace window reads mtime only — VS Code restores archive mtimes, so a fresh CLI reads weeks old; find errors fail open
item.body:
## Summary
`recently_touched()` in `scripts/disk-gc.sh` reads **mtime only**. VS Code's extractor restores archive mtimes, so a build or CLI downloaded a minute ago can read as weeks old, and the grace window (#394 / #485) won't protect it. The function also **fails open**: if `find` hits an error, the tree counts as settled. Found while porting the grace window to power-map's prune (CannObserv/power-map#669, shipped in CannObserv/power-map#670).

## Where (`d04ecea5`)
`scripts/disk-gc.sh:202-208`:
```bash
recently_touched() {
    ...
    [ -n "$(find "$1" -mmin "-$GRACE_MINUTES" -print -quit 2>/dev/null)" ]
}
```
`consider()` calls it for `vscode-server` (`cli/servers/Stable-*`), `vscode-cli` (`code-*`), `vscode-extension`, `plugin-cache` and `npx-cache`.

## Evidence (measured on the power-map VM, 2026-10-16)
| path | mtime | ctime (when it landed) |
|---|---|---|
| `~/.vscode-server/code-07f806f9…` (CLI, a plain file) | 2026-09-30 09:04:44.**000000000** | 2026-10-04 16:55:01 |
| `cli/servers/Stable-6d62b1d5…/server/node` | 2026-09-07 23:56:43.**000000000** | 2026-10-15 09:30:01 |
| `cli/servers/Stable-6d62b1d5…/` (dir) | 2026-10-15 09:30:00 | 2026-10-15 09:30:03 |

The zero nanoseconds show the mtimes came from the archive. npm left real mtimes on `_npx/<hash>` (both clocks 2026-09-27), so the npx tier is not affected today.

## Consequences
1. **`vscode-cli`: the grace window can't protect a CLI that just landed.** A `code-*` CLI is a single file, so `find code-x -mmin -60` checks only that file's archive mtime. A CLI downloaded during the run reads as days old, and it's a candidate as soon as no process names it. That is the gap between download and exec, exactly what the window exists for.
2. **`vscode-server`: protected today only by accident.** Files under a new build read as weeks old. `find` still matches, but only because the extractor leaves *directory* mtimes alone. If an extractor update restored those too, the build would read as settled.
3. **Fails open.** `2>/dev/null` plus an empty-output test means an unreadable subtree (EACCES, or a tree vanishing mid-walk) gives "not recent", unless some readable entry happens to match first. The tree becomes a candidate even though nobody could tell whether it was still being written.

## Suggested fix
- Test ctime as well as mtime. ctime can't be backdated by `utime`, and restoring an mtime moves ctime to now:
  `find "$1" \( -mmin "-$GRACE_MINUTES" -o -cmin "-$GRACE_MINUTES" \) -print -quit`
- Withhold when `find` exits non-zero, rather than discarding its errors. For example, capture the exit status, and on a failure return 0 (recent) with a reason recorded in the withheld list.
- Tests: a fixture tree (and a single file) with every mtime backdated (`touch -d 2020-01-01`) must still be withheld right after creation. A mode-000 subdir must be withheld, not listed as a candidate.

## How power-map did it, for reference
`scripts/prune_disk.py` `withhold_reason()` takes `max(st_mtime, st_ctime)`. It checks the path's own `lstat`, then walks directories only and stops at the first recent entry; that's enough because each file created moves its parent dir's ctime. It withholds on any unreadable entry or a 100 000-dir bound. Under `--execute`, an unchecked withhold exits 1, so a tree that can never be checked still pages instead of sitting quietly.

## Cohort
CannObserv/provisioner#61 / gregoryfoster/skills#425 (shared GC): whatever lands there should use the ctime clock and withhold on errors.

item.title: Roster backfill wrote three seated events that never held; the parse merges successor rows (Raugust, M. B. Happy lost)
item.body:
Found during #360 part A ([comment](https://github.com/CannObserv/usa-wa/issues/360#issuecomment-6234759456)). It's the #468 class: three `seated` operator events written by the `roster-pdf-backfill` that never held. Two roster parse defects sit behind them, and one of those drops whole tenures. Measured on the 2026-10-17 build against roster edition `legroster:2025-06-05`.

## 1. Three events to retract

| event id | event | what the roster says (2025 ed.) | published effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| `01a031bd-5449-71da-ee74-d5403541650e` | `jhrobertson:1943` seated LD-8 1949-08-25 | p.39: *"J. H. Robertson (Resigned August 24, 1949; Appointed Employment Security Commissioner)"*. The next row is *"W. C. Raugust (Appointed August 25, 1949 to serve 1950 Ex. S.)"* | **Phantom.** `seat:senate:ld-8` J. H. Robertson 1949-08-25 → 1950-12-31, plus his party span to 1950-12-31 |
| `01a031bd-5524-992f-0dcc-d3a78067bf92` | `francispearson:1937` seated LD-24 1957-04-01 | p.84: *"Resigned; Appointed to the Public Service Commission, April 1, 1957"*. The date belongs to an external office | none (absorbed) |
| `01a011df-c8bc-4c3e-1ad2-a89d73b7985d` | `11998` (Rolfes) seated LD-23 2023-08-23 | p.81: the date is Drew Hansen's appointment, merged into her annotation | none (her `departed 2023-08-15` wins) |

Simulated with the write-free rebuild: retracting all three changes exactly two rows, both Robertson's.
- `seat:senate:ld-8|…|1949-50`: 1949-08-25 → 1950-12-31 **becomes** 1949-01-01 → 1949-08-24
- `party-role:republican|…|1943-44`: ends 1950-12-31 **becomes** ends 1949-08-24

So retraction alone **isn't enough**. Robertson still publishes nothing for 1947-01-01 → 1948-12-31, because his own row still carries Raugust's "Appointed August 25, 1949" and projects as a successor opening in 1949-50. That's §2.

Pearson's resignation is also dated by that annotation. A `departed`/`resigned` 1957-04-01 is a fair reading, but it's a separate, judgment-call record. It would move his end from the derived 1957-06-06 to 1957-04-01 and resolve no gate pair.

## 2. The parse merges a successor's row into the predecessor's annotation

`stg_roster_members` has 4 annotations containing `) (`, where two PDF rows were joined:

| roster row | lost row (PDF) | effect |
|---|---|---|
| 1947 Senate LD-8 J. H. Robertson | **W. C. Raugust**, appointed Aug 25, 1949 (p.39) | Raugust's 1949–50 tenure is published as Robertson's (§1). Raugust appears only from 1951. Robertson loses 1947–48 |
| 1959 Senate LD-6 John H. Happy | **Mrs. Marjorie B. Happy**, appointed 1962 (p.34) | absent from `persons` entirely. LD-6 shows a vacancy from 1962-06-21 to the end of 1962 |
| 1987 House LD-18 Joe Tanner | **David Cooper**, appointed Dec 12, 1986 (p.69) | no published effect today (pre-2001 House isn't spanned), but the record is wrong |
| 2021 Senate LD-23 Christine Rolfes | **Drew Hansen**, appointed Aug 23, 2023 (p.81) | covered by the WSL wire, but it produced the §1 event |

The shape: the PDF wraps a two-line annotation, and the continuation's left column carries the next member's name. ARCHITECTURE.md's second rule applies here (never key a parser on an exact upstream string), so the fix belongs in row segmentation, not in matching on `) (`.

## Suggested approach

- [ ] Fix the row segmentation so all 4 successors parse as their own rows. Pin a test on each of the 4 PDF excerpts. Re-measure the `) (` count (expect 0) and the persons count (expect +1, Marjorie B. Happy).
- [ ] Retract the three events (`operators.cli --retract <id> --evidence-url <page>`). The retraction evidence is the page above.
- [ ] Sweep: re-check every live `roster-pdf-backfill` `seated` event against its **own** row's clause. A seating date must come from an `Appointed`/`Sworn in` clause on the member's own row, not a merged one and not an external office. #468's sweep matched by surname and date, which is how these three passed.
- [ ] List every changed published row in the PR, before and after (the #282 lesson).

## Related, not this issue

- #360 accepted pair #35 (Couplin, LD-9 1921, *"Elected and subsequently resigned without serving"*): a whole span that shouldn't exist, and no event kind removes one.

slot.instructions: `epic` is a GitHub issue that tracks a body of work through a checklist of child issues: `epic.goal` says what it covers, `epic.scope` holds its boundary decisions and rules, `epic.children` its checklist lines (done: ticked), and `epic.parked` what waits on a trigger. `item` is an issue filed since the coordinator last looked, with its state now. Which slot does the coordinator give `item` in this epic?

criteria.child: Work this epic covers and that should be done now or in order: it gets its own checklist line, slotted by dependency. A follow-up to a child, a bug in what a child shipped, or a piece split off a child is a child.
criteria.closed-in-fact: Work this epic covers that is already delivered: the item is closed, or a child's merged change already did it, so it is verified, linked and closed with evidence instead of slotted.
criteria.split: The item mixes work this epic covers with work it doesn't, so the epic's part is filed as its own issue and the rest is left out.
criteria.out of epic: Not this epic's work: another skill, service, area or epic, a record or notice with no action, or tooling around the epic rather than its work. It is said so plainly and cross-linked only where it changes a remaining step.
criteria.duplicate: The same work as an existing child or another open issue, so it is closed in favour of that one.
criteria.park: This epic's concern, but not to be done yet: it waits on a trigger (another repo, a decision, a date, an event) and goes in the parked table with that trigger.

item.title: Seat spans merge a member's return tenure around the interim holder (4 accepted occupancy pairs; the gate cites closed #267)
item.body:
Four of the 35 accepted seat-occupancy pairs (`dbt/seeds/accepted_seat_overlaps.csv`, reason `merged_tenure`) are **return tenures published as one span**. A member served, left, and came back; the span covers both stints plus the gap, so it wraps around whoever held the seat in between.

| #360 pair | Member | Two tenures merged | Wrapped around |
|---|---|---|---|
| #14 | Kathryn E. Malstrom, LD-27 | 1933–36 + 1938–44 | Harry H. Brown (1937) |
| #30 | Harry A. Binzer, LD-42 | before and after military service | Thomas R. Waters |
| #31 | Harry A. Binzer, LD-42 | (same span) | Ralph C. Tenney |
| #34 | W. C. McCoy, LD-9 | 1913–16 + a 1917 return | Dr. W. W. Brand |

Source: #360 part A's build report (`For #267:`).

**Why a new issue.** The gate's comment (`dbt/tests/assignments_seat_occupancy.sql:25`, `merged_tenure … (#267)`) and the #360 notes point at **#267**. But #267 was closed on 2026-08-24, and it's about something else: a person-scoped `departed` truncating the party span of a resign-and-return member. So the split of these spans has no open issue. This is it. Update the SQL comment's reference here when this lands.

**Shape of the fix (to design):** the roster family merges consecutive observations into one span (`build_tenure_spans`). A return after a dated `departed`/`vacated` should open a new span, which means a new span_key keyed at the return biennium. Check whether #226's fix (the party side of the same resign-and-return shape) already gives the seat side a hook.

**When a split lands:** remove the four seed rows **in the same PR**, or `assignments_seat_occupancy_stale` warns. List every changed `assignments` row, before and after; the splits re-key, so power-map sees retractions plus new rows.

Not urgent. These are lawful-looking overlaps already on the accepted list, and nothing errors.

slot.instructions: `epic` is a GitHub issue that tracks a body of work through a checklist of child issues: `epic.goal` says what it covers, `epic.scope` holds its boundary decisions and rules, `epic.children` its checklist lines (done: ticked), and `epic.parked` what waits on a trigger. `item` is an issue filed since the coordinator last looked, with its state now. Which slot does the coordinator give `item` in this epic?

criteria.child: Work this epic covers and that should be done now or in order: it gets its own checklist line, slotted by dependency. A follow-up to a child, a bug in what a child shipped, or a piece split off a child is a child.
criteria.closed-in-fact: Work this epic covers that is already delivered: the item is closed, or a child's merged change already did it, so it is verified, linked and closed with evidence instead of slotted.
criteria.split: The item mixes work this epic covers with work it doesn't, so the epic's part is filed as its own issue and the rest is left out.
criteria.out of epic: Not this epic's work: another skill, service, area or epic, a record or notice with no action, or tooling around the epic rather than its work. It is said so plainly and cross-linked only where it changes a remaining step.
criteria.duplicate: The same work as an existing child or another open issue, so it is closed in favour of that one.
criteria.park: This epic's concern, but not to be done yet: it waits on a trigger (another repo, a decision, a date, an event) and goes in the parked table with that trigger.

item.title: Operator events: a member-wide departed dated at a move to the other chamber closes the new tenure; add a sweep check (#514's Hurley case)
item.body:
From #514 (PR #516), "For later backfill or proposer work (no issue yet)".

**What happened:** the roster backfill wrote `margarethurley:1953 departed 1979-11-28`. She resigned from the **House into the Senate**, and `departed` is person-scoped: it closes *every* open span. Once her Senate row existed (the #514 parse fix), that event would have ended her Senate tenure on the day it began. #514 retracted it. It was caught by a manual sweep, not by any check.

**The class:** a member-wide `departed` dated at a move to the other chamber. The right shape is a seat-scoped `vacated` on the old seat (plus a `seated` on the new one where needed), as ONTOLOGY.md § The operator event shapes describes for a chamber move.

**A check that catches it** [stated, #514]: a `departed` member with an other-chamber roster row whose term covers the event date. On the 2026-10-18 data it finds Hurley plus two false positives, both judged legitimate in #514:
- Klinefelter, who never took his House seat;
- Huntley, whose 1965 → 1967 gap is a real return.

**Proposed:**
- Add the check to the backfill proposer or a pipeline probe, reporting by name with a declared allowlist for the two (stale entries reported, the #452/#360 pattern).
- Run it once over the live events. Expect 0 after #514's retraction, or report what it finds.

Small. A guard against a recurrence, with no data change expected.

item.title: Install provisioner#62's LogTarget drop-in on this host: PID1's lines leave the journal after the first daemon-reload
item.body:
**Size:** XS. This body is the brief (coordinator, #414 check-in 2026-10-19).

## Why

After the first `daemon-reload` since boot, systemd's own lines (`Started`, `Failed with result`, `Deactivated successfully`) leave the journal on this VM. The image's exeuntu `container-overrides.conf` sets `LogTarget=console`, so a reload sends them to `hvc0` instead. They stay out of the journal until the next boot.

Measured 2026-10-19:
- `systemd-analyze get-log-target` prints `console`;
- `/etc/systemd/system.conf.d/` holds only `container-overrides.conf`.

CannObserv/provisioner#62 fixed this in the cohort image (`d2bdd36`) with a one-setting drop-in. It leaves hosts that predate that image to their own repos. On `co-provisioner`, an older-image host, the same drop-in measured working after a `daemon-reload`: `get-log-target` read `journal-or-kmsg`, and a check unit's `Started` and `Deactivated` lines reached `journalctl -u`.

**Decided 2026-10-19 (owner):** install it here, before #501's build, so release night has PID1's lines.

## The file

It must be byte-identical to provisioner's `image/rootfs/etc/systemd/system.conf.d/zz-cannobserv-log-target.conf` at `d2bdd36`, sha256 `0f16a1e6986d15ebb8d40999e05980ce0ce386d0cb8c1b8efa55881b478cb54d`:

```ini
# #62: keep PID1's own lines in the journal after a daemon-reload.
# exeuntu's container-overrides.conf sets LogTarget=console, which a reload
# applies: from then until the next boot, PID1 writes only to hvc0. exe-init's
# --log-target=syslog holds only until that first reload. Drop-ins sort by name
# across every system.conf.d, and a later one wins per setting: zz- sorts after
# exeuntu's, and only LogTarget= is set, so its other settings stay its own.
[Manager]
LogTarget=journal-or-kmsg
```

Keep the name and the bytes. The `#62` in its comment means provisioner's issue, not ours. That's acceptable in a copied file, but say so where the docs introduce it.

## Scope

1. **`deploy/system.conf.d/zz-cannobserv-log-target.conf`.** It goes beside `journald.conf.d/`, `sysctl.d/` and `needrestart.conf.d/`, under the same copy-don't-symlink rule (`docs/DEPLOYMENT-HOST.md`, the `journald.conf.d` paragraph).
2. **A small pinning test.** It checks three things:
   - the file's sha256 equals the one above;
   - its only setting is `[Manager] LogTarget=journal-or-kmsg`;
   - its name sorts after `container-overrides.conf`.

   No test pins the journald cap today [measured: grep], so this is the first. Find the closest home among the existing `deploy/` tests rather than inventing a new layout.
3. **Docs.**
   - `docs/DEPLOYMENT-HOST.md`: add it as the next host-config copy, with its install lines and its revert. Measure the doc first.
   - `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md` is at about 9,932 of its 10,000 tokens: don't edit it.
4. **Rider (#414 standing check, now due).** The skills submodule is at `fb6c297`, which contains `9851de0`, the fix for gregoryfoster/skills#411. In `docs/SKILLS.md`'s `coordinating-epics` row:
   - cut the `origin/HEAD` sentence;
   - correct "With this host's `gh` 2.45 it attributes no commit to a child". It does attribute, through subject refs. Today's scan attributed all five #518 commits. gregoryfoster/skills#412 only loses attribution that would come through a PR's closing links. #500's comments carry the correction.

## Hazards

- **`daemon-reload` re-reads every unit file, not just this setting.** Before reloading, `diff -q` each `deploy/` unit against `/etc/systemd/system/`. A copy that differs would deploy on the reload. #509 left them 15 of 15 identical.
- **Reload outside the nightly.** Don't reload while `usa-wa-pipeline.service` is active (it fires at 08:00 UTC and runs about 3 minutes).
- **A PID1 re-exec is unmeasured with the drop-in.** CannObserv/provisioner#67 flags it: a `systemd` upgrade in a patching run re-executes PID1. Our next patch window could do that. The post-patch read is one line, `systemd-analyze get-log-target`. Put it in the host steps as a check for the next patch run. Don't build anything for it.

## Post-merge host steps (write them on this issue)

1. `sudo install -D -m 0644 deploy/system.conf.d/zz-cannobserv-log-target.conf /etc/systemd/system.conf.d/zz-cannobserv-log-target.conf`
2. Check that the unit copies match, then run `sudo systemctl daemon-reload`.
3. Verify:
   - `systemd-analyze get-log-target` prints `journal-or-kmsg`;
   - `systemd-analyze cat-config systemd/system.conf | grep LogTarget` shows both files, ours last;
   - a throwaway `sudo systemd-run --unit=log-target-check true` puts `Started` and `Deactivated successfully` in `journalctl -u log-target-check`.
4. No service restart is needed.
5. To revert: `sudo rm /etc/systemd/system.conf.d/zz-cannobserv-log-target.conf && sudo systemctl daemon-reload`.

## Out of scope

- Provisioner's open console question (their Q1).
- Moving this VM onto the new image (CannObserv/provisioner#16).
- #414's verify recipe: the coordinator rewrites its `systemctl show` rule once this is verified.

item.title: Identity: juriebsmith:1933 merges Jurie B. Smith and his widow Nettie Luella; her 1943–47 House service publishes nowhere
item.body:
**Size:** S. Filed by the #414 coordinator from #501's build report ([comment](https://github.com/CannObserv/usa-wa/issues/501#issuecomment-6280730267), "For a new issue"). **After the 2.1.0 release** (#501, Thu 2026-10-22). It's an identity change, and it changes published rows.

## The defect

`juriebsmith:1933` is one registry entity for two people: Jurie B. Smith and his widow, Nettie Luella Smith. Their roster rows, from `stg_roster_members` in the 10-19 build, all fold to `juriebsmith`:

| chamber | LD | year | name | annotation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| house | 32 | 1933–1941 (5 rows) | Jurie B. Smith | |
| house | 32 | 1943 | Jurie B. Smith | Deceased November 17, 1942 |
| house | 32 | 1943 | Mrs. Jurie B. Smith | Appointed to serve unexpired term |
| house | 32 | 1945 | Mrs. Jurie B.(Nettie Luella) Smith | |

So the resolver mints **one** identity. That entity's only published tenure is **his** party span, 1933-01-01 → 1942-11-17, closed by his death. **Her 1943–47 service publishes nowhere.** Meanwhile `persons.name_full` shows her printed form on his entity, and after 2.1.0 so does `name_own` = `Nettie Luella Smith` (#384). The row underneath is his.

## Shape of the fix (the implementer reviews it against the code first)

- **`IDENTITY_SPLITS` can't express this one as it stands** (`roster_pdf/identity.py`). It splits a fold at a boundary *year*, and 1943 holds a row for each person: his row carries the death annotation, hers the appointment. A year boundary would put his 1943 row in her identity. The split has to tell the rows apart some other way: the printed `Mrs.` honorific, which the name fold strips, or a row-level adjudication. Pick one, and say why it won't catch any other fold.
- **Registry:** her new roster key needs `adjudicate register` with `distinct_person` (#514's verb), so that it mints instead of re-keying his.
- **`name_own`:** the `OWN_NAMES` entry moves from his key to hers. Check the `name_full` survivorship for both entities.
- **The publication diff:** one new `persons` row, her new spans, and anything about his entity that changes. List every changed row, as #514 did, and tell power-map on CannObserv/power-map#671 (or #489) with the owner's consent.
- **Sweep the class.** Look for other folds where a `Mrs. <his name>` row follows a husband's death in the same district. The roster prints a widow's appointment that way. Marjorie B. Happy (#514) is the precedent with her own name. Count the folds before fixing just this one.

## Out of scope
House seat spans before 2001 (#140/#229/#230). In practice her tenure publishes as a party span.

slot.instructions: `epic` is a GitHub issue that tracks a body of work through a checklist of child issues: `epic.goal` says what it covers, `epic.scope` holds its boundary decisions and rules, `epic.children` its checklist lines (done: ticked), and `epic.parked` what waits on a trigger. `item` is an issue filed since the coordinator last looked, with its state now. Which slot does the coordinator give `item` in this epic?

criteria.child: Work this epic covers and that should be done now or in order: it gets its own checklist line, slotted by dependency. A follow-up to a child, a bug in what a child shipped, or a piece split off a child is a child.
criteria.closed-in-fact: Work this epic covers that is already delivered: the item is closed, or a child's merged change already did it, so it is verified, linked and closed with evidence instead of slotted.
criteria.split: The item mixes work this epic covers with work it doesn't, so the epic's part is filed as its own issue and the rest is left out.
criteria.out of epic: Not this epic's work: another skill, service, area or epic, a record or notice with no action, or tooling around the epic rather than its work. It is said so plainly and cross-linked only where it changes a remaining step.
criteria.duplicate: The same work as an existing child or another open issue, so it is closed in favour of that one.
criteria.park: This epic's concern, but not to be done yet: it waits on a trigger (another repo, a decision, a date, an event) and goes in the parked table with that trigger.

item.title: Dependabot landing recipe after the first monthly run: bump the ruff hook with the lock; dependabot.yml's specifier comment doesn't match increase-if-necessary
item.body:
**Size:** XS. Docs and config only: no lockfile change, no runtime change. Filed by the #414 coordinator from #504's gate report ([comment](https://github.com/CannObserv/usa-wa/pull/504#issuecomment-6291894864), its two "For #499" notes). #499 is closed, so they land here.

## What the first monthly landing showed
1. **The landing recipe misses the ruff hook.** ruff 0.17 in the lock left `.pre-commit-config.yaml` at `v0.15.14`, and pre-ship went red on `ruff format --check`. #504 added `scripts/tests/test_ruff_pin.py`, which fails with the remediation. But `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md` § "Landing the month's PR" should say it before the gate does: "if the lock moves ruff, bump the hook `rev` to match".
2. **`dependabot.yml`'s comment says something that didn't happen.** It reads "rewrites a specifier only when the new version falls outside it". Under `increase-if-necessary`, #504 raised **every** floor (for example `anyio>=4.0` → `>=4.15.1`), and only `pytest-cov<7` actually needed a rewrite. notifier#103 saw the same. Either correct the comment to match what was measured, or change the strategy and say why. For a one-lock app the raised floors are harmless.

## The catch: DEPLOYMENT.md is full
It has about 68 tokens of headroom (estimated offline after #519). Measure it with `measure-context.sh`, then curate before adding. Move prose out to `DEPLOYMENT-HOST.md` (about 7,500 of 10,000) or to a section of its own, rather than squeezing a sentence in.

## Rider (optional, from #520)
An XS test pinning `deploy/journald.conf.d/10-usa-wa-journal-cap.conf`, shaped like `scripts/tests/test_log_target_dropin.py`. It's the only host-config copy with no test (#414 Follow-ups).

## Constraint
Don't touch the files #501's release PRs (#523, #524) touch, or `uv.lock` / any `pyproject.toml`. That way merging `main` into the release branches before Thursday stays trivial.

slot.instructions: `epic` is a GitHub issue that tracks a body of work through a checklist of child issues: `epic.goal` says what it covers, `epic.scope` holds its boundary decisions and rules, `epic.children` its checklist lines (done: ticked), and `epic.parked` what waits on a trigger. `item` is an issue filed since the coordinator last looked, with its state now. Which slot does the coordinator give `item` in this epic?

criteria.child: Work this epic covers and that should be done now or in order: it gets its own checklist line, slotted by dependency. A follow-up to a child, a bug in what a child shipped, or a piece split off a child is a child.
criteria.closed-in-fact: Work this epic covers that is already delivered: the item is closed, or a child's merged change already did it, so it is verified, linked and closed with evidence instead of slotted.
criteria.split: The item mixes work this epic covers with work it doesn't, so the epic's part is filed as its own issue and the rest is left out.
criteria.out of epic: Not this epic's work: another skill, service, area or epic, a record or notice with no action, or tooling around the epic rather than its work. It is said so plainly and cross-linked only where it changes a remaining step.
criteria.duplicate: The same work as an existing child or another open issue, so it is closed in favour of that one.
criteria.park: This epic's concern, but not to be done yet: it waits on a trigger (another repo, a decision, a date, an event) and goes in the parked table with that trigger.

item.title: Lock window 2026-10-27: land Dependabot #529 with pillow 13 and certifi transitive advisories; audit-lock wording
item.body:
**Size:** S. Filed by the #414 coordinator, 2026-10-20, from #526's report ([PR #528](https://github.com/CannObserv/usa-wa/pull/528), "For #414"). **Decided 2026-10-20 (owner):** one PR, landed in the **Tue 2026-10-27 window** (16:00–23:30 UTC), after #501's release. The recipe is `docs/DEPLOYMENT-HOST.md` § Dependency updates (#499), as rewritten by #526.

## What lands
1. **PR #529**, Dependabot's off-cycle group PR: ruff 0.17.0 → 0.17.1, plus `sqlalchemy`, `fastapi` and `dbt-core`. Read the real moves from the `uv.lock` diff, not the PR's table (#526). Bump the ruff hook `rev` to 0.17.1 as well, or `test_ruff_pin` goes red.
2. **Transitive advisories, out of cycle:** `uv lock --upgrade-package pillow --upgrade-package certifi`. Measured 2026-10-20 at `cb9886d4` by `scripts/audit-lock.sh`, 10 advisories:
   - **pillow 12.3.0 → 13.0.0**, 9 advisories (heap overflow in JPEG decode, OOB reads in TIFF, PDF page-tree recursion, among others). It's a **major** version. It arrives only through `pdfplumber` 0.11.10 (`usa-wa-adapter-legislature`'s roster PDF extraction), so check that pdfplumber accepts 13. Afterwards, the roster parse must give byte-identical `stg_roster_members` against the archived edition: run the extraction tests, and compare a staged build if you can.
   - **certifi 2026.5.20 → 2026.10.19**, via httpx/httpcore.
3. **Rider (XS):** `scripts/audit-lock.sh:31` and `scripts/tests/test_audit_lock.py:98` say the monthly PR "moves direct dependencies only". It *targets* direct dependencies (#526 measured 22 moved against 12 named), so reword it.

## Hazards
- **Merge `origin/main` into #529's branch first.** It was cut from `cb9886d4`, and #501's release lands on Thursday. Gate the merged tree, which is the one that lands.
- **Editing `.github/dependabot.yml` triggers an immediate Dependabot run.** #528's merge at 21:34 UTC spawned #529. Don't touch that file here unless you mean to trigger a run. If you do, expect another PR.
- **#527** (declaring sqlalchemy in six packages) also changes `uv.lock`. Whichever lands second rebases onto the other and relocks.

## Post-merge
The `git pull` / `uv sync --locked` / restart block, then check:
- `/health` build;
- `audit-lock.sh` clean, or every remaining advisory named;
- `alembic current` at head;
- 0 failed units.

Then the next nightly (roster extraction under the new pillow) and the backup.

item.title: Layers contract: facts_seats : pipeline is non-independent, so 'neither may import the other' is unenforced, and the pipeline imports facts
item.body:
**Size:** S, once the owner decides the direction. Found while reviewing #527 ([review comment](https://github.com/CannObserv/usa-wa/issues/527#issuecomment-6353325113), "For a new issue"). Measured at `b75bd451`.

## The defect
The layers contract in the root `pyproject.toml` says facts and the pipeline are independent, but it does not enforce that, and the code depends on the opposite.

- **The contract** (`pyproject.toml:186-189`, written in #303):
  ```toml
  # facts and pipeline are independent siblings: both compose across adapters
  # (...), neither may import the other (#302/#303).
  "usa_wa_facts_seats : usa_wa_pipeline",
  ```
  In import-linter (2.15 here), `:` separates **non-independent** siblings, and `|` separates independent ones (`importlinter/contracts/layers.py:20-21`). So the contract allows imports both ways, and `lint-imports` stays green.
- **The code** has imported facts from the pipeline since #309:
  - `usa_wa_pipeline/conformed/house.py:67-72`: `backchain`, `positions.merge_positions`, `roster.build_house_roster`, `house_mover_ids` (#309).
  - `usa_wa_pipeline/conformed/movers.py:54-59`: `REDISTRICTING_ERA_START_BIENNIA`, `HouseRosterEntry`, `build_house_roster`, `house_mover_ids` (#490).
  - `conformed/house.py`'s own docstring calls it "the conformed analog of `usa_wa_facts_seats.house.build`". The pipeline composing facts' pure logic is the design in practice.
- **The pipeline does not declare `usa-wa-facts-seats`.** Nothing it declares brings it in either: facts depends on the adapters, not the other way round. It is installed only because the root `dev` group lists every workspace member. #527's `test_declared_dependencies` covers third-party imports only, so it doesn't catch this.
- **The docs repeat the claim:** AGENTS.md's layer table ("3c pipeline … facts sibling"); `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` ("the layer order above, with no back-edges").

## Shape: the owner picks one
- **A. Make the code's direction the rule.** The pipeline sits above facts. Split the entry into two layers (`"usa_wa_pipeline"` above `"usa_wa_facts_seats"`), which then forbids facts → pipeline, the edge that matters. Declare `usa-wa-facts-seats` in `usa-wa-pipeline`, rewrite the comment, and update the AGENTS.md table and ARCHITECTURE.md. No code moves. *(Recommended: it matches #309 and #490 as built, and turns a rule nobody enforced into one that is enforced.)*
- **B. Make the comment true.** Change the entry to `|`, and move what the pipeline imports into a layer both may use (`usa-wa-common`, or the domain). `house.py` and `movers.py` change. It is a bigger change, and it reverses a dependency two shipped features rely on.

Whichever is picked:
- Add a check to `scripts/tests/test_import_contracts.py` that pins the separator, so an independence claim cannot be silently weakened again.
- Consider extending #527's rule to workspace siblings. The pipeline also imports `clearinghouse_domain_legislative` (14 modules) and `usa_wa_common` (10) without declaring them; those arrive through the adapters.
- No `uv.lock` version moves. Declaring a workspace member adds lock lines only.

slot.instructions: `epic` is a GitHub issue that tracks a body of work through a checklist of child issues: `epic.goal` says what it covers, `epic.scope` holds its boundary decisions and rules, `epic.children` its checklist lines (done: ticked), and `epic.parked` what waits on a trigger. `item` is an issue filed since the coordinator last looked, with its state now. Which slot does the coordinator give `item` in this epic?

criteria.child: Work this epic covers and that should be done now or in order: it gets its own checklist line, slotted by dependency. A follow-up to a child, a bug in what a child shipped, or a piece split off a child is a child.
criteria.closed-in-fact: Work this epic covers that is already delivered: the item is closed, or a child's merged change already did it, so it is verified, linked and closed with evidence instead of slotted.
criteria.split: The item mixes work this epic covers with work it doesn't, so the epic's part is filed as its own issue and the rest is left out.
criteria.out of epic: Not this epic's work: another skill, service, area or epic, a record or notice with no action, or tooling around the epic rather than its work. It is said so plainly and cross-linked only where it changes a remaining step.
criteria.duplicate: The same work as an existing child or another open issue, so it is closed in favour of that one.
criteria.park: This epic's concern, but not to be done yet: it waits on a trigger (another repo, a decision, a date, an event) and goes in the parked table with that trigger.

epic.title: [Epic] Headless Watcher and cohort boundaries
epic.goal:
Make Watcher a **headless service** (no HTML dashboard, no `/api/v1`; only `/health` and `/ready`), with Archiver as the cohort's only control plane, and **state the cohort's service boundaries and communication rules in one charter**. This is the parent epic.

**Charter in one line:** operator intent → Archiver; mechanism → the executor (except host-local break-glass); observations → the service that computes them; time-evolving intent is resolved by its owner. Intent travels as config/state, occasions as commands, edges as outboxed facts, levels as config/state, and HTTP only at the cohort edge.

**Watcher monitors and reports; Archiver decides who hears; Notifier delivers.**

Design of record: [docs/plans/2026-10-14-headless-watcher-and-cohort-boundaries-design.md](https://github.com/CannObserv/watcher/blob/main/docs/plans/2026-10-14-headless-watcher-and-cohort-boundaries-design.md)

item.title: Adopt the coordinating-epics skill for #368
item.body:
`coordinating-epics` v1 shipped in gregoryfoster/skills (gregoryfoster/skills#348, `fef0611`). It packages the protocol #368's coordinator runs by hand, and several of its rules came from this repo's burn-down findings (F1–F63, and #368's own F1–F3). This issue moves #368 onto it.

**What v1 brings**
- `epic-edit.sh`: one guarded call per body edit. It refuses foreign edits against a saved baseline (a tick you have verified passes with `--accept-ticks`), anchors each operation by ref, derives checkbox counts, lints refs, placeholders and secrets, compare-and-swaps before the PATCH, and reads the body back.
- `scan.sh`: the three re-scan cursors (number watermark, updated-since, and the commit range attributed to children), the epic's own new comments, and cross-repo ref states, as JSON.
- `assets/epic-template.md`: the header cursor lines both scripts read.

#368 is a cross-repo parent over six repos. v1 runs its check-ins, but `scan.sh` scans one repo: watcher's. The other five repos' re-scans stay by hand, as now. Creating a cross-repo parent epic is v1.1 (gregoryfoster/skills#396).

**Steps**
1. **Vendor it.** `skills-vendor/gregoryfoster-skills` is at `85caed2`, one commit before the skill. Bump it to `fef0611` or later, then symlink `skills/coordinating-epics` and `.claude/skills/coordinating-epics` (managing-skills, Step 2/2b). The auto-refresh hook bumps the pointer but creates no symlinks.
2. **Adopt at the next check-in, as that check-in's one write** (SKILL.md, "Adopt an epic that exists"). Run `scan.sh --repo CannObserv/watcher --epic 368 --since <last check-in, with a time and zone> --watermark 383 --from-sha <last verified SHA>`. Then make one `epic-edit.sh --repo CannObserv/watcher --epic 368 --adopt-live --lint-all --scan <report> --ops <file>` call, dry-run first, with `header` ops for `Last check-in` (`{checked}`), `Last issue seen` (`{last_seen}`) and `Last verified SHA`.
3. **After that,** every body edit goes through `epic-edit.sh`, and each check-in starts with `scan.sh`.

**What a dry run on today's body found** (a copy of the body, run against the fake `gh` in the skill's tests; nothing was written):
- **`Last check-in` has a date but no time** ("2026-10-15"), so `scan.sh` can't read it. Pass `--since` this once; `{checked}` writes a full time from then on.
- **The same line holds all six watermarks.** A `header` op on `Last check-in` rewrites the whole line, so move the other five into their own section in the same call, e.g. `add-section` "Other repos' watermarks". Write them as one line of prose, not bullets: CannObserv/archiver#383 already leads a bullet in the epic, and the editor refuses a second line led by the same ref. The call applies cleanly.
- **The new cursor lines land above "Coordination",** apart from `Last check-in`, which stays where it is. Both scripts read them wherever they sit.
- **`--lint-all` flags three refs:**
  - `#566` in `Next` (`cannobserv#563–#566`): it's bare, so GitHub reads it as this repo's #566, which doesn't exist. Write `CannObserv/cannobserv#566`; it's a `header` op.
  - `#571` in the watermarks line, which is rewritten anyway.
  - `#127` after CannObserv/archiver#380 on the screenshot-capture line: watcher's own #127, but qualify it.

  Fix them in the same call.

**Known limits in v1:** CI by job is still checked by hand (gregoryfoster/skills#394), and comments are not linted before posting (gregoryfoster/skills#395).

**When the run ends:** journal it in the skill's process log. The skill is vendored here, so draft the entry in this repo and file it upstream as an issue on gregoryfoster/skills ("Adding an entry" in `references/process-log.md`).

item.title: Cohort disk GC: adopt one shared implementation (provisioner#61); age-only VS Code pruning
item.body:
**Context:** six cohort hosts each built their own root-disk GC. **CannObserv/provisioner#61** proposes one canonical host-tooling GC + headroom sensor in co-image-base, and **gregoryfoster/skills#425** proposes a skill to adopt it on hosts not yet on the image. This repo's implementation is in the comparison table there, so please weigh in on #61, especially if your rules differ.

**When it lands:** adopt the canonical files and retire the local implementation.

**Here:** `scripts/cleanup.sh` + `watcher-cleanup` (weekly).

**Worth checking now** (found on another host, may apply here):
- Age-only VS Code server pruning (>30 d) can keep weeks of ~650 M builds, and can delete a build a long-lived window still runs. Liveness from `/proc` plus the newest build by `lru.json` is the safe pair (CannObserv/usa-wa#394, CannObserv/power-map#665).
- `~/.vscode-server/extensions/` accumulates a ~255 M Claude Code version per release (CannObserv/usa-wa#399).
- Pruning `~/.npm/_npx` by age or liveness can delete the **pinned SocratiCode tree** while no session is up. The next session then reinstalls it uncapped. Keep the dir named `sha512(spec)[:16]` for the pinned `SOCRATICODE_SPEC`, both the repo-declared spec and the one in the VS Code machine setting `claudeCode.environmentVariables` (CannObserv/usa-wa#485, CannObserv/power-map#665).

item.title: Route content.derived's dead_lettered to a processor-blaming failure, not the extraction-failure path (cannobserv#536)
item.body:
**Filed by CannObserv/cannobserv#561's coordinator (owner request, 2026-10-17).** This is the Watcher half of CannObserv/cannobserv#536, which you asked for on CannObserv/watcher#325 (decision 3, 2026-10-02). Read against watcher `main` at `0eba3bc`.

## What changed upstream

co-core's `ProcessingFailureReason` gains **`dead_lettered`**: terminal, no re-fetch. It covers a command Processor quarantines in `content.process.dlq`, because the attempt that reached its cap raised past Processor's own error handling (a bug outside it, or a non-transient publish refusal). The name is the owner's narrowing of the "e.g. `processor_error`" in the original ask, scoped to Processor's **escape cap** only. A give-up the handler caught at its strike cap (every attempt timed out, crashed, or raised outside the parser) still arrives as `extraction_error`. The contract is the `ProcessingFailedEvent` docstring in co-core.

It ships in co-core **v0.37.0** (CannObserv/cannobserv#568, a MINOR by owner's choice, being cut now). Processor adopts it in CannObserv/processor#21: only `handler.publish_gave_up` moves to `dead_lettered`.

## Today's routing

`_decide` (`src/workers/process_commands.py`) sends every terminal reason except `input_unreadable` down the extraction-failure path: `fail_extraction`, reason `processing_failed`, audit `CHECK_EXTRACTION_FAILED`. So `dead_lettered` would be reported as if the item's spec were bad. Nothing breaks meanwhile `[traced]`:
- `ProcessingFailedEvent.reason` is a `str` on the consumer class, so the token decodes on co-core 0.32.0;
- `process_commands.failure_reason` is a `Text` column.

## Ask

Route `dead_lettered` to a failure that **blames the processor, not the spec**. The exact shape is Watcher's call. One precedent is in this file: `_end_lineage` for `processing_timeout` clears the validators (the bytes were never judged; #362, #363) and records the failure with the processor's reason, not the spec's. To weigh:
- **A Watcher reason token** for it, or reuse `processing_timeout`'s path with a distinct token. A new token joins `WatchHealthReason`'s vocabulary on `info.watch-events` / `info.watch-status`. co-core's docstring keeps the registry of tokens and their owners, so tell cannobserv to add it (a doc-only change).
- **Validators:** clear them, as the timeout path does. A dead-letter judged nothing.
- **The audit event:** `CHECK_EXTRACTION_FAILED` names the wrong cause. Decide whether a processor-fault event belongs beside it.
- **`_decide`'s docstring** ("`extraction_error` from a give-up (processor#17) included") stays half true: the strike cap keeps `extraction_error`.

## Order

None strictly required. Watcher can branch on the string before Processor ever sends it. Adopt co-core v0.37.0 with this change for the documented constant and the other headless-Watcher contracts (CannObserv/watcher#368, Phase 1). Processor's adoption (CannObserv/processor#21) doesn't wait on this; until this lands, a dead-letter keeps reading as an extraction failure, as it does today.

Refs: CannObserv/cannobserv#536, CannObserv/cannobserv#568, CannObserv/processor#21, CannObserv/processor#17, CannObserv/watcher#325, CannObserv/watcher#368.

item.title: Give the test suite its own Postgres role: TEST_DATABASE_URL runs as the production schema owner
item.body:
## Problem

The test suite connects to Postgres as `watcher`, the **production schema owner**. `TEST_DATABASE_URL` in the repo `.env` names that role, pointed at `watcher_test`.

So the credential that pytest and the dev server load into every agent and developer shell is also the credential with DDL rights over the production `watcher` database:

| Role | Production rights | Who loads it |
|---|---|---|
| `watcher` | Owns every `watcher*` database, prod included. Owns the schema, runs migrations, `CREATEDB` | `/etc/watcher/.env` (`WATCHER_MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL`) **and** the repo `.env` (`TEST_DATABASE_URL`) |
| `watcher_app` | DML only | The service (`DATABASE_URL`) |
| `watcher_backup` | `pg_read_all_data`, peer auth, no password | The backup unit |

**Why it matters:**

- **The tests already run destructive DDL with it.** `tests/conftest.py` runs `create_all` / `drop_all` and `DROP SCHEMA … CASCADE` as `watcher`. `db_safety` only checks the database *name* (`_test`/`_dev`). Nothing stops the same credential from reaching `watcher` if a URL is misedited, a guard regresses, or someone pastes it into psql.
- **A test-side leak is a production leak.** On 2026-10-18 the role's URL was echoed into an agent transcript. The rotation had to touch both files, and the only copy of the old password left on disk was in editor snapshots of the repo `.env`.

## Proposal

1. **Add a test role**, e.g. `watcher_tester`. It gets `LOGIN`, `NOCREATEDB` and `NOCREATEROLE`, and no grant on `watcher`. It owns `watcher_test` and the rehearsal `*_test` scratch databases:
   - `ALTER DATABASE … OWNER TO`
   - `REASSIGN OWNED BY watcher TO watcher_tester`, run *inside* each of those databases (the schemas and procrastinate objects pytest doesn't recreate)
2. **Close the side door:** `REVOKE CONNECT ON DATABASE watcher FROM PUBLIC`, then grant `CONNECT` explicitly to `watcher`, `watcher_app` and `watcher_backup`. Today any login role can connect to prod by default. Check the backup unit and the recovery rehearsals' scratch databases (`docs/RECOVERY-REHEARSALS.md`) after the revoke. `docs/RECOVERY.md` notes `watcher_backup`'s reads are cluster-wide "on every database it may connect to, which PUBLIC may by default".
3. **Point `TEST_DATABASE_URL` at the new role**, with its own password, in the repo `.env`. Keep `watcher` only in `/etc/watcher/.env`.
4. **Guard on capability, not name.** At session start, `tests/conftest.py` (or `src/core/db_safety.py`) refuses a test connection whose `current_user` can `CONNECT` to any database *without* the `_test`/`_dev` suffix, via `has_database_privilege` over `pg_database`. That turns "the test role can't reach prod" into a failing check rather than a convention, and it would have caught today's setup.
5. **`watcher_dev`:** `scripts/dev_server.sh` defaults to `TEST_DATABASE_URL`, so it inherits the fix. `WATCHER_DEV_DATABASE_URL`, when set, should follow the same rule. Decide whether `watcher_dev` (owned by `watcher` today) moves to the new role too.

## Not affected

- **CI** uses the container's own `postgres` superuser against a throwaway database (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`).
- **The service** connects as `watcher_app`, and `deploy/watcher.service` unsets `WATCHER_MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL`.
- **The autogenerate scratch-DB procedure** (`docs/COMMANDS.md`) needs `CREATEDB` and stays on the migration role, which is correct: it is run deliberately, from a shell that has loaded `/etc/watcher/.env`.

## Done when

- [ ] A test-only role owns `watcher_test` (and the `*_test` scratch DBs) and can't connect to `watcher`.
- [ ] `PUBLIC` no longer has `CONNECT` on `watcher`; the service, backup and migrations still work.
- [ ] `TEST_DATABASE_URL` names the new role; `watcher`'s password appears only in `/etc/watcher/.env`.
- [ ] A test fails if the test connection's role can reach a non-`_test`/`_dev` database.
- [ ] `docs/MIGRATIONS.md` (the role table and its one-time section) and `docs/COMMANDS.md` (the test database) describe the new role. `scripts/setup-db-roles.sql` or a sibling script creates it, with the password read from the environment and never written into the file.

epic.title: [Epic] Headless Watcher and cohort boundaries
epic.goal:
Make Watcher a **headless service** (no HTML dashboard, no `/api/v1`; only `/health` and `/ready`), with Archiver as the cohort's only control plane, and **state the cohort's service boundaries and communication rules in one charter**. This is the parent epic.

**Charter in one line:** operator intent → Archiver; mechanism → the executor (except host-local break-glass); observations → the service that computes them; time-evolving intent is resolved by its owner. Intent travels as config/state, occasions as commands, edges as outboxed facts, levels as config/state, and HTTP only at the cohort edge.

**Watcher monitors and reports; Archiver decides who hears; Notifier delivers.**

item.title: info.watch-check consumer: dead-letter a command that fails deterministically after N deliveries (before F4)
item.body:
Follow-up from #371's review (CR 6, held). Filed by the coordinator of #368. **This must land before F4**, when Archiver's check-now button (CannObserv/archiver#370) starts issuing on `info.watch-check`.

## Problem
In the `info.watch-check` consumer (`src/workers/watch_check.py`, on the shared `run_fact_consumer` loop), **only an undecodable command reaches `info.watch-check.dlq`.** A decodable command that fails *deterministically* gets reclaimed and retried forever, and every command behind it waits. #371's example is a NUL in `info_item_id`, which JSONB refuses at the outbox write. co-core leaves the delivery-count → DLQ policy to the first real consumer, and that consumer is watcher's [stated: #371's closing comment].

## Ask
Decide and implement a **delivery-count threshold**: past N deliveries, dead-letter the command to `info.watch-check.dlq` with its raw fields, ack it, and log it.
- Where it applies: the command stream only, or the two fact inboxes too (`content.blobs`, `content.derived`), which ack past failures today.
- N, and where it lives. A constant is enough until someone needs to tune it.
- A test: one poison command stops blocking the commands behind it.

## Notes
- The DLQ writer rule (`TestNoDeadLetterWriterExistsYet`, flipped in #371) pins one writer and one enabler. Keep it true, or widen it on purpose.
- broker owns the probe that watches `info.watch-check.dlq`'s length and age.
- Size S.

item.title: Bump SocratiCode 1.14.0 → 1.16.1 (SOCRATICODE_SPEC); safe for the shared store, no re-index
item.body:
`.claude/settings.json:58` pins `SOCRATICODE_SPEC` to `socraticode@1.14.0`. The latest release is **1.16.1** (2026-10-15). broker, observo and processor already build on 1.16.0.

## Safe for the shared store

There's no need to re-index or remove anything on co-index (CannObserv/index#13).

- **The embedding text is unchanged from 1.14.0 to 1.16.1.** In the npm tarballs, `embeddings.js`, `embedding-config.js` and `index-profile.js` are byte-identical, and the `indexer.js` changes don't touch chunking. So vectors from 1.16.1 compare with the rest of the store as before (D7), and co-index's `reembed.py` still models them.
- **Qdrant on co-index is now 1.20.0.** SocratiCode's client is `@qdrant/js-client-rest ~1.18.0` with `checkCompatibility: false`. The calls clients make (taken from co-index's access log), plus create, payload index, upsert, delete and a hybrid query, were all tested against 1.20.0.

## What changes

- **1.15.0:** PHP code-graph fixes, Qdrant errors keep their reason, and SocratiCode now waits for its own collection create before reading it.
- **1.16.0:** an opt-in refresh triggered by Git (`SOCRATICODE_WATCHER=git`).
- **1.16.1:** a `limit` on `codebase_symbol`, `codebase_impact` and `codebase_flow`; the symbol graph retries a Qdrant request once on a closed connection; Kotlin Multiplatform and PHP graph fixes; an opt-in auto-cleanup.
  - **Leave `SOCRATICODE_AUTO_CLEANUP` unset.** It refuses a shared, non-loopback store anyway, so it can't fire against co-index.

Changelog: https://github.com/giancarloerra/socraticode/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md

## Ask

1. Set `SOCRATICODE_SPEC` to `socraticode@1.16.1`. Then grep the repo for any other `socraticode@1.14.0` (docs, health hook) and bump those too.
2. Restart the session, then run `codebase_status`. After the next graph build, co-index's `socraticode_metadata` records `builtByVersion: 1.16.1` for this repo.

item.title: Retire the brainstorming override: vendor symlink + watcher preferences in AGENTS.md
item.body:
## Problem

`skills/brainstorming/` is a 23 KB fork of `obra-superpowers/brainstorming`, taken at v6.4.1 (`5bf4e78`). Since then upstream has rewritten the skill twice: v7.0.0 ("rebuilt brainstorming") and v7.0.1 ("brainstorming retune", `2ce8aa1`). Because of that, `.skills/doctor.sh` reports override drift on every run. Re-syncing means re-applying our deltas onto a rewritten upstream, and that cost recurs with every upstream release.

The deltas themselves are few and stable, and they're project preferences, not skill logic. The override's own `override-reason` lists them. They belong in `AGENTS.md`, where they apply whatever the vendored text says. Upstream v7.0.1 already allows for this: on where the design doc goes, it says *"Your human partner's preferences override both."*

## Proposal

1. **Symlink, not fork.** Replace the `skills/brainstorming/` directory with `skills/brainstorming -> ../skills-vendor/obra-superpowers/skills/brainstorming`, the same shape as every other vendored skill. `.claude/skills/brainstorming` already points at `skills/brainstorming`.
2. **Preferences in `AGENTS.md`**, as a short section (for example `## Design work`, or a block under *Agent Skills*). Carry over only what isn't already stated there:
   - design docs go in `docs/plans/`, not `docs/superpowers/specs/`;
   - a GitHub issue on the architectural path;
   - `writing-plans` is optional, not mandatory. After design approval, multi-step work goes to `using-git-worktrees`;
   - the visual companion's port must be in the exe.dev proxy range (3000–9999).

   Already in `AGENTS.md`, so not repeated: the `#<n> [type]:` commit convention and TDD as the implementation workflow. Also dropped: the `elements-of-style` pointer. That skill isn't vendored here, and v7.0.1 no longer has the line anyway.
3. **Docs:** remove the `brainstorming` row from the override table in `docs/SKILLS.md` and the brainstorming sentences in its `synced-from:` paragraph. Update the `.socraticodeignore` comment (line 9) that names the overrides.

## Risks to check while implementing

- **The HARD-GATE conflict.** Upstream's gate ends with *"invoke superpowers:writing-plans and no other skill"*. A preference in `AGENTS.md` has to override that explicitly, and it has to work in practice: dry-run a brainstorm and confirm it hands off to `using-git-worktrees` or an issue rather than forcing a plan. If upstream's gate wins, keep a minimal override, or raise it upstream instead.
- **Namespaces.** Upstream names `superpowers:writing-plans`. Here `writing-plans` is the vendored gregoryfoster skill. Confirm the handoff resolves.
- **Budget.** `AGENTS.md` is at 5,885 of 6,000 tokens (exact, 2026-10-23). The new section has to be tight, or demote detail to `docs/SKILLS.md`. Run `curating-context` afterwards.

## Done when

- `skills/brainstorming` is a symlink into the vendor tree, and `find skills .claude/skills -xtype l` prints nothing.
- `.skills/doctor.sh` reports no `brainstorming` override drift.
- `AGENTS.md` carries the preferences and stays at or under budget. `prove-no-loss` and `check-seams` are clean.
- A brainstorm dry run writes to `docs/plans/` and honours the handoff preference.

## Context

- Precondition: the obra-superpowers submodule bump to v7.0.1 (filed alongside this issue). That bump drops the override's `spec-document-reviewer-prompt.md` symlink: v7 no longer ships the file, and the override's body never used it.
- Out of scope: the `shipping-work-python-fastapi` override. Its deltas are script resolution and `.skills/` tailoring, which can't move to `AGENTS.md` the same way.

item.title: Report-only lock audit workflow (port CannObserv/broker#86)
item.body:
Split from #392 (its brief's open operator decision; operator OK 2026-10-24: its own issue, so #392 stayed a pure bump). Belongs to the backlog burn-down epic #394.

## Problem

Runtime advisories in `uv.lock` are found today only when someone runs `uv audit` by hand (#382's patching-hosts class 6, #392's tally). #392 took the runtime set from 20 unique advisories to **0** on `main`. Without a recurring check, a new advisory sits unseen until the next monthly patching run.

## Shape: port CannObserv/broker#86

The report-only lock audit. CannObserv/archiver#420 is porting the same thing now, so read both before writing:
- `.github/workflows/audit.yml`: scheduled plus `workflow_dispatch`, and on PRs touching `uv.lock`/`pyproject.toml`. It runs `uv audit --frozen` and reports, with no gate on merges at first.
- `scripts/audit_lock.sh`: the one invocation CI and a human both run. Decide `--no-dev` vs. all groups. #392 scoped runtime only; the dev set (virtualenv, soupsieve, openapi-python-client, pygments) is #382's class 6.
- **A pin test** on the workflow/script's decisions, the broker#86 way, so a later edit fails a test before it changes the behaviour.
- **No secret.** `uv audit --frozen` reads the lock alone and asks OSV. It needs no wheelhouse, though check whether the `find-links = ["./.wheelhouse"]` requirement bites in a bare checkout. #392's run had the wheelhouse present.

## Notes

- `tests/test_dependency_advisory_floors.py` (#392) is the complement, not a substitute. It holds each **fixed** advisory's floor with no network; this workflow finds **new** advisories.
- `uv audit` is still experimental in uv 0.13.5 (it warns on every run). Pin the uv version in the workflow, or pass `--preview-features audit-command`.
- patching-hosts has no knob `<what>` for a language-dependency exception (noted on #392 for #382). An accepted advisory therefore needs this workflow's own allowlist, with a reason and a review-by date.

## Done when

- [ ] The workflow runs on schedule and on a lock-touching PR, and its report is readable from the run summary.
- [ ] The script and the pin test are in place and green in CI.
- [ ] One deliberate run is recorded on this issue. On today's lock it reports 0 runtime advisories, plus the dev set.

item.title: fastapi 0.135.1 -> current: decide whether and when (no advisory requires it)
item.body:
Split from #392. Operator OK 2026-10-24 to file it; not yet scheduled in an epic.

## Context

#392 fixed starlette's five advisories by moving **starlette alone** (0.52.1 → 1.9.0). The locked fastapi **0.135.1** declares `starlette>=0.46.0`, uncapped, and has supported starlette 1.0+ since 0.133.0. So no advisory requires a fastapi upgrade: `uv audit --frozen --no-dev` is clean on `main` after #392. This issue is about **currency, not security**. Decide whether and when, rather than drifting.

## What 0.135.1 → 0.162.0 (latest when #392 shipped) changes for this codebase

Read from fastapi's release notes during #392; re-read at the target version.

| Release | Change | Reaches watcher? |
|---|---|---|
| 0.137.0 | `router.routes` becomes a tree of intermediate objects; `APIRouter`/`APIRoute` instances preserved | No `.routes` iteration in `src/` or `tests/` at #392. Re-grep. |
| 0.142/0.143 | Native OpenTelemetry; **`opentelemetry-api>=1.44.0` becomes a hard dependency**; exporter auto-config opt-in (`FASTAPI_OTEL_AUTO_CONFIGURE`) | The lock grows a package (1.45.1 is the fixed release for GHSA-xcq7-p3pf-p88h, CannObserv/processor#71). Confirm no `OTEL_*` env reaches the unit. |
| 0.147 → 0.162 | Omitted `bool` form fields inferred `False` (0.147), then reverted to declared defaults (0.162) | No `bool` `Form()` today: all 19 are `str`. |
| 0.148 | Defaults for omitted Query/Header/Cookie/Form are no longer validated | Check any validator relying on running for a default. |
| 0.149 / 0.153 | Empty scalar form-model values treated as missing | No form models today. |
| 0.151 | JSON `null` distinguished from omitted for `Body` values | `/api/v1` bodies (until #378 deletes them). |
| 0.155 | `**extra` removed from `Path`/`Query`/`Header`/`Cookie`/`Body`/`Form`/`File`: unknown kwargs raise `TypeError` | Fails at import if present, so the suite catches it. |
| 0.136.3 | Underscore headers rejected under `convert_underscores=True` | No `Header()` params; exe.dev headers are read from `request.headers`. |
| 0.146 | `root_path` parameter deprecated | Not used. |

## Sequencing

#378 (deletes `/api/v1`) and #377 (deletes the dashboard), both in #368 and both blocked on Archiver, shrink the surface to `/health` and `/ready`. After them, this is nearly a no-op. Before them, it's the table above. Prefer after, unless a fastapi advisory forces it first: `tests/test_dependency_advisory_floors.py` and the lock audit issue would surface one.

## Related

- starlette 1.9 warns that `TestClient` over `httpx` is deprecated in favour of `httpx2`. Moving the dev group to `httpx2` pairs naturally with this upgrade.

## Done when

- [ ] Decision recorded: upgrade now, after #377/#378, or close as not planned.
- [ ] If upgraded: the lock diff is limited to fastapi and its declared pull-ins; the full suite runs, both halves; the changelog sections from 0.135.2 to the target are checked and listed; the service is restarted, and `/health` reports the merge SHA.
