item.title: test_relative_links: a code span runs past a list item, heading, blockquote or table cell, so a link GitHub renders goes unchecked
item.body:
Follow-up to #416, from its review (CR 366, held there as a known limit). A child of #404 by its boundary rule: a gate the skill relies on.

**What:** `test_relative_links.py`'s `_code_spans` lets an unclosed backtick's closer search run on until a blank line. GitHub ends that search sooner: at the start of a list item, a heading, a blockquote, or the next table cell. Each of those starts a new block, and a span can't cross one. A link after such a boundary renders, but the gate masks it as code, so a dead one passes.

**Seen on** [measured 2026-10-19, at ae5338c, with `gh api markdown` and `dead_links_in`]. Each case is two lines: an opener on line 1, and a link to a missing file, then a closing backtick, on line 2. GitHub renders the link in four of the five; the gate reports none of them.

| Line 2 starts | GitHub renders | Gate at ae5338c |
|---|---|---|
| a list item (`- `), under a list item | a link, in the second item | masked |
| a heading (`# `) | a link, in the heading | masked |
| a blockquote (`> `) | a link, in the quote | masked |
| the next cell, on one table row | a link, in that cell | masked |
| plain text (the control) | code, so no link | masked (right) |

**Why it matters:** the same class as #416. The gate's span model is wider than GitHub's, so a link a reader sees goes unchecked. Nothing in the tree hits it today [stated by #416's implementer], so it closes a hole for later docs.

**Suggested fix:** stop `_code_spans`' closer search where a new block starts: a line opening a list item, a heading, a blockquote or a fence, and a table cell's pipe, as well as a blank line. Keep the gate self-contained, as #416 did. Measure each boundary with `gh api markdown` before encoding it. A list item's lazy continuation line is not a new block, and a span may wrap into it.

**Test:** each row above as a gate case (a dead link caught after each boundary, the control still masked), plus a span that wraps into a lazy continuation line staying masked.

item.title: curating-context: a TypeSafe Choice per section as a second reading of the Phase 3 class, recorded in the telemetry row
item.body:
**What:** Phase 3 gives each `##` section (and each subsection over ~5% of the file) one class, A/B/C/D, from [keep-cut-rubric.md](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/skills/curating-context/references/keep-cut-rubric.md). That class is the most consequential call in a run: the skill itself says "compressing class B is wasted work, deleting class A is damage." Yet it is pure agent judgment, and the ledger records only the actions that followed (`demote:X`, `prune:Y`). Neither the class nor how close the call was is recorded.

**Proposal:** add an optional script that sends the policy file to [TypeSafe](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/system-one.md) Jev as structured state (`sections[i].heading`, `.text`, `.tokens`). The request asks:
- one **Choice** per section over A/B/C/D, with each option's criteria taken from the rubric's class definitions, so the classes mean the same thing in the script as in the rubric;
- one **Noul** per section: "Does `sections[i].text` restate a default a capable coding agent already follows?" This is the one class-D clause a model can judge. *Duplicates another part of the surface* and *disproven* stay with Phase 2's scripts.

All of these go in one request ([speculative fan-out](https://docs.typesafe.ai/patterns/fan-out.md)). The script outputs JSON: per section, the class, its per-class probabilities, the confidence, and the Noul.

**How it's used:**
1. The agent's class stays authoritative. A section where Jev's class differs, or its confidence is low, gets a second look before Phase 4. It is never re-classed automatically.
2. A new telemetry field (e.g. `class_contested`, the number of contested sections, `null` when the step didn't run) lets the cohort roll-up see which classes are hard to call.

**Must not:** license a delete. The iron law's warrants (relocated, duplicated, disproven) are unchanged. A "D" from Jev with no warrant only means "look here".

**Why it matters:** the class is the one call in the run nobody checks. A probability distribution per section makes a contested call visible, before it turns into an edit, and after it, in the ledger.

**Evaluation:** past cohort runs give a labelled set. The ledger's action tags plus the curation diffs recover which sections were demoted, tightened or pruned. Measure agreement against those first. Cost [estimated]: at the listed $0.042/Mtok input price, a 6k-token policy file plus the questions costs well under a cent per run.

**Constraints shared with the other TypeSafe proposals:**
- **Opt-in and advisory.** If `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` is missing, the step skips and says so loudly, and the run goes on exactly as it does today. The opt-in knob goes in [docs/KNOBS.md](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/docs/KNOBS.md), which `test_skills_knob_inventory.py` requires.
- **Data leaves the machine.** This sends repo text to typesafe.ai. Today the only API call any skill script makes is `measure-context.sh --exact`'s token count, and that sends no text to be judged. Some cohort repos are private, so the opt-in is per repo, never cohort-wide.
- **Pin the model.** Use `jev-1.13.0`, not `jev-latest`. The alias moves when a new version ships, and thresholds tuned against one version don't carry to the next ([models](https://docs.typesafe.ai/models.md#aliases)).
- **Measure before gating.** Collect a labelled set and measure agreement before any threshold changes what the run does. A typed answer guarantees the shape of the answer, not that it is true.

Sibling TypeSafe proposals: #435 section class · #436 harvest · #437 CR tiers · #438 stale issue prose · #439 epic slotting · #440 backlog scoring · #441 bare-digit counts · #442 semantic no-loss · #443 close-gate requirements · #444 process-log recurrence · #445 cross-repo present tense · #446 pre-batch body decay · #447 index-line accuracy.

item.title: coordinating-epics: rank harvest candidates with a TypeSafe Noul per (paragraph, open child), so a note reaches a child it never names
item.body:
**What:** check-in §2, Harvest ([check-in.md](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/skills/coordinating-epics/references/check-in.md#2-harvest)), reads the closing comment, the PR, and every comment since the hand-off. From them it routes contract diffs, `For #N:` notes, asides in prose, verification debt and corrections to the children they affect. An explicit `For #N:` heading names its target. The hard cases have no heading: a contract diff that should reach "every downstream child", or a later child's precondition mentioned in passing. Here the coordinator has to match a paragraph to a child it never names. Several log entries cite a note that didn't reach its child (archiver 19, 32; private-backlog 103, 110).

**Proposal:** add an optional script that produces a ranked list of harvest candidates:
- Code splits the harvest sources into paragraphs and fetches the open children's titles and bodies through `gh`.
- One [TypeSafe](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/system-one.md) request per source comment, with that comment's paragraphs and the open children in the state:
  - a **Noul** per (paragraph, child): "Does `paragraphs[i]` change a fact, contract, or step that `children[j].body` relies on?";
  - a **Choice** per paragraph over the harvest kinds in §2: contract diff, note for a later child, new state/code/message, verification debt, accepted limitation, correction to a claim, answer to a later child's step, or **none**.
- Output: (paragraph, child, kind, probability) rows sorted by the Noul, written to the coordinator's scratch, where it reads them beside `scan.json`.

**Must not:** write to GitHub. The coordinator still verifies each candidate and writes the "Changed since filed" comment, and the "coordinator never writes code" rule is unchanged. The script only reorders what the coordinator reads first.

**Why it matters:** a note that never reaches its child surfaces only when that child's implementer runs into it. The cost of a missed harvest is paid late and in someone else's thread.

**Evaluation:** the process-log issues (#428, #431 and their predecessors) record harvest misses together with the comment and child involved. Replaying those pairs gives a labelled set before the step is enabled anywhere. This is the [re-ranking](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/rerank_typesafe.md) pattern; a ranked list doesn't need a threshold to be useful.

**Constraints shared with the other TypeSafe proposals:**
- **Opt-in and advisory.** If `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` is missing, the step skips and says so loudly, and the run goes on exactly as it does today. The opt-in knob goes in [docs/KNOBS.md](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/docs/KNOBS.md), which `test_skills_knob_inventory.py` requires.
- **Data leaves the machine.** This sends repo text to typesafe.ai. Today the only API call any skill script makes is `measure-context.sh --exact`'s token count, and that sends no text to be judged. Some cohort repos are private, so the opt-in is per repo, never cohort-wide.
- **Pin the model.** Use `jev-1.13.0`, not `jev-latest`. The alias moves when a new version ships, and thresholds tuned against one version don't carry to the next ([models](https://docs.typesafe.ai/models.md#aliases)).
- **Measure before gating.** Collect a labelled set and measure agreement before any threshold changes what the run does. A typed answer guarantees the shape of the answer, not that it is true.

Sibling TypeSafe proposals: #435 section class · #436 harvest · #437 CR tiers · #438 stale issue prose · #439 epic slotting · #440 backlog scoring · #441 bare-digit counts · #442 semantic no-loss · #443 close-gate requirements · #444 process-log recurrence · #445 cross-repo present tense · #446 pre-batch body decay · #447 index-line accuracy.

item.title: reviewing-code: a TypeSafe Score per finding as a calibration check on its severity tier
item.body:
**What:** Phase 3 sorts findings into 🔴 Bugs / 🟡 Issues to fix / 💭 Minor based on the reviewer's judgment alone. Nothing checks a tier call. Yet the tier steers the user's directives, especially a blanket `address the findings`, which answers every tier in one pass.

**Proposal:** after Phase 3.5 verification, an optional script reads each finding (the required `What:` / `Why it matters:` / `Suggested fix:` labels make that parse reliable) plus the diff hunk at its `file:line`, and sends one [TypeSafe](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/system-one.md) request with:
- a **Score** per finding on three levels, each describing a concrete situation (e.g. *produces wrong output, a crash, or data loss on an input the code can reach* / *a correctness or maintenance cost a user or later change will hit* / *style, naming, or an observation with no failure attached*);
- a **Noul** per finding: "Does `findings[i].why` name a concrete failure, meaning specific inputs or state leading to a specific wrong outcome?"

Where the Score's peak level differs from the reviewer's tier, or its [confidence](https://docs.typesafe.ai/confidence.md) is low, the report marks the finding *tier contested*. The user then sees which calls to look at before giving directives. The reviewer's tier stays authoritative, and nothing is re-tiered automatically.

**Why it matters:** a finding that is really a bug, filed under 💭, can be stetted with the rest of its tier. A 🔴 with no failure scenario costs the user a careful read for nothing.

**Prerequisite:** directives aren't recorded durably today. Only fixed findings land, as `CR N` commits, and stet/GH decisions disappear. Recording each finding's tier and directive over a few rounds builds the labelled set; without it there is nothing to measure agreement against.

**Scope:** the variants (`-php`, `-python-fastapi`, `-python-click`) are self-contained, so start in the baseline and copy to the variants only once agreement has been measured.

**Constraints shared with the other TypeSafe proposals:**
- **Opt-in and advisory.** If `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` is missing, the step skips and says so loudly, and the run goes on exactly as it does today. The opt-in knob goes in [docs/KNOBS.md](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/docs/KNOBS.md), which `test_skills_knob_inventory.py` requires.
- **Data leaves the machine.** This sends repo text to typesafe.ai. Today the only API call any skill script makes is `measure-context.sh --exact`'s token count, and that sends no text to be judged. Some cohort repos are private, so the opt-in is per repo, never cohort-wide.
- **Pin the model.** Use `jev-1.13.0`, not `jev-latest`. The alias moves when a new version ships, and thresholds tuned against one version don't carry to the next ([models](https://docs.typesafe.ai/models.md#aliases)).
- **Measure before gating.** Collect a labelled set and measure agreement before any threshold changes what the run does. A typed answer guarantees the shape of the answer, not that it is true.

Sibling TypeSafe proposals: #435 section class · #436 harvest · #437 CR tiers · #438 stale issue prose · #439 epic slotting · #440 backlog scoring · #441 bare-digit counts · #442 semantic no-loss · #443 close-gate requirements · #444 process-log recurrence · #445 cross-repo present tense · #446 pre-batch body decay · #447 index-line accuracy.

item.title: curating-context: a TypeSafe Noul per sentence flags prose that still calls a closed issue pending (or an open one done)
item.body:
**What:** `verify-facts.sh --issues` resolves each `#N` and stops at the reference. A closed one comes back as `TRUE issue <file> #N closed — check whether the prose still describes it as pending` ([verify-facts.sh:366](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/skills/curating-context/scripts/verify-facts.sh#L366)). [fact-verification.md](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/skills/curating-context/references/fact-verification.md#issue-and-pr-references) calls the sentence around that reference "the most common real staleness in the cohort's 'Known Issues' sections." The agent re-reads every such sentence, and nothing puts the stale ones first.

**Proposal:** a separate optional script that reads `verify-facts.sh`'s TSV, so the verifier itself stays deterministic and free. For each issue row, code extracts the sentence or list item holding the reference and fetches the issue's title, state, `stateReason` and `closedAt`. One [TypeSafe](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/system-one.md) request then carries a **Noul** per row:
- **closed ref:** "Does `sentence` describe `ref` as still open, pending, planned, or blocking something?" (e.g. "pending in #42" after #42 shipped);
- **open ref, the reverse case:** "Does `sentence` describe `ref` as done, fixed, or shipped?" (prose that got ahead of the issue).

The output is the TSV with a probability column, sorted so the likely-stale sentences come first.

**Must not:** change a verdict. The row stays TRUE, a stale sentence gets rewritten (class C) rather than deleted, and only FALSE is ever eligible for deletion.

**Why it matters:** this is one narrow judgment on one sentence, with the evidence that decides it attached. That is a natural fit for a fast typed judgment. The agent's reading then goes to the few sentences that are stale, not to every reference.

**Evaluation:** cheap labels already exist. `git log -S'#N'` over the cohort's policy files finds sentences rewritten after their issue closed, which are positives. References that survived several curations untouched are negatives. Of the TypeSafe proposals, I'd build this one first: it is the smallest and the easiest to measure.

**Shared constraints** (the same as #435–#437):
- **Opt-in and advisory.** With no `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` the step skips loudly and the run is unchanged. The knob goes in [docs/KNOBS.md](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/docs/KNOBS.md).
- **Data leaves the machine.** Repo and issue text goes to typesafe.ai, so the opt-in is per repo. Private cohort repos decide for themselves.
- **Pin the model:** `jev-1.13.0`, not `jev-latest`.
- **Measure before gating.** Collect a labelled set and measure agreement before any threshold changes what the run does.

item.title: coordinating-epics: a TypeSafe Choice per new item proposes its §3 slot, with a Noul per open child for duplicates
item.body:
**What:** at each check-in, `scan.sh` reports new items through three cursors (number watermark, updated-since, commit range). [check-in.md §3](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/skills/coordinating-epics/references/check-in.md#3-re-scan-and-slot) then classifies each new item as **child**, **closed-in-fact**, **split**, **out of epic**, **duplicate**, or **park**, which is a closed set of six. The coordinator classifies each item by reading it, and a re-scan can return many items at once.

**Proposal:** an optional script that reads `scan.json` and proposes a slot for each item. One [TypeSafe](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/system-one.md) request per item, with the item (title, body, labels, state, linked PRs), the epic's goal and child lines, and the open children in the state:
- a **Choice** over the six outcomes, each option's criteria taken from §3's own definitions;
- a **Noul** per open child: "Does `item` describe the same work as `open_children[j]`?" The top match names the duplicate's survivor;
- a **Noul**: "Does `item` contain both work this epic covers and work it does not?" This is a signal for a split.

The output is the proposed slot, its probabilities and confidence, and the top duplicate candidate, written beside `scan.json`. Low confidence means the item gets a full read.

**Must not:** act. *closed-in-fact* still needs §1's evidence (merged, CI green on the final SHA, live), and all edits still go through `epic-edit.sh`, whose refusals are unchanged. A proposal only orders the coordinator's reading.

**Why it matters:** a duplicate or an out-of-epic item that gets slotted as a child costs a whole hand-off. The six outcomes are already defined, which is exactly the shape a Choice needs.

**Shares a loader with #436:** both read the same state (new comments or items, open children). Build them on one fetch.

**Evaluation:** where check-in log lines and epic edit history record how past items were slotted, they form the labelled set. Replay them before enabling the step.

**Shared constraints** (the same as #435–#437):
- **Opt-in and advisory.** With no `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` the step skips loudly and the run is unchanged. The knob goes in [docs/KNOBS.md](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/docs/KNOBS.md).
- **Data leaves the machine.** Repo and issue text goes to typesafe.ai, so the opt-in is per repo. Private cohort repos decide for themselves.
- **Pin the model:** `jev-1.13.0`, not `jev-latest`.
- **Measure before gating.** Collect a labelled set and measure agreement before any threshold changes what the run does.

Sibling TypeSafe proposals: #435 section class · #436 harvest · #437 CR tiers · #438 stale issue prose · #439 epic slotting · #440 backlog scoring · #441 bare-digit counts · #442 semantic no-loss · #443 close-gate requirements · #444 process-log recurrence · #445 cross-repo present tense · #446 pre-batch body decay · #447 index-line accuracy.

slot.instructions: `epic` is a GitHub issue that tracks a body of work through a checklist of child issues: `epic.goal` says what it covers, `epic.scope` holds its boundary decisions and rules, `epic.children` its checklist lines (done: ticked), and `epic.parked` what waits on a trigger. `item` is an issue filed since the coordinator last looked, with its state now. Which slot does the coordinator give `item` in this epic?

criteria.child: Work this epic covers and that should be done now or in order: it gets its own checklist line, slotted by dependency. A follow-up to a child, a bug in what a child shipped, or a piece split off a child is a child.
criteria.closed-in-fact: Work this epic covers that is already delivered: the item is closed, or a child's merged change already did it, so it is verified, linked and closed with evidence instead of slotted.
criteria.split: The item mixes work this epic covers with work it doesn't, so the epic's part is filed as its own issue and the rest is left out.
criteria.out of epic: Not this epic's work: another skill, service, area or epic, a record or notice with no action, or tooling around the epic rather than its work. It is said so plainly and cross-linked only where it changes a remaining step.
criteria.duplicate: The same work as an existing child or another open issue, so it is closed in favour of that one.
criteria.park: This epic's concern, but not to be done yet: it waits on a trigger (another repo, a decision, a date, an event) and goes in the parked table with that trigger.

item.title: orchestrating-issue-backlog: pre-score the Step 4 rubric with TypeSafe Scores, weights stay in the formula
item.body:
**What:** [Step 4](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/skills/orchestrating-issue-backlog/SKILL.md#step-4-scoring-rubric) scores every issue on three dimensions with concrete 1–3 levels, then combines them with a formula the user may re-weight: `(Foundation × 2) + (Correctness × 2) + Scope`. The agent assigns each score by reading.

**Proposal:** an optional script that pre-scores the backlog. This is TypeSafe's [composite-scoring](https://docs.typesafe.ai/patterns/composite-scoring.md) pattern: Jev scores the dimensions, and the weights stay in code.
- **Correctness Risk** and **Scope Clarity:** one **Score** each per issue, with the rubric's level descriptions as the levels, verbatim.
- **"Does this issue name a decision it leaves unresolved?"** One **Noul** per issue. This feeds the existing *decide-then-rescore* rule directly, so the decisions to raise at the approval gate surface before the table is presented.
- **Foundation Leverage** is relational, not a property of one issue. Ask one **Noul** per ordered pair: "Would resolving `issues[i]` unblock or simplify `issues[j]`?" Code then maps the count of confident pairs onto levels 1–3. Pairs grow as n²: for 40 issues that is 1,560 questions. Prefilter pairs in code (shared paths, labels, cross-references) and measure the request sizes against the 64k-per-request / 32k-per-question limits before choosing a batching scheme.

The table shows Jev's scores beside the agent's. A score with low confidence, or one that disagrees with the agent's, marks an issue to read in full.

**Bonus:** when the user re-weights the formula at the gate, the table recomputes without re-running inference, because the judgments haven't changed.

**Must not:** replace the HARD-GATE. The user still approves the scored table, and blast radius stays a sequencing input computed by code.

**Evaluation:** the approved tables in cohort design docs, and the re-scores recorded in process-log entries (e.g. the 14 → 16 move in the 2026-08-11 observo log), are the labels.

**Shared constraints** (the same as #435–#437):
- **Opt-in and advisory.** With no `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` the step skips loudly and the run is unchanged. The knob goes in [docs/KNOBS.md](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/docs/KNOBS.md).
- **Data leaves the machine.** Repo and issue text goes to typesafe.ai, so the opt-in is per repo. Private cohort repos decide for themselves.
- **Pin the model:** `jev-1.13.0`, not `jev-latest`.
- **Measure before gating.** Collect a labelled set and measure agreement before any threshold changes what the run does.

item.title: curating-context: check-counts' bare-digit gap, closed by an advisory TypeSafe Noul that tells a tally from a port, code or version
item.body:
**What:** `check-counts.sh` deliberately skips bare digits ([its --help](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/skills/curating-context/scripts/check-counts.sh)). In a policy file a bare digit is "overwhelmingly a status code, a port, a standard or a version, and a gate that cries wolf on `403` and `ISO 8601` is a gate someone deletes." The help names the gap this leaves: "\"182 hx-get reveals\" unbackticked passes."

**Proposal:** an optional advisory pass that covers that gap without making the gate noisy:
- **Code finds the candidates:** clauses with a bare digit, outside fenced code, that the deterministic class didn't already report. It splits clauses the way the existing class does.
- **One [TypeSafe](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/system-one.md) request, one Noul per clause:** "Does the number in `clause` state how many of something exist in this repo or project, a tally that goes stale when the repo changes, rather than a status code, port, version, date, standard, or configured limit?"
- **Two more Nouls for each likely tally,** suggesting which warrant fits: *enumerated* ("Are the counted things listed in `section`?") and *stable* ("Is this count structural, so it can't change without rewriting the sentence?"). The other two remedies, attaching the counting command or dropping the precision, stay the reader's call.

The output is a separate advisory section of the report, **outside** the `counts` telemetry field.

**Must not:** enter the gate. The deterministic class, its closed warrant set and `.skills/context-counts-ok` are all unchanged. An advisory hit needs no acknowledgement entry, and no warrant is ever written on the reader's behalf.

**Why it matters:** the gap exists only because a regex can't tell `403` from `182 reveals`. That distinction is exactly the semantic judgment a typed yes/no is for.

**Evaluation:** the bare digits across the cohort's policy files are few enough to label by hand once. Measure precision on that set before any repo enables the pass.

**Shared constraints** (the same as #435–#437):
- **Opt-in and advisory.** With no `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` the step skips loudly and the run is unchanged. The knob goes in [docs/KNOBS.md](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/docs/KNOBS.md).
- **Data leaves the machine.** Repo and issue text goes to typesafe.ai, so the opt-in is per repo. Private cohort repos decide for themselves.
- **Pin the model:** `jev-1.13.0`, not `jev-latest`.
- **Measure before gating.** Collect a labelled set and measure agreement before any threshold changes what the run does.

Sibling TypeSafe proposals: #435 section class · #436 harvest · #437 CR tiers · #438 stale issue prose · #439 epic slotting · #440 backlog scoring · #441 bare-digit counts · #442 semantic no-loss · #443 close-gate requirements · #444 process-log recurrence · #445 cross-repo present tense · #446 pre-batch body decay · #447 index-line accuracy.

slot.instructions: `epic` is a GitHub issue that tracks a body of work through a checklist of child issues: `epic.goal` says what it covers, `epic.scope` holds its boundary decisions and rules, `epic.children` its checklist lines (done: ticked), and `epic.parked` what waits on a trigger. `item` is an issue filed since the coordinator last looked, with its state now. Which slot does the coordinator give `item` in this epic?

criteria.child: Work this epic covers and that should be done now or in order: it gets its own checklist line, slotted by dependency. A follow-up to a child, a bug in what a child shipped, or a piece split off a child is a child.
criteria.closed-in-fact: Work this epic covers that is already delivered: the item is closed, or a child's merged change already did it, so it is verified, linked and closed with evidence instead of slotted.
criteria.split: The item mixes work this epic covers with work it doesn't, so the epic's part is filed as its own issue and the rest is left out.
criteria.out of epic: Not this epic's work: another skill, service, area or epic, a record or notice with no action, or tooling around the epic rather than its work. It is said so plainly and cross-linked only where it changes a remaining step.
criteria.duplicate: The same work as an existing child or another open issue, so it is closed in favour of that one.
criteria.park: This epic's concern, but not to be done yet: it waits on a trigger (another repo, a decision, a date, an event) and goes in the parked table with that trigger.

item.title: curating-context: prove-no-loss --semantic, a TypeSafe Noul per base sentence asks whether a tightened section still states its rule
item.body:
**What:** `prove-no-loss.sh` enforces curating-context's iron law with two matchers ([its --help](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/skills/curating-context/scripts/prove-no-loss.sh)). **Whole-line matching** sees a class-C tightening as 100% lost, because "a paragraph is one line." **`--claims`** checks atoms: backticked spans, `#NNN` references, link targets, bare URLs. Neither can see what a tightening most often drops, which is the *rule* between the atoms: a "never", a condition ("only when …"), an exception, or a reason. A rewrite can keep every atom and still change what the section tells an agent to do, and the verdict comes back `ok`.

**Proposal:** an optional, advisory `--semantic` pass for sections a run tightened:
- **Code pairs the sections:** each base section with its successor (same heading, or the one the run's `retarget` / `tighten` warrant names). It splits the base section into sentences and list items.
- **One [TypeSafe](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/system-one.md) request per section pair,** with `after_section` and the base sentences in the state. It asks a **Noul** per base sentence: "Does `after_section` still state what `base_sentences[i]` requires or forbids, including its conditions, exceptions and stated reason?" This is the [citation-check](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/citation_check.md) pattern: one claim checked against one source.
- **Output:** base sentences sorted by how unlikely they are to have survived, printed after the existing report.

**Must not:** move the verdict. `ok` / `failed` / `skipped`, exit 3, and both warrant files are unchanged. A low Noul means "re-read this sentence against the rewrite before you commit". It is not a loss, and never a pass either. The pass reports in its own section, so the `no_loss` and `claims_*` telemetry fields keep their meaning.

**Why it matters:** the iron law exists to stop content being dropped, and a tightening is the edit most likely to drop it without anyone seeing. Today the only check on a rewritten rule is that the agent re-read it.

**Evaluation:** cohort curation diffs that a later review corrected (a reverted or re-added clause) are positives, and tightenings that stood are negatives. Measure recall on the positives first: a miss here is worse than a false alarm.

**Related:** #435 classifies sections *before* the edit; this checks the edit *after*.

**Shared constraints** (the same as #435):

item.title: shipping-work: a TypeSafe Noul per issue requirement builds a requirements-vs-commits table for the Step 6 close gate
item.body:
**What:** every shipping-work variant has the same Step 6 HARD-GATE ([baseline](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/skills/shipping-work/SKILL.md#step-6--close-github-issues)): "Re-read the issue body. Confirm each stated requirement is addressed in commits. If any requirement is missing: do NOT close." The check is a single act of reading, and nothing in what the user sees shows which requirements were matched to which commits.

**Proposal:** an optional script that runs before `close-issue.sh` and produces a requirements table:
- **Code extracts the requirements** from the issue body (checklist items, list items, paragraphs under a "Suggested fix" or "Acceptance" heading) and the evidence from the commit range: messages, changed paths, and the hunks of each changed file.
- **One [TypeSafe](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/system-one.md) request per issue,** with the requirements and the evidence in the state. It asks a **Noul** per requirement: "Do the changes in `commits` address `requirements[i]` as stated, not just touch the same area?"
- **Output:** a requirement / probability / closest-commit table. The agent shows it at the gate, and a weak row turns into the gate's existing question: descope or continue?

**Must not:** close anything, or count as the gate's verification. The HARD-GATE's wording is unchanged, and a high probability doesn't excuse re-reading the body.

**Why it matters:** an issue closed with a missing requirement is reopened by whoever runs into the gap, usually long after the context is gone. A table makes a requirement that got skimmed past visible at the one moment it is cheap to act on.

**Costs to measure first:**
- **Context limits:** diffs push against the 64k-per-request / 32k-per-question limits. Send hunks scoped to each requirement's paths, not the whole diff.
- **Four copies:** the four variants (`shipping-work`, `-php`, `-python-fastapi`, `-python-click`) are self-contained, so the script and its SKILL.md step land in each. Start in the baseline, measure, then copy.

**Evaluation:** in this repo, issues closed and later reopened, plus "descoped to #N" comments, give positives. Issues closed and never revisited give negatives.

**Shared constraints** (the same as #435):
- **Opt-in and advisory.** With no `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` the step skips loudly and the run is unchanged. The knob goes in [docs/KNOBS.md](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/docs/KNOBS.md).
- **Data leaves the machine.** Repo and issue text goes to typesafe.ai, so the opt-in is per repo. Private cohort repos decide for themselves.
- **Pin the model:** `jev-1.13.0`, not `jev-latest`.
- **Measure before gating.** Collect a labelled set and measure agreement before any threshold changes what the run does.

item.title: process logs: TypeSafe Nouls spot a finding's second occurrence, the signal the promotion rule waits for
item.body:
**What:** three skills keep a per-run process log: [coordinating-epics](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/skills/coordinating-epics/references/process-log.md), [orchestrating-issue-backlog](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/skills/orchestrating-issue-backlog/references/process-log.md) and [patching-hosts](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/skills/patching-hosts/references/process-log.md). Each promotes a recurring pattern into the skill and lists it under *Rules promoted into the skill* with the findings it came from. coordinating-epics states the rule as "a pattern that recurs in two runs, or that prevented damage once, is promoted." patching-hosts adds where a rule goes: a pattern that recurs on one environment goes into that environment's profile, and one that recurs across environments goes into the core. Spotting the recurrence is done by memory. A new run's findings have to be matched against every earlier entry's findings and every promoted rule, and as the logs grow, a second occurrence can go unnoticed.

**Proposal:** an optional script that runs when an entry is journaled. Code parses the new entry's findings, the promoted rules, and the earlier entries' unpromoted findings. Then one [TypeSafe](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/system-one.md) request per new finding asks:
- a **Noul** per promoted rule: "Is `finding` another instance of `rules[j]`?" A high value means the finding should be cited under that rule, not re-promoted;
- a **Noul** per earlier unpromoted finding: "Do `finding` and `prior[k]` describe the same failure, even in different words or repos?" A high value means a **promotion candidate**: the second occurrence the rule is waiting for;
- a **Choice** over the skill's SKILL.md and reference headings (for patching-hosts, also its `environments/<id>.md` profiles), plus *none*: "Which section owns the step this finding is about?" The answer names where a promoted rule would land.

**Output:** for each finding, any existing-rule matches, promotion candidates with the earlier finding's run and number, and the owning section. All of it goes into the journaling agent's view.

**Must not:** promote anything. Promotion stays a judged edit to SKILL.md, made under the self-budget ratchet.

**Why it matters:** this rule is how a run's lessons reach the skill, and it depends on someone remembering that they've seen a pattern before. Across three skills, many runs and hundreds of numbered findings, that memory is the bottleneck. The section map also turns the logs into data: which sections produce the most lessons is a measured signal for which sections to revise.

**Evaluation:** the *Rules promoted into the skill* lists already record which findings were judged to be the same pattern (e.g. "From 2026-10-09 archiver (10, 17), 2026-10-13 status (18) …"). Those groupings are a ready-made labelled set for the pair Noul.

**Shared constraints** (the same as #435):
- **Opt-in and advisory.** With no `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` the step skips loudly and the run is unchanged. The knob goes in [docs/KNOBS.md](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/docs/KNOBS.md).
- **Data leaves the machine.** Repo and issue text goes to typesafe.ai, so the opt-in is per repo. Private cohort repos decide for themselves.
- **Pin the model:** `jev-1.13.0`, not `jev-latest`.
- **Measure before gating.** Collect a labelled set and measure agreement before any threshold changes what the run does.

item.title: docs conventions: an advisory TypeSafe Choice per added sentence flags a present-tense claim about another repo, without the network gate the convention rejected
item.body:
**What:** [docs/CONVENTIONS.md § Claims about another repository](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/docs/CONVENTIONS.md#claims-about-another-repository) bans stating another repo's current state in the present tense ("every cohort repo runs…"). A claim must be either **a shape without names** or **a dated observation** with the command that re-derives it, and **an event** needs neither form. The rule came from #322: a present-tense claim about `CannObserv/power-map`'s `scripts/pre-ship.sh` was cited as evidence two days after the file was deleted. The convention also says **"Do not gate this"**, because a test that queries GitHub for thirteen repos adds a network dependency to the suite. So today nothing catches a violation except a reviewer's eye.

**Proposal:** the gate the convention rejected would *verify* each claim against GitHub. Spotting the banned form is a different judgment, one that needs no GitHub call: is this sentence about another repo, and which of the convention's forms is it in? An optional, advisory script runs over the **added lines of a diff** in `*.md` files:
- **Code** splits the added prose into sentences, skipping fenced code and inline code spans.
- **One [TypeSafe](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/system-one.md) request per diff,** a **Choice** per sentence over {**shape without names**, **dated observation**, **event**, **present-tense claim about another repo's current state**, **not about another repo**}. Each option's criteria quote the convention's own definition and examples.
- **Output:** the sentences whose peak is *present-tense claim*, with the convention's two allowed rewrites linked.

**Where it runs:** beside `pre-ship.sh` or in reviewing-code's documentation pass, **never inside the pytest suite**. That keeps the convention's network-dependency reason intact.

**Must not:** block a commit. A flagged sentence is a prompt to choose a form; the author may decide it's an event.

**Why it matters:** the convention is right that verification can't be gated, but detection can be advisory, and a present-tense claim slips through review because it reads as a plain fact.

**Evaluation:** `git log -p` over `docs/` and `skills/**/*.md` finds sentences rewritten from present tense into an observation, which are positives (e.g. the #322 fix). The convention's own examples are fixed test cases.

**Shared constraints** (the same as #435):
- **Opt-in and advisory.** With no `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` the step skips loudly and the run is unchanged. The knob goes in [docs/KNOBS.md](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/docs/KNOBS.md).
- **Data leaves the machine.** Repo and issue text goes to typesafe.ai, so the opt-in is per repo. Private cohort repos decide for themselves.
- **Pin the model:** `jev-1.13.0`, not `jev-latest`.
- **Measure before gating.** Collect a labelled set and measure agreement before any threshold changes what the run does.

item.title: orchestrating-issue-backlog: at each batch boundary, a TypeSafe Noul per (claim, merged hunk) flags issue-body decay before workers launch
item.body:
**What:** orchestrating-issue-backlog carries a **runtime note on issue-body decay** ([SKILL.md](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/skills/orchestrating-issue-backlog/SKILL.md)): "the backlog is N sequential mutations of what the bodies describe, so re-verify the specifics of any issue whose files an earlier batch touched (Worker step 5); the later the batch, the staler the body." reviewing-architecture records how bad this gets, measured: a 13-issue backlog carved from one review "carried a material error in **every** issue body by implementation time." One finding's branch-point table was 5 of 7 stale, because an earlier batch had changed a column type (process-log 2026-08-09 observo). The re-verify step relies on each worker noticing that its issue's files moved.

**Proposal:** an optional script the coordinator runs at each batch boundary, before workers launch:
- **Code** collects, for each issue in the next batch, the hunks merged since the issue was filed (or since its last "Changed since filed" comment) that touch the paths, symbols or tables its body cites. It also splits the body into claim sentences.
- **One [TypeSafe](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/system-one.md) request per issue,** a **Noul** per (claim, hunk): "Does `hunks[k]` make `claims[i]` untrue or out of date, for example a line, count, signature, column type or file it states?"
- **Output:** for each issue, the flagged claims with the hunk and merge commit that invalidates them. The worker's brief carries it, and the coordinator posts it as a "Changed since filed" comment, as coordinating-epics does.

**Must not:** edit issue bodies or reorder batches. The worker still re-verifies (step 5), and the script tells it where to look first.

**Why it matters:** the decay concentrates in the later batches, where the work is hardest. A worker that trusts a stale body re-does work or implements against a shape that's gone.

**Shares machinery with #436 and #439:** the same fetch of issues and comments, and the same paragraph and hunk splitting. Build it on that loader.

**Evaluation:** the Step 5 rescope comments and process-log entries record which bodies were stale and why. Replaying their batches gives labelled (claim, hunk) pairs.

**Shared constraints** (the same as #435):
- **Opt-in and advisory.** With no `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` the step skips loudly and the run is unchanged. The knob goes in [docs/KNOBS.md](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/docs/KNOBS.md).
- **Data leaves the machine.** Repo and issue text goes to typesafe.ai, so the opt-in is per repo. Private cohort repos decide for themselves.
- **Pin the model:** `jev-1.13.0`, not `jev-latest`.
- **Measure before gating.** Collect a labelled set and measure agreement before any threshold changes what the run does.

item.title: curating-context: a TypeSafe Noul per index line checks it still describes its doc, and flags sibling lines that steal a topic's route
item.body:
**What:** an agent picks a reference doc by its **line in the policy file's index**, and curating-context has measured that being reachable through links doesn't make a doc findable ([cohort-patterns.md § Reachable is not routable](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/skills/curating-context/references/cohort-patterns.md#reachable-is-not-routable)). A doc named nowhere in the policy file fell from 12/12 to 2/12 tasks reaching it, and a sibling line that named a topic better took every first hop. `docs_unindexed` counts docs with **no** line. Nothing checks whether an existing line still **describes** its doc after the doc grew, split, or absorbed a demotion. `check-counts.sh` bounds a line's *length*, not its accuracy.

**Proposal:** an optional, advisory pass in Phase 6.5:
- **Code** pairs each index line with its target doc's headings and opening paragraph, and lists the doc's `##` topics.
- **One [TypeSafe](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/system-one.md) request per policy file:**
  - a **Noul** per index line: "Would an agent reading only `index_line` expect to find what `doc.headings` covers, with no major topic missing and none claimed that isn't there?"
  - a **Noul** per (doc topic, index line naming a *different* doc): "Does `index_line` claim `topic` more directly than its own doc's line does?" This flags the sibling line that steals a route.
- **Output:** inaccurate lines and topic collisions, ranked, beside `check-seams.sh`'s report.

**Scope:** this checks whether a line *describes its doc accurately*. It does not *simulate routing*. Whether an agent actually finds the doc is a property of the agent's model, and the measurement in cohort-patterns.md should keep using the real agent. Jev standing in for it would measure a different model.

**Must not:** rewrite index lines, or count toward any gated telemetry field.

**Why it matters:** an inaccurate index line is a routing loss that every task pays and no current field records. The curation that caused it, a demotion that grew a doc, is exactly the run in which nobody re-reads that line.

**Evaluation:** index-line rewrites in cohort curation diffs (a line re-worded after its doc changed) are positives. The routing measurements above give a small set with known outcomes.

**Shared constraints** (the same as #435):
- **Opt-in and advisory.** With no `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` the step skips loudly and the run is unchanged. The knob goes in [docs/KNOBS.md](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/docs/KNOBS.md).
- **Data leaves the machine.** Repo and issue text goes to typesafe.ai, so the opt-in is per repo. Private cohort repos decide for themselves.
- **Pin the model:** `jev-1.13.0`, not `jev-latest`.
- **Measure before gating.** Collect a labelled set and measure agreement before any threshold changes what the run does.

item.title: typesafe: stdlib client, opt-in knob and skip-loudly contract for skill scripts (foundation for #435–#447)
item.body:
Foundation child for the TypeSafe epic (#451). Every proposal in #435–#447 calls the same endpoint under the same constraints. This lands that plumbing once, before any proposal builds on it.

**What:** a TypeSafe client and contract shared by skill scripts:
- **A standard-library client.** `_typesafe.py`, `urllib` only: `POST https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone` with bearer auth, JSON in and out ([API reference](https://docs.typesafe.ai/api.md)). Every skill script imports only the standard library today [measured 2026-10-19: the import set across `skills/*/scripts/*.py`], and the API's one endpoint doesn't justify breaking that. So: no `typesafe-sdk` dependency (PyPI 0.7.5).
- **Pinned model** `jev-1.13.0`, overridable by flag for evaluation runs only. The response's `model` field is echoed on stderr.
- **Opt-in knob** `.skills/typesafe`, read in the knobs' usual order: the env var, then the file, then a default of **off**. Add it to [docs/KNOBS.md](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/blob/main/docs/KNOBS.md) so `test_skills_knob_inventory.py` holds it. Opting in is per repo, because judged text leaves the machine.
- **Key** from `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` only, never logged and never on a command line.
- **Skip-loudly contract.** A step that isn't opted in, or has no key, prints one line saying which and exits with a distinct code (proposed `3`, "skipped"), so a caller can't read a skip as an empty result. Network or API failures exit `2` with the server's status and message on stderr. A `429` honours `retry-after` and retries a bounded number of times.
- **Size guard.** Estimate each request against the documented 64k-per-request / 32k-per-question limits and refuse an oversize one before sending.
- **One copy per consuming skill,** held byte-equal by a structural test. A skill is vendored on its own, so it can't import another skill's scripts. Precedent: `TestPythonClickHelperByteEquality`.
- **No network in the suite.** Structural tests drive the client through an injectable fake transport. One `-m integration` test (billed, never gated) makes a single live call and checks the echoed model ID.

**Done when:**
- the client, knob, contract and byte-equality test are merged;
- `scripts/pre-ship.sh` is green;
- one live integration call has returned `jev-1.13.0`, run once `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` exists (see the epic's Waits).

item.title: typesafe: evaluation harness — labelled JSONL in, agreement and calibration out
item.body:
Foundation child for the TypeSafe epic (#451). Every proposal in #435–#447 says to **measure before gating**. This gives them one way to measure.

**What:** a repo-level dev tool, `scripts/typesafe-eval.py`, that is not shipped inside any skill:
- **Input:** a labelled JSONL set, one row per case: `id`, `state`, `questions`, `expected` (a choice, a level, or a yes/no), and an optional `source`. It also accepts a cached-responses file, so a re-run replays without calling the API.
- **Output:**
  - for Choice/Score: agreement, a confusion matrix, and accuracy by confidence band;
  - for Noul: precision and recall at a sweep of thresholds, plus a calibration table;
  - in every case: the model ID that answered, and the token usage.
- **Uses SUB1's client.** The evaluator owns no HTTP code.

**Boundary:** a labelled set drawn from a **private** cohort repo is never committed here. It stays in scratch or off-repo, and only its aggregate result is posted on the child's issue. A committed fixture must come from public material (this repo, its issues, or public cohort repos).

**Done when:** the tool is merged with structural tests that run on a fake transport and a cached-responses file, `--help` documents the JSONL schema, and `scripts/pre-ship.sh` is green.

item.title: reviewing-code: record each finding's tier and directive (the labelled set #437 needs)
item.body:
Split from #437 by the TypeSafe epic (#451). #437's Score per finding can't be measured until something records how findings were *judged*. Today only fixed findings leave a trace, as `CR N` commits. Stet and GH decisions disappear, and so does the tier each finding was given.

**What:** reviewing-code records, per finding, its number, tier, `file:line` and the user's directive (`fix` / `stet` / `GH` / blanket `address the findings`) in an append-only ledger. The location and format are this child's design call. That ledger is the labelled set #437 needs, and it can also measure the reviewer on its own: a high stet rate in one tier is a signal even without TypeSafe.

**Scope:** the baseline `reviewing-code` first, and the variants only after the format has held for a few rounds. Like any other repo file, the ledger is subject to the private-content rule: a consuming private repo keeps its own.

**Done when:** a review round run under the new step leaves one ledger row per finding, including the stetted ones, and `scripts/pre-ship.sh` is green.

slot.instructions: `epic` is a GitHub issue that tracks a body of work through a checklist of child issues: `epic.goal` says what it covers, `epic.scope` holds its boundary decisions and rules, `epic.children` its checklist lines (done: ticked), and `epic.parked` what waits on a trigger. `item` is an issue filed since the coordinator last looked, with its state now. Which slot does the coordinator give `item` in this epic?

criteria.child: Work this epic covers and that should be done now or in order: it gets its own checklist line, slotted by dependency. A follow-up to a child, a bug in what a child shipped, or a piece split off a child is a child.
criteria.closed-in-fact: Work this epic covers that is already delivered: the item is closed, or a child's merged change already did it, so it is verified, linked and closed with evidence instead of slotted.
criteria.split: The item mixes work this epic covers with work it doesn't, so the epic's part is filed as its own issue and the rest is left out.
criteria.out of epic: Not this epic's work: another skill, service, area or epic, a record or notice with no action, or tooling around the epic rather than its work. It is said so plainly and cross-linked only where it changes a remaining step.
criteria.duplicate: The same work as an existing child or another open issue, so it is closed in favour of that one.
criteria.park: This epic's concern, but not to be done yet: it waits on a trigger (another repo, a decision, a date, an event) and goes in the parked table with that trigger.

item.title: Epic: TypeSafe advisory judgments across the skills (#435–#447)
item.body:
Turns the thirteen TypeSafe proposals (#435–#447) into opt-in, advisory steps in the skills they name. Each step calls TypeSafe's Jev model for a narrow typed judgment, and none changes a verdict, a gate or a GitHub write. Done when every proposal has either shipped with its agreement measured on a labelled set, or been closed or parked with its measurement as the reason.

- **Last check-in:** 2026-10-19T19:55:40Z
- **Last issue seen:** #451
- **Last verified SHA:** ae5338c
- **Next:** #448, brief on the issue (https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/issues/448#issuecomment-6275994142)
- **Last probe:** 2026-10-19T20:31Z

## Order

Operator's rule: none given at creation; the coordinator proposed this one. Challenge it here.

> Foundation first; then one skill cluster at a time, cheapest-to-measure first within a cluster; nothing that touches a gate, or ships in several variants or skills, until the advisory pattern has been measured once.

Tiebreaks the coordinator added, numbered so the operator can challenge one:
1. Dependency outranks size: #448 before everything; #449 before any child that sets a threshold.
2. Within a cluster, the child that lands the shared piece (sentence splitter, issue/comment loader) goes first.
3. The cheaper labelled set goes first.
4. Multi-variant or multi-skill children go last, because the copy cost multiplies any design mistake.

## Boundary decisions

- Every TypeSafe step is advisory. It never changes an existing script's verdict or exit code, never passes or fails a gate, and never writes to GitHub. Proposed at creation.
- No network in the pytest suite. Structural tests use a fake transport, and live calls run only under `-m integration` (billed, never gated). Proposed at creation.
- A labelled set drawn from a private cohort repo is never committed to this public repo. Only its aggregate result is posted. Proposed at creation.
- curating-context and orchestrating-issue-backlog SKILL.md edits are net-zero in tokens, and new prose goes to `references/` (see Measured state). Proposed at creation.
- The model is pinned to `jev-1.13.0` across the epic. Moving to a later version is its own child, re-measured. Proposed at creation.
- A proposal whose measurement shows no useful agreement is closed as not planned, with the numbers. That is a successful outcome for this epic, not a failure. Proposed at creation.

## Exit criterion

Every line below is ticked on one of two kinds of evidence: shipped as an opt-in advisory step, with its agreement measured on a labelled set and posted on the issue; or closed or parked with that measurement, or its absence, as the reason. "All shipped" isn't required.

## Verify recipe

- Gate: `bash scripts/pre-ship.sh` (budget + ruff + suite) on the merged commit. CI doesn't run the suite: the two workflows are the scheduled `context-cadence.yml` and `skill-budget-exact.yml` [measured 2026-10-19]. Run at creation: green.
- Deploy: none. Live means an ancestor of `origin/main` (`git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> origin/main`), and consumers pick it up when their submodules bump.
- Baseline: `bash scripts/pre-ship.sh`, `.env` not sourced: 6,811 passed, 184 skipped, 1 warning (lapsed patching-hosts token anchors, pre-existing), 11m35s, 2026-10-19 at ae5338c. The skip set by ID is in the baseline comment.
- By deliverable:
  - **script:** `--help` exits 0. Run without the knob or the key, it prints the skip line and exits with the skip code. `skills-ref validate skills/<name>` passes.
  - **live call:** one `-m integration` run with the key, echoing `jev-1.13.0`.
  - **measurement:** the evaluator's report posted on the child's issue, with the labelled set's source (aggregate only if private).

## Tier 0 — Foundation

- [ ] #448 TypeSafe client, opt-in knob and skip-loudly contract for skill scripts · M · Brief posted 2026-10-19: exit 3 is taken, so skips are signalled through the API; canonical copy at scripts/_typesafe.py is an open operator decision (recommended). · Key wait cleared 2026-10-19: live call due in this child.
- [ ] #449 TypeSafe evaluation harness: labelled JSONL in, agreement and calibration out · S–M · after #448

## Tier 1 — curating-context advisory passes

- [ ] #438 stale prose around a closed (or open) issue reference · S · lands the shared sentence splitter
- [ ] #441 check-counts' bare-digit gap, as an advisory pass · S
- [ ] #442 prove-no-loss `--semantic`, a rule kept through a tightening · M
- [ ] #447 index lines that misdescribe their doc, and sibling lines that steal a route · M
- [ ] #435 a second reading of the Phase 3 class, plus a telemetry field · M · last in the tier, because it touches the ledger schema

## Tier 2 — issue-thread judgments

- [ ] #436 harvest candidates per (paragraph, open child), plus the repeated-limit extension in its comment · M · lands the issue/comment loader
- [ ] #439 a proposed §3 slot per new item · S–M · reuses #436's loader
- [ ] #446 issue-body decay at each batch boundary · M · orchestrating-issue-backlog; loader copied, not imported
- [ ] #440 backlog pre-scoring, plus the pair-classification extension in its comment · L · O(n²) pairs; measure request sizes first

## Tier 3 — cross-skill and gate-adjacent

- [ ] #445 present-tense claims about another repo · S · advisory, on the diff, outside the suite
- [ ] #444 process-log recurrence across three skills · M · three skills
- [ ] #443 requirements against commits at the shipping-work close gate · L · four variants

## Tier 4 — labels first

- [ ] #450 reviewing-code: record each finding's tier and directive · S · no TypeSafe; split from #437
- [ ] #437 a severity Score per finding · M · after #450 has recorded enough rounds to measure against · Split 2026-10-19: labels moved to #450 (comment on #437).

## Waits

None open. The API-key wait cleared 2026-10-19 (see Log).

## Measured state

Measured 2026-10-19 at ae5338c:
- `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` is in the repo-root `.env` (added by the operator). `GET /v1/models` returns 200 and lists only the aliases `jev-latest` and `jev-preview`. A one-question probe pinned to `jev-1.13.0` returned `"model": "jev-1.13.0"`, Noul 0.9, on 297 input tokens.
- Every `skills/*/scripts/*.py` imports only the standard library. The PyPI `typesafe-sdk` is at 0.7.5 (not used: stdlib decided).
- SKILL.md headroom (estimate against ratchet): curating-context 7,579 / 7,600 (exact 7,591 at #294's anchor); orchestrating-issue-backlog 9,183 / 9,200; coordinating-epics 4,313, reviewing-code 4,238, patching-hosts 4,035, and the shipping-work variants 3,575–4,165, each against the 6,000 standard.

item.title: test_relative_links: a backtick inside inline raw HTML opens a code span that masks a link
item.body:
Follow-up to #434, from its review (CR 379, held there as a known limit, the model change unbuilt). A child of #404 by its boundary rule: a gate the skill relies on. The same class as #416 and #434.

**What:** `test_relative_links.py`'s `_code_spans` doesn't model inline raw HTML. On GitHub, a backtick inside an inline tag (in an attribute value, say) or inside an HTML comment is part of that HTML, so it opens no code span. The gate opens one there and masks the link after it, which GitHub renders.

**Seen on** [measured 2026-10-20, at 468bf14, with `gh api markdown` and `dead_links_in`]:

| Line | GitHub renders | Gate at 468bf14 |
|---|---|---|
| `` a <span title="`">[l](gone-attr.md) y` `` | a link, inside the `span` | masked |
| `` a <!-- ` --> [l](gone-comment.md) y` `` | a link, after the comment | masked |
| `` a `<span title="` [l](kept.md) y` `` (the control) | code up to the attribute's backtick, then a link | checked (right) |

The control is the other precedence: a span that opens before the tag wins, and the tag is then code.

**Why it matters:** this is a hole, not a false red: a link a reader sees goes unchecked. Nothing in the tree hits it today [stated by #434's implementer].

**Suggested fix:** in `_code_spans`, step over an inline raw HTML construct (an open tag, a closing tag, a comment, a processing instruction, a declaration, CDATA) found before a backtick run opens a span, as CommonMark's left-to-right inline scan does. Measure each construct with `gh api markdown` before encoding it: #434 found that GitHub's parser reads some HTML rules differently from the current CommonMark spec. Keep the gate self-contained.

**Test:** the three rows above as gate cases, plus one per construct encoded, and its look-alike that isn't raw HTML (such as `<` followed by a space).

epic.title: Epic: TypeSafe advisory judgments across the skills (#435–#447)
epic.goal: Turns the thirteen TypeSafe proposals (#435–#447) into opt-in, advisory steps in the skills they name. Each step calls TypeSafe's Jev model for a narrow typed judgment, and none changes a verdict, a gate or a GitHub write. Done when every proposal has either shipped with its agreement measured on a labelled set, or been closed or parked with its measurement as the reason.

scope.text:
- Every TypeSafe step is advisory. It never changes an existing script's verdict or exit code, never passes or fails a gate, and never writes to GitHub. Proposed at creation.
- No network in the pytest suite. Structural tests use a fake transport, and live calls run only under `-m integration` (billed, never gated). Proposed at creation.
- A labelled set drawn from a private cohort repo is never committed to this public repo. Only its aggregate result is posted. Proposed at creation.
- curating-context and orchestrating-issue-backlog SKILL.md edits are net-zero in tokens, and new prose goes to `references/` (see Measured state). Proposed at creation.
- The model is pinned to `jev-1.13.0` across the epic. Moving to a later version is its own child, re-measured. Proposed at creation.
- A proposal whose measurement shows no useful agreement is closed as not planned, with the numbers. That is a successful outcome for this epic, not a failure. Proposed at creation.

Every line below is ticked on one of two kinds of evidence: shipped as an opt-in advisory step, with its agreement measured on a labelled set and posted on the issue; or closed or parked with that measurement, or its absence, as the reason. "All shipped" isn't required.

item.title: coordinating-epics: process-log entry — 2026-10-20 private-library
item.body:
A process-log entry for `coordinating-epics`, from a run on a host that consumes this repo as a submodule. The process-log rules send it here as an issue, because writing it in the vendored copy would leave the host with a modified submodule. The host repo is private, so the entry is anonymized as `private-library`.

**Please add** the entry below as `process-log/2026/2026-10-20-private-library.md`, and its row to `process-log/2026/index.md`.

**New candidates for #404:**
- **Finding 4:** the kickoff prompt, or the brief template, should carry the epic's close-at-merge practice.
- **Finding 8:** a `note` on a table row always lands in the last cell. For a Parked row that's "Last re-read", so a note there garbles the date column.

---

## Session 2026-10-20 — private-library

**Way in:** adoption ([creation.md](../../creation.md)). The epic body already existed, written from a sibling repo's design doc. A dated decision comment widened its scope to the shared library's work that downstream services were waiting on. It was adopted with `epic-edit.sh --adopt-live --lint-all`, after a dry run shown to the operator.

**Shape:**
- 12 children planned across four tiers, plus one parked.
- 3 more slotted mid-run: a correctness fix filed from a consumer, and two release vehicles the coordinator filed.
- 3 residuals filed and parked.
- About 20 check-ins over 5 days, three releases (MINOR, PATCH, MINOR), closed on an empty re-scan.
- Two "scope it" requests were handled as a check-in type of their own: read and probe, post a proposal, and mark the line "awaiting the owner".

**What was different:**
- A shared library whose consumers live in five sibling repos. Every release needed a pointer on each waiting issue. The order rule was "unblock a waiting consumer first, then group by release".
- Most children were contract or extractor changes. A wire-visible change that the changelog rule can't see, such as how an envelope key is derived, had to be harvested by hand.

### Findings
1. **When the next child waits on the owner, run the next unblocked one, and re-route its obligations in writing.**
   - A dependency approval held child A, so child B went first.
   - B inherited an obligation the plan had given A: declaring a mirror obligation.
   - One harvest comment on A recorded the reorder and the shifted obligations, and B's brief carried them.
   - Nothing was lost, and A's brief later built on B's merged surface.
2. **The coordinator's claims about consumer code were wrong four times,** each time taken from notes rather than the consumer's `main`:
   - two briefs put a closed `Literal` on a vocabulary the producer owns;
   - one said a consumer's preview caught only `ValueError`, when it also caught the selector error;
   - one framed an uncaught exception as a production crash, when the consumer's child process already caught `BaseException`.

   The implementer's pre-build review corrected each one, and each was recorded on the epic line as a coordinator error. **Candidate rule:** label a claim about consumer behaviour `[traced]` only when it was read on that consumer's `main` in this check-in. Otherwise label it `[stated]`.
3. **Probe a new dependency in the real environment, not only a clean one.** A throwaway-environment probe leaked the workspace venv and showed the library loading an optional regex engine, a C extension. That turned out to be the production fact: an existing dependency always installs the engine, so the library always switches behaviour. The brief then asked for tests that pin it. A truly clean probe would have hidden it.
4. **Put "close at merge" in the brief.** Three implementers in a row wrote "leave open until the release" in their post-merge steps. Each then corrected themselves by citing the previous child. The epic's practice should travel in the kickoff, not be rediscovered each time.
5. **A Waits row is "met" only when its unblock condition is met, not when our side is done.** At close, the coordinator nearly marked rows met whose condition was a consumer deploying the release. They became "our part done; waits on X". The exit criterion allowed that, because the downstream half lives in the sibling repos.
6. **A release vehicle the coordinator files carries the bump as an operator decision, and starting the thread does *not* approve it.** The body gave the rule (breaking means MINOR) and its precedent. The owner chose MINOR twice: once against the rule, to signal a contract set, and once with it.
7. **Pre-flight found two measured hazards no issue mentioned:**
   - a selector error that isn't a `ValueError` escaped the extraction-error path;
   - a canonicalizer shared "as is" would have rejected the floats and nulls real bodies carry.

   Both went into briefs as items with options, and each was settled in its thread.
8. **Scripts.**
   - `scan.sh` caught every downstream move. It also caught the epic's own new issue right after the coordinator filed it, so re-scan after filing, before `{last_seen}` is written.
   - `epic-edit.sh`'s lint refused a short cross-repo ref once.
   - Missed: a `note` on a Parked table row lands in its "Last re-read" cell. It's harmless, but a note target that knows the row's columns would read better.

### Index row
| [2026-10-20](2026-10-20-private-library.md) | private-library | Adopted a widened epic: 12 children plus 3 slotted, 3 releases in 5 days. When a child waits on the owner, the next unblocked one runs, with obligations re-routed in a harvest comment. Consumer claims taken from notes were wrong 4 times: trace them on the consumer's main. Probe new dependencies in the real environment. "Met" means the unblock condition is met, not that our side is done |

item.title: Shared import-closure diff for wheelhouse-pinned libraries (co-core pin moves), lifted from CannObserv/replicator
item.body:
**Proposal:** add a shared script that diffs the **import closure** of a wheelhouse-pinned library between two versions. Every cohort repo that pins `co-core` from the private wheelhouse would vendor it, instead of each repo rebuilding the method by hand at every pin move.

**Filed from:** CannObserv/replicator, where the tool now exists locally (CannObserv/replicator#145, merged `9fcd33b`): [`scripts/co_core_closure_diff.py`](https://github.com/CannObserv/replicator/blob/main/scripts/co_core_closure_diff.py), about 450 lines, standard library only, with 36 tests. It was scoped "local, cohort-ready" on purpose, so lifting it doesn't mean generalizing it first.

## Why
- **A module list misses what actually loads.** In CannObserv/replicator#140 (a 17-minor catch-up), an import of `extract.canonical` from the models module ran the `extract` package's `__init__`. That pulled in a whole subpackage that had changed, and no import line in the consumer names it. Only a walk of the transitive closure found it.
- **The hazard is silent.** The change-bus payloads are `extra="ignore"`, so a moved field fails without an error. The version distance tells you nothing; what matters is which surface moved.
- **It has been rebuilt by hand three times in one repo**: CannObserv/replicator#77 (a `diff -rq` of wheels), #140 and #136 (an AST walk, each written from scratch).
- **Another repo did without it.** CannObserv/broker#104 did its 0.19.6 → newest bump from a CHANGELOG read alone, with no closure walk.

## What the local tool does
`co_core_closure_diff.py OLD NEW [--root …] [--package …] [--wheelhouse …] [--diff]`
- It reads the wheels straight from the wheelhouse, with no install.
- It walks every static import from the consumer's roots: parent-package `__init__`s, `from pkg import submodule` edges, relative imports, and imports under `TYPE_CHECKING`, inside `try` and inside functions. It stops at third-party modules and lists them.
- It reports a verdict per file: `identical`, `docstrings-only` (equal ASTs once docstrings are stripped), `version-only` (only `__version__` changed), `changed`, `added` or `removed`. It also lists the Requires-Dist delta, files that don't parse, unresolved definite imports, and the dynamic-import sites it couldn't follow.
- The output is Markdown that pastes into the pin comment. Exit 0 means a report was written; exit 2 means a usage error, a missing wheel or a corrupt wheel, with advice to re-sync.

## What a cohort version needs (from the implementer's notes)
1. **A distribution → import-name mapping.** Locally, `--package` names both the import package and the wheel, which only holds because co-core's three packages spell them the same (`co_core_aio` ↔ `co-core-aio`). A general tool needs `--package dist=import`, or to read `top_level.txt` / `RECORD`.
2. **Roots per repo.** Replicator's defaults are `src/` and `scripts/`. Siblings differ: some have `app/`, some ship a CLI. The flags exist; the defaults would come from the vendoring repo.
3. **The limits it records**, which a cohort version should keep visible:
   - Dynamic imports aren't followed, only listed. co-core-sync has two lazy `__getattr__` sites, and their targets are reached only because they're also named under `TYPE_CHECKING`.
   - `from pkg import *` doesn't expand `__all__`.
   - Only `.py` files are compared.
   - PEP 420 namespace packages count as resolved.

## Where it could live (the maintainer's call)
- **`init-project-fastapi`**, beside `references/private-wheelhouse.md`, which already owns the wheelhouse and pin pattern. The script would ship in its `scripts/`, and the reference would say "run it on every pin move". This is the suggested home.
- Or a small new skill for pin moves on a private library, if more than the diff is wanted (for example, the pin-comment shape and the "every pin move, not just multi-minor" rule from CannObserv/replicator's DEPLOYMENT.md).

**Out of scope here:** a CI gate on pin moves. A `changed` verdict needs a reader's judgement, so a gate would need a policy first.

item.title: patching-hosts: `database:` exceptions match exactly, so a test suite's per-worker databases need a line each and a new worker is a new finding
item.body:
Found adopting the skill on host 6 (process log `2026-09-28-host-6.md`; a private repo, so no identifiers here), at `468bf14`, on 2026-10-20.

### Command
```
bash skills/patching-hosts/scripts/probe.sh --refresh-into <scratch> --dry-run-into <scratch>
```

### Output
```
{"kind":"knob","id":"database:<app>_test_gw0","exception_what":"database:<app>_test_gw0",
 "message":"The 16/main cluster holds <app>_test_gw0, which no datastore line names, so the recovery point wouldn't cover it. Name it in a datastore postgres line (knob.md)."}
```
There are nine of these: `<app>_test` and `<app>_test_gw0` through `gw7`.
- **What they are:** the test suite's databases, one per pytest-xdist worker, created on demand and rebuilt on every run.
- **Why they're excepted:** there's nothing in them to recover, and dumping them would add about 100 MB to every recovery point.

### Expected
One line for the family:
```
exception database:<app>_test* 2027-04-20 the test suite's databases, rebuilt by every run
```
Today that takes nine lines.

### Why
`exception_for` (probe.sh, about L383) matches `<what>` by string equality: `[ "${_f[0]}" = "$1" ]`. The knob already takes globs for `[host <glob>]`, `hold` and `owner`.

So with exact matching:
- a tenth xdist worker (`-n auto` on a bigger host) creates `<app>_test_gw8`;
- that's a new finding on the next probe;
- the knob has to be edited for a database that holds nothing.

### Scope
- **Shape:** a glob, `*` and `?` as for `[host]`, in `database:` alone. Other kinds name one thing, such as a `held:<package>`, where a glob could over-cover.
- **Precedence:** an exact `<what>` should beat a glob.

item.title: patching-hosts: pending.language skips a root-owned uv.lock, so a root-owned release tree is never audited
item.body:
Found adopting the skill on host 6 (process log `2026-09-28-host-6.md`; a private repo, so no identifiers here), at `468bf14`, on 2026-10-20.

### Command
```
bash skills/patching-hosts/scripts/probe.sh --refresh-into <scratch> --dry-run-into <scratch>
```

### Output (`pending.language.trees[0]`)
```
{"dir":"/srv/<app>/live","lockfile":"uv.lock","units":["<app>.service", …],"owner":"unknown",
 "owner_line":null,"audited":false,"advisories":null,"packages":null,
 "why":"its uv.lock is root's, and uv never runs as root here"}
```
- **The layout:** the service runs from an immutable, root-owned release tree. A deploy script builds `/srv/<app>/releases/<sha12>` as root, and `live` links to the current one.
- **What runs it:** the service user `<app>` (`User=`).
- **Who can read it:** the tree is world-readable.
- **The result:** the class this reading exists for (#366) is reported unaudited on exactly the hosts that hardened their deploys.

### Expected
The audit taken as the **invoking user** (`$SUDO_USER`, or whoever started the probe, the user knob commands already run as), when the lockfile's owner is root and the user can read `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock`.
- It would run in a copy, as `lang_audit` already does.
- It would use the root-owned `/usr/local/bin/uv` or `/usr/bin/uv` first, never `~/.local/bin`, since the invoking user's home is where a writable `uv` would come from.

By hand, as the invoking user, on a copy of the same two files, the audit runs. Counts only:
```
uv audit --frozen   # uv 0.11.3
Found 255 known vulnerabilities and no adverse project statuses in 190 packages
```

### Why
- **The current rule:** `lang_audit` (probe.sh, about L1762) returns at once when `u` is root.
- **What it guards against:** running a `uv` that a non-root user can rewrite, as root.
- **That stays out of reach:** running as the invoking user never needs root, so it doesn't reopen that risk.

**Related, minor:** `"owner":"unknown"`. A release tree is an export, with no `.git` remote to read. The knob has no way to name a tree's owner, short of an `owner` glob over the tree's path, if that's meant to apply.

item.title: AGENTS.md says three knobs share the env → file → default lookup; seven KNOBS.md rows say so, and context-docs-dir is an unlisted eighth
item.body:
Found in #448's close-out (its [report](https://github.com/gregoryfoster/skills/issues/448#issuecomment-6283033094), "For the epic") and re-measured by the epic #451 coordinator. Not part of that epic.

**What:**
- **AGENTS.md undercounts the knobs that share the lookup.** Its "Resolution knobs" section says "**Three** of those resolve through the same three-step lookup — `<NAME>` env var, then the file, then a built-in default" and names `worktree_root`, `plans_dir` and `skills-pin`. [measured 2026-10-20, `docs/KNOBS.md` at d8e9fd4] Seven rows state that shape: those three, plus `context-budget` (`CONTEXT_BUDGET`), `context-doc-budget` (`CONTEXT_DOC_BUDGET`), `context-proximity-pct` (`CONTEXT_PROXIMITY_PCT`), and `typesafe` (`TYPESAFE_OPT_IN`, added by #448).
- **An eighth knob has the shape, but its KNOBS row doesn't say so.** `context-docs-dir`'s row reads "replaces the default", yet `prove-no-loss.sh --help` documents "Default: CONTEXT_DOCS_DIR, then .skills/context-docs-dir, then docs" [traced].

**Why it matters:** the sentence already says it isn't the inventory ("That is the shared *shape*, not the inventory"). But a reader who counts "three" learns that the budget knobs and the TypeSafe opt-in have no env override, and the `context-docs-dir` row hides an override the scripts honour. #261 was this failure: a repo couldn't discover a knob's companion.

**Suggested fix:** drop the count from AGENTS.md, so the sentence names the shape and points to KNOBS.md for which knobs have it. Don't restate a number that rots (cf. `check-counts.sh`'s form 2). Correct the `context-docs-dir` row's "Replaces or extends" cell to name `CONTEXT_DOCS_DIR`. AGENTS.md had 7 tokens of headroom at #448's measurement (5,993 / 6,000), so the edit must be net-zero or a reduction. Removing the count is.
